Hi Guys, Have been following this thread off and on for a while now and have decided to do some more in depth analysis to see how price reacts to pivot levels. I've computed pivot levels for the past 52 weeks of EURUSD and plotted how far price has traveled each week in relation to pivots. Below is the result. Attached Image (click to enlarge) A couple of observations: Price has passed R2 and S2 (0.62 pivot) 41 times in the past 51 weeks. I've then computed the probabilities of what happens after it has passed this point giving the following table. Attached Image What this shows is that of the 41 times price has passed R2/S2, 12 of these weeks price never crossed S/R 3 (29% of the 41 weeks); 11 times never crossed S/R 4 after crossing S/R 3 (27%) and 10 times never crossed S/R 5 after crossing S/R 4 (24%). This support Davits view of price retracing from these points 0.61 - 1.00 pivots. Some more stats... When price is in S/R2+ zones there is a 44% chance that price will cross 1.00 pivot and a 20% chance that price will cross 1.38 pivot. This sort of states the obvious that the higher the price travels from the pivots, the more likely it is to retrace. In future I'll be comparing various pairs to see which react to pivots better/more predictably, pivot timeframes and other things as ideas come to me. If you have any ideas on analysis, let me know and i'll share my info/results with you all. Cheers, David Edit: These stats are based on EURUSD 1 year data with pivots calculated weekly so may not be accurate for other pairs and pivot timeframes.

Hi guys, Another update. I've computed 5 years worth of pivots for EURGBP and have counted the number of times pivots and S/R have been hit. Output is below: Attached Image (click to enlarge) So how to interpret this... Weeks hit S/R is straight forward. The amount of weeks in that year that any S or R was hit. Below that is the probability of S/R being hit given that the previous S or R was hit. So for example, 5th year R5 is 33% because the previous R4 was hit 3 times and only one time did the price hit R5 so 1/3 = 33%. At the bottom is the sum of all the years and a sum weighted probability which accounts for the frequency that a pivot is hit as the further out you go, the less instances you get of S/R being hit. There are various ways of interpreting this information and it would be good to look at this while looking at a 5 year chart to see what the pivots do when 1 year price action is only in 1 direction etc. A couple of observations: If we look at the sum weighted probability on the resistance side, if R1 is hit, it is more likely that R2 will be hit. If R2 is hit, then R3 is just around the corner with a chance of 75%. Notice this on the support side aswell. This is because the distance from 0.62 to 0.786 is generally small and price can travel fairly quickly through this area. If price hits R3 then there is still a high chance of R4 being hit(70%). After that there is a sudden drop to R4. This means that it's fairly safe to start opening shorts between 1.00 and 1.38 with a stop above the 1.38 pivot. If R5 is hit, then it is highly likely that R6 and R7 will then be hit. What I find interesting is that the pivots are fairly consistent throughout the 5 years with the upside running far above R6 and R7 when price hits R5 whereas on the downside, S6 and S7 are less predictable and by my interpretation doesn't seem to run as far. The drop at R5 is fairly consistent too. The support side doesn't look too interesting for this pair but the same story goes. After price hits S3, it is still more likely than not that S4 will be hit but probability of this occurring reduces. If the price is between S1 and PP, then there is a 68% chance that S1 will be hit. This info can be used to trade with the pivots. e.g. if R1 is hit, then it would be more likely that R2 will be hit, then R3 followed by R4. So the plan could be to wait till R1 is hit, if it retraces a bit, enter a long position below R1 and have a stop below pivot(note, these probabilities don't mean that if price is at R1 that it is unlikely that the price will fall below pivot. It just means that in a given week, if R1 is ever hit, R2 has a 66% chance of being hit. In between, price may hit S3 and then come back to hit R2). We can then exit our long position as PA loses steam and starts stalling preferably at R4. Then shorts can be open. I'll stop here as I've been rambling on for a while now. --- 帖子 #19560 ---
I was testing ADR_v2 and I'm not sure but ADR % dont fits with any value showed by indicator. An example: GBPCHF shows now -&gt; ADR 90.5 | T 92 | 1D 59 | 5D 92 | 10D 107 | 20D 96 Any value is 90.5%. I tried all combinations In bold only 2 possible values can be "90.5%" of today

--- 帖子 #19561 ---
To simplify the concept, the ADR % at T period is the "rounded" result from this calculation: T ADR / (10D ADR + 20D ADR)/2 * 100. I wrote "rounded" because decimal part of the specific ADR value is truncated and only the integer part of number is displayed at screen. Hope it helps.

hi June1989, just a piece of advice. Always trade and create demo accounts with the size you would actually trade. If your live account is 2000 USD then open a demo account that is of that size. This way your psychology gets on the right path. Your mind now thinks "hey I can trade so high no problem to do it live" and thats where the killer punch to you and your account comes. Your mind with these percentage gains that you have done will now not be happy when in a real account you will only make 1/10 of your percent forcing you to overtrade again.Get yourself another demo for a month with an account size that matches your live account and trade as it would be your live account. Do not go live until you feel content with far smaller gains/ Just my opinion Cheers Jester

Just a heads up for this week. 1. There will be ample opportunities due to high volatile news events on major pairs this week. If the market is quite now don't push the trades, let the trade come to you. 2. You don't have to be in a lot of trades at one time to make a good return on your account if you have a small account size. One good trade with controlled positions can bring you a good percentage increase on your account. 3. If you see an opportunity and scared of news start with a small position size and once news comes in your favor you add more to your trade. Remember don't exhaust all your position size because you feel like you know which way the trade will go for sure. Remember, you don't know what the market will do next (MD) thus the reason we trade in small positions here at Pivot trading. 4. You don't trade the ideas of others on the forums . You trade your own plan, if you don't have one, make one its still Monday and trade accordingly. 5. Last but not the least, stay focused away from negative vibes and you will win at the end. Best regards

GBP Nice article about GBP from ING. https://think.ing.com/articles/gbp-t...rexit-trinity/ Short-term Brexit uncertainties keeping GBP sidelined for now We estimate that GBP/USD is trading with a 2.5-3.0% discount at present – which is indicative of a 'muddling through' Brexit risk premium. This is unsurprising given the near-term focus on the Commons Withdrawal Bill vote (tomorrow) and the 28-29 June EU leaders’ summit. We would expect this uncertainty premium to remain in the price of GBP until further clarity on the Brexit front. However, GBP's currently depressed value suggests that a lot of 'bad' Brexit news is already in the price. For a more sustained downturn, we'd need to see the probability of a 'hard' Brexit pick-up substantially. This week's events in the House of Commons are unlikely to shift one's assessment materially (in either direction). Summary of the article, Bottom line: A lot of bad news priced in... but hard to find a positive Brexit catalyst While a tricky summer of Brexit politics lies ahead, with May facing an impossible Brexit trinity, the pound still remains a good long-term value play. Our current forecasts continue to look for sterling to navigate towards levels consistent with a ‘neutral’ Brexit later this year ( GBP/USD: 1.43 and EUR/GBP: 0.86 )* – with the near-term balance of risks tilted towards GBP/USD moving back towards 1.36 (200-day moving average). *These remain under review – and we will address GBP's longer-term direction in a note later this summer.

regarding pivots levels - what did the job for me, because none of the options worked for me, generally speaking. Had problems mainly with AUD and JPY pairs, even if most of the other pairs were correct. Even had 25-35 pips difference for some (using Oanda Europe). I took each pair and played with - and +, or simply set broker candle to true, so the pivots were aligned with the pivots from the site previously mentionet by Davit. https://www.actionforex.com/markets/...-pivot-points/ Then saved the template for that pair. I usually have opened in tabs each pair that I follow, but won`t be much of a trouble to load the template for that pair. So it`s pretty easy: align all pairs you trade -&gt; save template for each chart -&gt; load template every time you need that pair.

--- 帖子 #20271 ---
Hi Guys About drawdowns This subject is often misunderstood and twisted into gross forum debates and traders who have history of blown accounts.Very few understand nature of DD DD is essential part of any successful trading system if anyone tells you otherwise they are lying and deceiving you.There is no such thing as zero DD system that is successful long term.This comes down to stop losses.Are you going to take a loss every time price goes against you 20-30pips?If yes you will deplete your account before you know it. Trades need room to develop!! If executed properly based on the Edge of the system then allow the edge to develop.Running 5% 10% even 15% is acceptable if you are growing your account same time. This is true of most successful systems. If you are running 10% DD but gaining your account same time by end of the year you will be still in great profit.This is the truth in trading The dream of novice market speculators is that they will continually bask in the warmth of profitable times. This myth is falsely promised by the promoters of trading systems and trading training programs. In fact, just the opposite is true. Most long-term profitable traders spend the vast majority of their trading careers either in Trading Drawdowns or recovering from a drawdown. Any slick promoter who tells you different is not dealing from a full deck. Most successful long-term traders are underwater the majority of time. Welcome to trading! I have and had DD most of the times.In fact it does not bother me at all because I trust my EDGE to generate more then my DD in consistent bases. That's it

Hi Mmarron, there's no predefined TP here. You start to build a position entering around key-levels (Weekly Fib Pivots) and then monitor the evolution of your trades. A good rule of thumb is to look at the next level in the direction of the trade: if it breaks that level then hold on, otherwise evaluate the situation, look at PA, TDI and Angulator and close all/part of your position. Hope this helps. Best regards, Bubincka

I fluctuate 2% to 15% average around 5-7%when holding a position for 2-3weeks.In fact this is normal meaning any system must accommodate DD unless you are day trading or scalping. Positions/Swing/Trend trading requires extra time hence why DD. DD is not to be confused with trades that are clearly wrong.DD are trades that have high probability to become winners but If I think Edge is no longer there and my SL requirement has been fulfilled I will take the loss .By no means I advocate holding a losing trades until your account goes bust.Like I said DD are positions that are high degree profit potential. cheers

I always look at my overall DD.When I think its not looking good I don't add new positions at all .I have never looked single pair DD because to me that's pointless.Its always been overall DD of the account. Each pair is unique and has its mini fundamentals chart location and should be managed singularly but DD should be looked at overall. When you must cut losses you should take the loss on a pair which has the least potential to be be profitable not necessarily biggest DD. I had DD on EU but end up being green by Friday close. I have small DD on AN but don't think its cause to worry. I have DD on AU but think its at great support level. Do you follow me? If you must take a loss take the pairs that stinks the most and that maybe not the biggest DD pair. Big DD could be result of greed because you entered bigger positions but on chart and fundamentals still could be great to become profitable hence why I said biggest DD does not automatically mean weakest position to take a loss.

Hallo Davit, traders thanks for thread for ideas! A couple of years ago I read Kostolany Andre 'Und was macht der Dollar?' ('And what does the dollar do') there was a topic about the gold standard and that, in the opinion of the author, there is no longer any need for it. He then explains that each currency, and so there is some value that determines its course, and conducts a short analysis: USD: political stability, absolute respect for private property, high technologies, raw materials, dynamics of entrepreneurs. D-Mark (euro): political stability (it was), diligence, propensity for economy and discipline of the German people. GBP: remnants of the former empire, world trade, City of London, an important banking and insurance center, shipping and a bonus to the North Sea oil. CHF: centuries of neutrality, legally protected bank secrecy (no longer). French franc: French style of life and taste, as well as the resourcefulness of the French - they do not have oil but have ideas. JPY: developed industry, the modesty of the Japanese worker. In short, these are all those qualities, virtues and circumstances that determine the rank of the currencies. If the virtues claim that the currency is worth more, they lose their importance and lose their meaning. I like you think fundamentals are very important, but this book was written 30 years ago. Can anyone either advise resources or books where a similar analysis of currencies, not just bare numbers in the form of GDP, PPI etc. Many thanks in advance and excuse my English

Trade Worksheets - Introductory &amp; Intermediate As a "retired" Fund trader responsible also for systems research and having traders reporting it was necessary for documentation to offer advice and assess trades by all traders. A "worksheet" was a simple method of hard copy also serving as a log and reasons for each trade. One key is to take a screen image immediately before or after entering a trade then follow-up screen images during the course of a trade as well at trade exit. These would be analyzed by traders in a seminar format on a weekly basis. I still marvel at traders who grew into very professional traders and attributed their improvement/success to a worksheet format with follow-up. I have consulted with Davit who was happy for these to be uploaded as two PDF files that may serve to assist as introductory and intermediate worksheets to those getting to grips with Davit's system. A brilliant system. These worksheets may be printed in color or black and white. I simply use a erasable pencil to check off the criteria. Yes, I still use them. They have been updated over the last 18-24 months to their present form. All professional traders I have been associated with have a method of self-discipline, a check list of criteria before entering any trade. A trade log is also carefully maintained. Davit may have comments or advice to improve or update these as required. Above all look at them and ask yourself if relatively new to Davit's system, am I disciplined and do I have confidence in entering a trade. These worksheets may help?

Since market does whatever, there have been times at the begining of the week pivots change and trade goes as planned. But also they just don't, so I stick to this method: As price travels progressively away from weekly pivot it becomes more likely to go into correction. 61 S/R key zone 78R/S is Scott Carney's last chance for reversal (spikes stops taken before reversal) 100R/S another major zone. Page 1 For me Sunday's are trap days, so even if at a key zone I allow the market to move and see if it "progressively moves further away from Pivot" then look for high probability setup. Looking at weeks Fundamentals also helps in deciding. I rather miss a trade than be in a bad trade. Also, when I miss a TP and market gives me a second chance at same location...I take it! Regardless of what it will do afterwards. It's called Second Chance not second guess. Hope this helps...btw not my image...sorry do not remember from who...but they get the credit

--- 帖子 #20726 ---
Hi fellow traders, on post 19617 I showed some screenshots with attached a trade manager that I've modified to suit Davit's strategy. Since some traders PM me looking for this EA, I asked Davit the permit to post it and here it is. Basically it let you set a unique TP equal for all the trades in your position or alternatively you can choose a different TP for each trade. These settings must be performed when you attach the EA to a chart. In case you choose a different TP for each single trade (allOrdersSameTP=false), it can be either a fixed numer of pips or a % of ATR calculated on a selectable timeframe. Then of course there's an equity SL you can set to an X% of your balance. Plus some buttons to enter/exit trades either in fixed lots or with a risk adjusted position sizing. As an example here I have set a unique TP for all the trades (allOrdersSameTP=true, unique_TP=1.5736). Last but not least, please consider that I am still learning Davit's strategy in demos, therefore you also do your demo tests before using it on a live account. Best regards, Bubincka

Key Quotes “In a worst-case scenario, the two countries could end up imposing additional tariffs averaging around 10% on all imported goods from the other country. Hi J1mm Please see highlighted excerpt of page 1 again; ' 'As price travels progressively away from weekly pivot it becomes more likely to go into correction. 61 S/R key zone 78R/S is Scott Carney's last chance for reversal (spikes stops taken before reversal) 100R/S another major zone. Should price smash 100 S/R then you are in strong trend supported by fundamentals.'' If you are in a trade and price smashes 100R/S, what you should do is see if the smashing is supported by fundamentals before closing your trades blindly, some times, MM fades this levels to take out the weak hands. If you feel based on your analysis that nothing major has shifted fundamentally, then you should be ready to see it out, that is why you have DD sometimes. If you cant withstand DD then the method/trading is not for you. The edge is in the system, but you have to work out the edge by trading it to generate pips for you. I hope this clarifies some of your concerns. Green pips

US Dollar Index inches higher toward the critical 95 mark. Trade deficit shrinks more than expected in the U.S. Earlier today, the AUD/USD pair rose above the 0.74 mark before losing its traction and coming under a heavy selling pressure in the second half of the day. As of writing, the pair was trading at 0.7352, losing 0.55% on the day. A stronger greenback is the primary driver of the pair's price action on Wednesday. The US Dollar Index, which briefly dipped below the 94 mark earlier this week, rose sharply today on the back of upbeat data from the United States and easing concerns over the trade conflict between the United States and the rest of the world further escalating. The data released by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis showed that the international trade deficit decreased to $64.8 billion in May to better the experts' estimate of $68.9 billion. Moreover, durable goods orders contracted by less than expected. Earlier today, senior administration officials claimed that President Trump wouldn't invoke a national emergency law on China. However, White House economic advisor Larry Kudlow later said that Trump was not planning to retreat on China and forced major equity indexes to retrace their early gains. Nonetheless, the US Dollar Index hasn't shown a negative reaction and is now within a touching distance of the 95 mark, up 0.6% on the day.

Money and Risk Management for Stacking positions on 5 pairs: from Davit's post#1 STOP LOSS 1 Decide how much each swing is worth example $500 2. Divide $500 into mini lots for multiple entries example .50c a pip gives 1000 pip distance 3. This allows averaging in orders as seen fit irregardless if previous orders are in red 4. Orders are placed as long as reason for trade is still valid 5. If conditions change loss is taken since orders are not placed all at once this allows smaller loss Swings Each Swing investment $500 (example yours could be anything) Swing is taken as loss once -$500 is reached There are no exceptions.No running red beyond $500 Orders broken down into mini lots that satisfies each swing consist of 10-15 trades My budget for this is 2-3% of account risk say $500 for example.I then enter trades on mini lots and as long as my 500 is not consumed on DD and I am still confident of my trade I stay on it.I may choose to get out early but most times my SL is predetermined.This allows me to cast a wider net. So my 10mini lots can cover 50pip distance hence capture better RR There is advantage to trade this way.Should PA go against you and you no longer like the trade you can get out by fraction of lot invested hence your loss is minimal instead of traditional 1 trade 1lot per trade when if wrong loss is substantially higher. Numbers posted are for examples only I attached the excel sheet of mine that helps me to stack on 5 pairs.

--- 帖子 #20876 ---
Hi Jester_73, below a short description of each parameter, as said many are self explanatory: input bool buttons = true; // Use Buttons to enter / exit trades. input bool checkMaxEquityLoss = true; // check if value in "_X_PercentLoss" is reached up, if reached close all at this loss level. input bool flagFixedLots = true; // use fixed lots according to value contained in setting "fixedLots". input bool flagAtrTp = false; // if set to true use an ATR based TP, used with parameters "atrTpFactor", "tf", "atrPeriod". input bool allOrdersSameTP = true; // same TP level for all trades. input double risk_MM = 1.0; // if fixedLots are not used, position size is calculated with the following formula: Inserted Code numLots = NormalizeDouble(((AccountBalance() * risk_MM) / 100) / tsl_MM / MarketInfo(Symbol(), MODE_TICKVALUE), 2); input double _X_PercentLoss = -5.0; // see parameter "checkMaxEquityLoss". input double fixedLots = 0.01; // self explanatory. input double atrTpFactor = 1.0; // see parameter "flagAtrTp". input double unique_TP = 0.0; // set TP level for all trades, used when parameter "allOrdersSameTP = true". input int ftp = 10000; // Fake Take Profit. input int fsl = 10000; // Fake Stop Loss. input int ttp = 250; // True Take Profit expressed in pips (points) used when "flagAtrTp = false" and "allOrdersSameTP = false". input int tsl_MM = 150; // Stop Loss used in MM formula, see parameter "risk_MM". input int xoff = 980; // Buttons X Offset. input int yoff = 120; // Buttons Y Offset. input int tf = PERIOD_M15; // see parameter "flagAtrTp". input int atrPeriod = 960; // see parameter "flagAtrTp". input color colorLineTP = clrBlue; // TP line color, I use Blue for longs, Red for shorts. Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #20932 ---
If you are new to Pivot trading I would like to share below what your thinking must be going forward from here. 1. This system is based on Probabilities which lies between S61-S100 (For buying) and R61-R100 (For Selling), See below. Attached Image (click to enlarge) 2. This system is based on starting with small positions which build into a larger position as the trade progresses. Don't get tempted with large pips numbers on the charts. Our trades must have a concrete foundation for entry and for exits (Which could be PA consolidating, Next Pivot zone, ADR etc.), See below Attached Image (click to enlarge) In above chart, ADR reached for the day and I have to leave for work now. Better close it and flat for the month. 3. Look at how much you are risking as opposed to how much you can make . This sound cliche but the more you will think about how much you want to risk on a trade the better money management you will have. There will be times when you won't exhaust all your positions on one trade and that is Ok. It's not about using all your lot size positions in one trade but to manage a trade in a manner which results in less risk, See below. Attached Image (click to enlarge) In above screenshot, I made AUD 77 in AUDUSD buying trade in 12 hours while I was asleep half of the time only using 10 positions of 0.02 cents which comes to $2. The max I try to go is $5 with my account but I saved $3 on this AUDUSD trade and still made AUD 77 not bad. Hope this helps. Best Regards

Calandar Tone of my canvas.Going into slow holiday summer days and range is pretty common and focus should be back exploiting this.USD may continue to decline continuing its corrections.Heavy news on GBP CAD USD and AUD.AUD may sharply decline specially against NZD after Tues. Monday GBP Manufacturing PMI could surprise everyone printing better then forecast if so GBP trajectory of going higher will find new wind. USD-ISM Manufacturing PMI 58.2 58.7 forecast is red but could print worse since all that tariff issues may have had some effect. What is ISM? A country’s economy is as strong as its supply chain. The Institute for Supply Management (ISM) measures the economic activity from both the manufacturing side as well as the service side. Formed in 1915, ISM is the first management institute in the world with over 40,000 members in 90 countries. Since it can draw from information gathered from the surveying its large membership of purchasing managers, the ISM economic news releases are carefully watched by Forex traders around the world as a reliable guide to economic activity. ISM publishes three surveys; manufacturing, construction, and services. Published on the first business day of the month, the ISM Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) is compiled from surveys of 400 manufacturing purchasing managers. These purchasing managers from different sectors represent five different fields; inventories and employment, speed of supplier deliveries, production level, and new orders from customers. In addition, ISM construction PMI is released on the second business day of the month, followed by services on the third business day. Forex traders will look to these releases to determine the risks at any given time in the market. Forex Market Impact The Manufacturing and Non-manufacturing PMI’s are big market movers. When these reports come out at 10:30 AM ET, currencies can become very volatile. Since these economic releases are based on the previous month’s historical data gathered directly from industry professionals, Forex traders can determine if the US economy is expanding or contracting. Forex traders will compare the previous month’s number with the forecasted number that economists have published. If the released PMI number is better than the previous number and higher than the forecasted number, the US dollar tends to rally. This is where fundamental and technical analysis comes together to create a trade setup. Manufacturing sector is roughly 12% of U.S. overall economic growth. Tues RBA rate expectation is same and I think AN could finally go into correction after Tues!I still have my shorts here.Nice level. Hi fellow traders, as my experience with Davit's Fib Pivot increases, I have decided to add some features to the trade manager published earlier here. Last week I wrote post 20931 because I was in deep DD on AN and very close to hit my equity SL. Since I still believed in this trade and probabilities of a reversal were increasing, I asked Davit if it could be a good idea to close only a fraction of my position, taking a partial loss instead of a full one. Davit answered on post 20934 , saying that this could be a possible way to manage the existing position while waiting for a probable correction. Even before my question, Davit on post 20918 remarked this concept : " ....usually happens after you throw the towel take the loss then price reverses and why I insist incremental losses taken never at once unless you must. " So, following this idea, I have added a couple of parameters to the trade manager to have the chance to take only a partial loss instead of been stopped out at a 100% loss, if you are convinced that reasons to stay in the trade are still valid. Please bear in mind that if PA doesn't turn in your favor the final total loss could be bigger than the one you set in the beginning. One way to avoid this could be to lower the _X_PercentLoss parameter value once you're out of DD, to reduce your SL equity amount accordingly. New parameters: input bool flagComment = true; // display on upper left corner Profit%, Profit$, Trades#, Lots#, PpP (experimental, rough amount of pips/trade to hit SL) input bool flagPartialClosing = true; // set ot tp true if you want to close only a few position once your equity SL has been reached input int fractionToBeClosed = 3; // represents the fraction of your total lot number to close, e.g. suppose your position has 0.03 lots, 1/3rd will be closed You can activate this feature while trades are running. It's important to know that will be closed the trade (or part of the trade) with the largest DD. As written in previous post the EA is provides "as is", there could be errors so if you want to use it do it at your own risk. Best regards, Bubincka

I have some other Pivot indicators that I utilize in the trading process I keep them on seperate templates to review charts, they come in handy. One is missed pivots. I like to look go through the charts and see if any pair has some missed pivots. Most importantly Weekly or Monthly ones. I learned a system years ago using divergence on a 4hr chart and missed pivots. It can yield good results. I like to know if there are any, and where they are especially in relationship to the levels in the Davit Pivot system. In the case of this pair EA there is a missed Weekly Pivot just above S61 @ 1.5655 and a Missed Monthly Pivot a line width above S78 @ 1.5622 I also like to keep in mind how the Traders mind thinks in Numbers. For example on this pair because the North American mind has been taught to divide the dollar into quarters I would be happy with the target of just above S61 @ 1.5655 because a lot of people would have the number in their head of 1.5650 as a potential target for price. as for the second missed pivot Monthly Pivot @ 1.5622 just above S78 I personally would target a price @ 1.5630 which would be just above 1.5625. I'm not greedy I don't need the whole pie, just consistent slices of it.

--- 帖子 #21465 ---
zzz18 I understand that the question was directed to Davit but if I may, I'll try to add few things on top of what Davit mentioned that one's mindset must switch from making profits on smaller accounts to learn the system. 1. The people with large trading accounts have the strategies that they trade because without a tested strategy they will blow up their accounts. 2. The people who have small accounts and no trading system neither appreciate the money nor do they appreciate the importance of learning and sticking to one system. 3. The people who have small accounts and a trading system are less worried about profit making but more determined about the repetition of the trades based on the trading system rules so that they can have data from enough sample size of trades to see if the system is working for them or not. My humble suggestion to you would be 1. To take trades based on the system rules mentioned on the first page. 2. Have small goals of trades(100, 200, 300 etc.) not the monetary goals. The money will come eventually but the most important task at this stage is to learn the system. 3. Take a screenshot of the before and after the trade. Put the reasons on the screenshot why you take the trade and why you exit the trade. 4. Before you even know you will have 100's of screenshots of trades which you can refer to later. Believe me, after 500 trades you won't make the same mistake you made in your first trade. 5. Use the template listed on the first page. I know people get tempted to add new indicators that they saw on someone else's chart, stay away from the temptation. Kindest regards

--- 帖子 #21655 ---
1) As price travels progressively away from weekly pivot it becomes more likely to go into correction. 2) 61 S/R key zone 78R/S is Scott Carney's last chance for reversal (spikes stops taken before reversal) 3) 100R/S another major zone. Should price smash 100 S/R then you are in strong trend supported by fundamentals. don't subscribe to typical bookish mentally that if previous H4 is bear then assumption should be another bear candle.This is very wrong way to look at the markets.Markets are in constant motion and within 1 H4 candle price can move opposite over 100pips against previous candle so its not about previous candles but where price is in relative to pivots.In simple terms Location is what is important. I trade 15-30min charts however bigger works as well. TDI is our friend.When price hit major pivots we wait for TDI to turn thus confirm the move. Sharp angles important when its almost horizontal PA is weak or consolidating thus avoid trading.PA is king always! STOP LOSS 1 Decide how much each swing is worth example $500 2. Divide $500 into mini lots for multiple entries example .50c a pip gives 1000 pip distance 3. This allows averaging in orders as seen fit irregardless if previous orders are in red 4. Orders are placed as long as reason for trade is still valid 5. If conditions change loss is taken since orders are not placed all at once this allows smaller loss Swings Each Swing investment $500 (example yours could be anything) Swing is taken as loss once -$500 is reached There are no exceptions.No running red beyond $500 Orders broken down into mini lots that satisfies each swing consist of 10-15 trades My budget for this is 2-3% of account risk say $500 for example.I then enter trades on mini lots and as long as my 500 is not consumed on DD and I am still confident of my trade I stay on it.I may choose to get out early but most times my SL is predetermined.This allows me to cast a wider net. So my 10mini lots can cover 50pip distance hence capture better RR There is advantage to trade this way.Should PA go against you and you no longer like the trade you can get out by fraction of lot invested hence your loss is minimal instead of traditional 1 trade 1lot per trade when if wrong loss is substantially higher. Numbers posted are for examples only Note very important this system does not work best with hyper pairs that usually have over 120pip ADR like GJ GA GN etc From numerous trial and errors low ADR pairs fits the best in my method Pairs I trade most often......UC AC NC EA AU GU NU AN EU

Mozart on how to unlock your inner creative genius The Myth Of ‘The Creative Genius’ There is a destructive myth that the ‘creative genius’ is born with an innate, godlike ability to create extraordinary work at the snap of their finger. This couldn’t be further from the truth. In a study into elite performance, researchers asked expert violinists from the Music Academy in West Berlin to keep detailed recordings of their daily practice regime for a week. (2) At the end of the week, they analyzed the results — comparing the different forms of deliberate practice between the elite violinists and the less accomplished performers. What they discovered was astonishing. On average, the violinists spent the same amount of time on music related activities—But, the elite performing violinist spent more than twice the time (25 hours) on deliberate practice than the other violinists (10 hours). To further reaffirm their findings, the researchers conducted additional research into the violinists’ practice habits. This time, they estimated how many hours of deliberate practice each violinist had accumulated over their lifetime. Once again the results were staggering. “ … the most elite violinists accumulated about the same number of hours of deliberate practice (about 7,410 hours) by the age of 18 as professional middle-aged violinists belonging to international-level orchestras (about 7,336 hours)! By the age of 20, the most accomplished musicians estimated they spent over 10,000 hours in deliberate practice, which is 2,500 and 5,000 hours more than two less accomplished groups of expert musicians or 8,000 hours more than amateur pianists of the same age.” (3) The best violinists had exceeded the 10,000 hours of deliberate practice required to become world-class in any field. This has been well noted by Malcolm Gladwell’s work in his book Outliers (audiobook). 10,000 hours isn’t necessarily the exact threshold —but it does highlight a very important factor in creating genius level work — g reat work requires a great amount of hours in deliberate practice on your craft.

--- 帖子 #21877 ---
The VIX Pairing the U.S. dollar index and the VIX together is powerful because the VIX measures the level of volatility in the market—specifically implied volatility in SPX options. It is sometimes called the “Fear Index” because it tends to spike up when fear and uncertainty abound. Now, if the VIX is showing a high level of volatility and fear, which direction do you think the U.S dollar index will go? Of course, it will most likely be headed up . Conversely, if the VIX is relatively low, showing strong confidence in the market, then the U.S. dollar index will most likely be falling . Attached Image (click to enlarge)

I suggest to go over your trades both good and bad right down notes what you should work on to improve. Do your calendar events and you will notice study improvements of your trading This is how you get better incremental improvements. Very similar to Chess if you just play without any study then you will stay certain rating for years and years and never improve however if you systematically study openings,defense,offense,combinations,tactics you will improve dramatically.Brain has a capacity to observe new information but you must provide that stimuli Losers generally lose because they are doing same things over and over and seldom consider it maybe the way they are trading.You must improve aspects that are winning and repeat it over and over until it becomes muscle memory. cheers

Consumer prices account for a majority of overall inflation. Inflation is important to currency valuation because rising prices lead the central bank to raise interest rates out of respect for their inflation containment mandate. Although this data is extremely late relative to inflation data from other countries, it's the primary gauge of consumer prices and tends to create hefty market impacts. Thank you Riese. If you have a small account like me you feel the urge to risk more than you actually can allow, you're basically chasing money. To lose 2 grand is not the same if you lose 200 grand. This time with this account I pressed this urge down and tried to not make money but gain certain percentage constantly every month, trading like I have a huge account. My goal is 0,5% a day or 10% a month but to be honest everything over zero is success. If I had 200K account I would be happy with even 5% or less, picking trades more conservatively. Secondly, you are right, I'm holding trades longer and let them work out. This needs a lot of trust into system. Hard to do if you're chasing money, your eyes are glowing when already in positive 5€. So I'm not doing that anymore. But basically having more positions in one trade allows you to profit at pre deteremined levels and let other positions run till market takes you out. Mostly I'm doing this with pairs which have positive swap. What I love about Davit's teachings is that he has many times pointed out the psychological aspects of trading, therefore are the books in the clipboard and videos of MD. I've actually read every one of them and watched the videos. I'm not saying that these are the books you should read but at least it's a start, I've read many other books as well. I believe that a trader needs a special mindset and this is what these books help you achieve. This system is one package with these books for a correct mindset, levels (fib pivot) to watch, risk and money management rules (you can set them according to your account and risk tolerance). Also I'm planning my trades ahead, doing the calendar, checking the levels where I would enter a trade and waiting till price gets there. Doing all that looks more professional. I mean not just doing the calendar but investing time into planning. This is my conservative style for capital preservance and minimizing DD. Future plans are achieveing 4K which is doubled money . I know it's not much but if you look at the gain percentage and DD percentage then it's more than satisfying. After that I will probably add more money into account and trying to double that in one year

--- 帖子 #22465 ---
Its always obvious that people who complain about DD dont know much about trading and have almost zero experience. Few months ago(with my personal style of swing trading) I held a total drawdown of 1400 pips accross 4 Positions(unexpected news while at work etc) and it didnt even make me sweat. Why? Because my RM was correct, I still had a healthy margin to keep on trading and knew the price was in a big range with having a clear exit strategy if it falls out that range. Most of the time when people cry about DD they just use too big lot sizes, they sacrifice safety for profits and use tight stop losses in order to use bigger lots. When they see then a DD of 50 pips they cant stand the pressure, close the trade and think the drawdown was the problem, while in fact it was their RM. At the end of the day I was back in profits after several weeks on all 4 positions(+ positive swap). Obviously its not the goal to have big drawdown but it happens. If you think you can always take the perfect entry in a +5 Trillion Dollar Market, you're pretty naive. Trading is a short term investment and if you want to earn money you have to invest it. Just imagine you are a Supercar Dealer and suddenly a rich Arab guy comes in and orders 20 cars which you dont have in stock. If you complain then that you first have to buy 20 cars in order to sell them with profit, then you re the same like the guy who is complaining about drawdown. Meanwhile still studying Pivots and almost done reading every page. I hope to contribute soon. Cheers.

I wanted to add to Davit's advice about an orderly exit. If you see that your absolute dollar stop will be hit within a two day ATR of your pair, consider reducing size until you get that up to a three day ATR. This is my suggestion only. This way, if you find yourself in a fundamental trend you can plan your exits. You can also begin to trade in the direction of the trend and begin to capitalize on that move. I will leave you to find out what pivot level Davit decides he is in a strong fundamental trend. It is in the thread. Hope this helps a little bit. There is no reason to panic and dump trades you had to work to get.

In short keep your head high and thrust forward few bumps should not derail your goals.Its a marathon and not a sprint.There will be mistakes made and they are natural since we are dealing with lots of unknowns however when made don't beat yourself forgive yourself learn from it and move on. The Secrets To: Emotion Free Trading “How To Consistently Act In Your Own Best Interest With Your Off-The-Floor Trading!” Written By Larry Levin "One of the biggest reasons people get into losing streaks while trading is because they confuse their losing trades with themselves. In other words, we conclude that because we had a losing trade or a series of losing trades, we are a losing trader. But the important thing to remember here is we are not our losing trades. Losing trades are part of trading . There isn’t a single trader in the world who doesn’t have losing trades. The only way to avoid them is not to trade in the first place. You cannot be a successful trader until you take mistakes and losing trades for what they really are. They are simply by-products in the trading game and need to be used to gain learning and understanding. But in no way do they define us as a person. But that is where the big problem comes in. Many people let their losing trades and mistakes define them . If they’re having trouble and have had a series of losing trades, they start to think of themselves as a loser. They continually think of themselves in that way. As we know from before, this kind of thinking will just bring on more of the same. Forgiving yourself completely is the only way to avoid this trouble. You are not your mistakes and losing trades. You must put the past behind you and go forward. Holding a grudge against yourself only hurts yourself. Forgive yourself, it’s the only way to be successful.

--- 帖子 #22755 ---
I still like EG short built a heavy positions on it.Yes I aware of issues with GBP but I feel comfortable on this trade. Google Scott Carney 786 fib you'll get interesting results. 78Fib is not even on Fib Meta tool default setting and many traders are unaware of its significance.I added the 78 to my fib default tool "0.786 Retracement The 0.786 retracement is the square root of the 0.618. The 0.786 retracement is the next critical area to examine, after the 0.618 has been clearly violated. The 0.786 is a vital Fibonacci number because it is often the last chance reversal area before retesting the original price point. Price action that does not reverse from the 0.786 usually will retest, and often break past the original starting point. Therefore, 0.786 failures are significant because the stop loss limit will be clearly defined by the original starting point and relatively small in comparison to the potential reversal. The 0.786 retracement is fairly unknown in the industry, although I believe that more technicians are becoming aware of its significance. In my opinion, it is a crucial Fibonacci number, since it is one of the last harmonic ratios before retesting a trends prior high or low and it can provide a clear indication of the future direction based upon the price action at the number. Another reason the 0.786 is a valuable Fibonacci number is because it can often gauge potential opportunities, especially when the surrounding market noise (information) suggests that the set-up is to be avoided. I have observed many situations, where the information in the media is quite contrary to what the price action at the 0.786 is indicating. If a stock is trending strongly, the 0.786 projection frequently can serve as a key reversal point, despite such contrary information. --- 帖子 #23017 ---
WTI jumps 1% on North Sea outage, OPEC cuts expectations 28 November 2018, 11:27 Expectations of OPEC output cuts, North Sea outage offer reprieve to oil prices. Buts gains appear capped amid a broadly stronger US dollar, as US-China trade woes spar safe-haven buying interest. Oil prices on both sides of the Atlantic bounced 1% on Wednesday, as the bulls found some respite from fresh supply disruption threats on reports that Britain’s largest North Sea oilfield is shut down for repairs. Reuters reported trade sources, as saying that the Buzzard oilfield, which pumps about 150,000 barrels per day (bpd) has closed temporarily after the discovery of pipe corrosion, which caused the cancelation of three cargoes due to be loaded next month. Moreover, it’s widely expected that the OPEC and non-OPEC producers will agree to reduce oil output further when they meet at their annual meeting in Vienna on December 6th. Hence, the barrel of WTI manages to find some support from the renewed hopes of OPEC output cuts that could help counter the emerging supply overhang worries.

--- 帖子 #23032 ---
Hi Gamagedara, I just tried myself and actually applying template in page #1 Fib Pivots don't show up. If you take a look in the Expert tab you'll see a line like this: Inserted Code "cannot open file 'C:\Your_MT4_Root\MQL4\indicators\Davits Pivot V3.2 Auto(2).ex4' [2]" that simply means that inside the .tpl you downloaded, the Fib Pivot Indicator has a different name. To solve this you can either try to edit the .tpl file and change the name of the indicator to match the actual name you downloaded or even better (for me) drag &amp; drop on a chart the "Pivot_Voty" Indicator leaving all the rest unchanged. At this point you should see the Fib Pivot levels to appear on your chart, then save this template and you're ready to trade. Green Pips, Bubincka

Today was the inauguration of the President of Mexico Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador. I had always mentioned he would be good for Mexico and his speech today was one for the History books. He stood by change in Mexico, the elimination of corrupt politics and being a government of and for the people. Among some of the changes were: *Eliminating perks for high ranking officials including their private jet travels and all other travels paid by the people, pensions for retired officials to include the former presidents and all excessive pays. *Starting Monday the Presidential plane, all public official helicopters and fleet will be up for sale...if anyone is interested in purchasing one... *He will only pay himself 40% of what the previous president earned. *He will not live in the "Presidential house" called Los Pinos and will transform it along with the park where it sits called Chapultepec into a public art and cultural institution. Google these and you will see the magnificence of this park which is larger than Central Park in NY and which even has a castle in it. *Within 3 years there will be free medical and medication assistance. (Much needed here). *Raising wages, reducing the price of gasoline (big issue in Mex since it is a huge oil producing country and there exists other issues involving the oil industry) reducing taxes and reducing drastically the wages for top officials to pay for all these changes. *Elderly, those with different abilities will have their benefits doubled. The young will be able to have paid internships to promote growth. *Past officials involved in corruption will be forgiven; however, from now on those officials caught in corruption will be punished even if it includes members of his family. (In the past officials used their families to carry out these acts). *They will refurbish old oil refineries and build a new one. It is not well known but Mexico has enough oil to be self sustained and sell to other countries...this is one of the main reasons I post this news here since sooner or later it will have an effect on a global scale. *He will work with Us and Canada for the approval of USMCA. ...and many more. If you have the opportunity to listen to his speech do so. For those of us who have a better understanding of this country and can find the hidden messages found in his words will see how this is the dawn of something big. Mexico can and might become a major power in the world economically and politically. Mexico has been kept hidden and is more like a sleeping giant. For those of us interested in making a career out of Forex should take notice. Green Pips

Now bulls are getting excited about a promise by the U.S. president and Chinese President Xi Jinping to put a temporary halt on new tariffs. With a month left in the year, the S&amp;P 500 is up 3.2 percent in 2018 and sits close to the midpoint of its annual range. Relative to earnings, the index trades at a multiple of about 19, cheaper than any time since early 2016. Bullish signals from Buenos Aires went beyond tariffs. Xi said he would consider approving a possible $44 billion deal for Qualcomm Inc. to purchase NXP Semiconductors NV if it’s brought to him again, the White House said in a statement. The canceled takeover was the highest-profile victim of the trade dispute between the world’s two largest economies. The market “is pricing some risk of further escalation in our view, and thus the absence of a negative G-20 outcome (i.e. agreement to just keep talking) could see the S&amp;P 500 trade toward 2,800,” Sterling will be vulnerable to swings on signs that lawmaker opposition to the deal is increasing or waning during debates that kick off on Dec. 4, ahead of a vote a week later.

Just my opinion, starting to use SL will probably lead to even more frustration. It might reduce your DD, but to me it would make more sense to work on better entrys rather than putting a SL on, because the SL wont make bad entries better, you just give the market the possibility to spike you out. To become a better trader feeling comfortable is key for me like a free solo climber feeling comfortable while climbing without ropes, with fear that wouldnt be possible. Everytime the price is heading to your SL you will start to feel uncomfortable and maybe make even more emotional decisions. The greatest thing about this pivot system to me is that it makes you comfortable while giving you space to breathe, with a SL you take that advantage away imho. When I started with Forex i thought 50 pips DD was huge. Then I saw 500, +1000 pip DD and just accepted it at one point. Happened very rarely to me, not that its a great thing, obviously you should always try to reduce DD as possible, but bad trades happen even to pro traders, therefore I think if you feel uncomfortable about DD most of the time reason for it is wrong money management. --- 帖子 #23873 ---
it isnt really that. January itself has little to do, it was a usual higher ADR trading day on the 2nd. the "crash" happened in the dead hours, after US close, before Tokyo or Sydney open. it is also clear to see that broker to broker, the scenario played out differently. see my earlier comment on how between brokers could have a further 1600 pips difference in quoted price, between their extreme. https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...1#post11840401 this is something that should never be the case, and it often is. imagine, you are a trader with 10k account, and a single 0.4 lot trade, with 50 pips SL....risking 2% of your equity; a prudent enough 2% risk with a hard SL. comes to crash, stops get ignored, and filled at the price where the broker could find a trade, if his platform havent freeze yet... ie. turned off until they internally assess their position, and match the trades as possible best suit them. remember, most brokers at best hedge part of their risk to outside, and even non full fledge bucket shops run a hybrid orderbook to their clients. then comes the time to find out how you fared, and that is where it is really hazy. GbpAud your chart Oanda high: 2.0274 on IC Markets chart: 1.8419 on Axitrader chart: 1.8826 what if you or lucky, and trading with broker A, and your loss is say 400 pips on the crash, and your account lose -2000$ on the example trade vs 2% risk "secured" by your hard SL? not great, but still enough to live another day. -20%. what if you are with broker B, and your loss is a further up to 1800 pips away, same time, same pair, just bcos your broker from somewhere quote that price? and you find out that you got hit with up to -2200 pips loss vs your 50 pips hard SL, and your 2% risk suddenly translate to up to -11000$...not only leaving you with a loss, but with a negative balance of -1000$ ( what your bucketshop broker gracefully excuse you if you deposit money again!). and that only from the unknown factor what otherwise "reputable and regulated" broker you selected, and even then with also the luck on your chosen pair in the moment of the crash. just for a second, imagine if your government lottery would pay the prize money based on location or weather you buy morning or evening the winning ticket. and as a final thought, even unleveraged, at 1:1, a possible 2200 pip drop can hurt ( see that oanda example)...10k account it means 0.1 lot ( 10k value), and a drop would still be up to 22%. these crashes not only hurt the small guys, but a lot of not so small ones as well, and on a similar drop ( 2015, CHF) a handful of smaller and bigger brokers went bankrupt... agree, Braintheboss! if any Oanda customers would ask them the simple Q: how on earth 1800 pip difference is possible on their quote vs some other broker(s)?!?!

--- 帖子 #23893 ---
Hi Nik-Nyc, far from having the real knowledge to answer your one million dollars question, first thing that comes to my mind is again ultra conservative risk management and position sizing so that you have more than enough margin to sustain such monster spikes related to your open trades. I don't say our pockets have to be deeper than the broker's ones, but the number and size of our trades should be as such to let us avoid a margin call. DD can become very big but in cases like these it lasts for a short time going from let's say 50% to less than 20% in few minutes. Another defence is to have partial closing instead of taking a full loss because these moves are instantaneous and almost immediately reversed . Then I have a personal consideration that takes me a few months back when I started to trade Davit's pivot system live. At the beginning I was happy with pips gained from simple swing between one pivot level and the previous / next so reducing my overall profits, but limiting my market exposure too. After some time, gaining confidence I began to look for bigger moves (that in theory is correct ), but doing this I leave more positions open and for much more time therefore being in danger to be hit by events like this one. From now on I'll try to go back to basics, running for lower targets for the most of my trades. Best regards , Bubincka

--- 帖子 #23899 ---
Bubincka, Thanks for sharing your thoughts. Regarding the reduction of position size and ultra-conservative money management, i see a few "problems": 1) Reward is tied to risk, so if we decrease risk too much will it be worth our time and effort to even trade? 2)Yesterday's flash-crash or spike was relatively small, as ProfitFarmer demonstrated a few posts back the probability of margin call is very real even with lower leverage. Regarding the smaller targets you mentioned, this is an interesting point because it addresses what i believe is the issue here: Exposure Risk. The longer you keep a trade open, the greater the chances of an unexpected event occuring. The only safe position in the market is to be completely flat with a regulated broker using segregated account funds. Decreasing the size of your targets, and therefore your time in the market, will decrease your exposure risk. Good point. Best, N

--- 帖子 #23901 ---
Happy new year everyone . My take on the avoidance of flash crashes is that it can't be avoided but can be managed by factoring it in into our trading. because we (retail traders) don't make this moves to occur and can't predict when . However, by careful observation of holiday periods----summer breaks (August),Christmas holidays(December) and January , I think the underlying factor that is common to all of them is Thin Liquidity. Huge market participants take advantage of this to gun for the stops and market behavior in this periods tend to be inconsistent with normal price movements. My Action plan would be to reduce my exposure to the market by at least 1/2 of my usual lot size and also my holding period of any pair will be reduced as dimmed fit .

--- 帖子 #23902 ---
True, there isn't a single solution to the overal problem, however, the risk can be minimized as much as possible. Agreed, SL simply exist to help retail traders sleep better at night. In low liquidity your exit will be based on the next available matching order, which could be 100's or 1000's of pips away from your emergency SL. Smart. Moving away from unregulated spot forex markets definitely decreases risk. Yesterdays Oanda spike should make any trader realize they are not operating on a level playing field and move on to greener pastures. Now, flash crashes and swan-type events can happen in the futures markets, but simply comparing their frequency and size should make you feel a lot more comfortable about trading these markets. Glad you escaped unscathed, even happier you realize it was nothing more than a lot of luck and a little patience. Discomfort can be a great motivator. If you haven't heard of Nassim Nicholas Taleb, i highly recommend his books, he is a bit of an authority on the subject. Black Swan, Anti-Fragile, and Fooled by Randmoness are all great reads.

--- 帖子 #23915 ---
No need to apologize to me, but perhaps to profitfarmer. Regarding Oanda, they are a terrible broker. The algorithm they use to display a "price" and "spread" to their trader is an aggregate of price from their liquidity providers which are a who's who of banks you'd rather not trust. Furthermore, the price displayed is always to the advantage of oanda's trades and disadvantage to their book (aka you). Furthermore, while spread is an natural phenomenon caused by il-liquidity in a dual auction process, bad brokers such as oanda use it artificially to either trigger stops, decrease their losers (your winners), or simply discourage trading at times they see fit.

--- 帖子 #23925 ---
Hi ASW, I am well versed on the aspects of leverage and what it means. Apologies, but its ludicrous to state that high leverage is a good thing. Unless you are a broker, they love it! The innate use of leverage means you are undercapitalised, you are trading on credit. I am not saying I don't use it, I do, but as I stated above, I use it within my means i.e relative to my 'actual' capital. If you like examples, look at this scenario: 10k account, 1:30 leverage, say I am in at 1:15 (using only half), so my position size is 150K. Then there is 400 pip spike akin to what just happened. The account is down over 5K, ~50%DD. Now, you say high leverage is good? (even typing that gives me shivers). What if we take it up to 1:20, or 1:25. The account is now as valuable as a tit on a man!

--- 帖子 #22761 ---
Photography used to be my favorite activity before I took up trading. Having a lens with f/1.8 (or faster) is nice for shooting low light indoor without flash. A steady tripod helps, but quite often one is not available. To get steady hands for 1/40 sec or even slower shutter speed can be achieved by the photographer leaning against a wall, have the elbow against the table, or the hand holding the camera rest against some solid place. To avoid "moving" the camera when pushing the shutter button, I sometimes use a shutter release cable. Sometimes I set the camera to a self timer (5 seconds) so my finger won't be applying any force on the camera when the shutter opens and closes. (I have not tried the new shutter-less cameras). Photography is fun. You took some pretty nice pictures, Davit, especially with the depth of field showing some promise. Have a good weekend. Bill

--- 帖子 #23961 ---
Hi, if your only light source is candles (no window or overhead lights), you might find the contrast is too much. If that’s the case you can point the flash at the ceiling as a fill light. Experiment with the power of the flash to get the contrast you like. Also, to keep the color balance you can put an orange gel over the flash, just go to Hunt’s in Melrose and they can guide you.

If your camera allows, you can try to set the color temperature to something like 4500 or 4000 degrees. That will reduce the orange of the candles a little bit but they’ll still have warmth. Alternatively, you can set the camera to daylight (but not auto) and put a blue gel over the lens, like a 1/8 or 1/4 blue. That will have the same affect on the candles, to reduce the orange just a little bit.

--- 帖子 #24180 ---
Bigger Picture, and I'm not guessing. S61 to look for swing fail Bullish inverted hammer TDI will make higher lows Main refinancing rate 5.1% Trader’s Behavior The pattern occurs in a bearish background and the black candlestick that appears on the first day further supports the bearishness. On the second day, in which an Inverted Hammer is seen, market opens at or near its low. Then prices change direction and we see a rally. However, the bulls do not succeed in sustaining the rally during the rest of the day and prices finally close either at or near the low of the day. It may not be clear why this type of price action is interpreted as a potential reversal signal. The answer has to do with what happens over the next day. If the next day opens above the body of the Inverted Hammer, it means that those who shorted at the opening or closing of the Inverted Hammer day are losing money. The longer the market holds above the Inverted Hammer’s body, the more likely these shorts will attempt to cover their positions. This may ignite a rally as a result of covered short positions, which may then inspire the bottom pickers to take long positions.

--- 帖子 #24192 ---
EC Google Scott Carney 786 fib you'll get interesting results. 78Fib is not even on Fib Meta tool default setting (you can add manually)and many traders are unaware of its significance. "0.786 Retracement The 0.786 retracement is the square root of the 0.618. The 0.786 retracement is the next critical area to examine, after the 0.618 has been clearly violated. The 0.786 is a vital Fibonacci number because it is often the last chance reversal area before retesting the original price point. Price action that does not reverse from the 0.786 usually will retest, and often break past the original starting point. Therefore, 0.786 failures are significant because the stop loss limit will be clearly defined by the original starting point and relatively small in comparison to the potential reversal. The 0.786 retracement is fairly unknown in the industry, although I believe that more technicians are becoming aware of its significance. In my opinion, it is a crucial Fibonacci number, since it is one of the last harmonic ratios before retesting a trends prior high or low and it can provide a clear indication of the future direction based upon the price action at the number. Another reason the 0.786 is a valuable Fibonacci number is because it can often gauge potential opportunities" Scott Carney

Consumer confidence surveys 8. Trade balance 9. Manufacturing sector surveys Keep in mind any of these events can be more important then others if that's the only thing in the week.Above are key events.Why is being aware of events help trading?This is like asking why study the terrain before a battle.Its about planning your trading ahead of news and after.Your expectations may not meet but does not mean ignorance is an Edge its not. I study weekly events for planning my trades but its a loose concept meaning I am not 100% committed before I see how prices move.For example I could not say before ECB Thurs I would sell EU on Sat prior.This would be projecting your bias incorrectly.What is correct behavior is know that ECB is on Thurs and wait to see opportunities to hit. Example both EC and EA hit Pivots tops hours ego and descending now and one could sell until ECB then get out.This is good example of being aware you would be surprised how many traders don't even know ECB event today.Like I said ignorance is not an EDGE I don't trade news I trade sentiment /pivots and price action .News to me is part of sentiment. Being aware of this helps understanding the market moves. Over time you will see moves almost predict it with higher accuracy because you are in tune with the market.Takes time and why trading is hard there is no easy steps of 1 2 3.I am not an expert I share what helps me.You laid out your EDGE and rest is probabilities.I know my EDGE. regards

Many fail here in fact ... most. because they just hit trigger when price is at one simple 61 or 78 , without chart bigger structure picture view and PA , 61,78 or 100 are just simple lines that may means ... nothing.

--- 帖子 #24358 ---
Here is https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...6#post10795636 STOP LOSS 1 Decide how much each swing is worth example $500 2. Divide $500 into mini lots for multiple entries example .50c a pip gives 1000 pip distance 3. This allows averaging in orders as seen fit irregardless if previous orders are in red 4. Orders are placed as long as reason for trade is still valid 5. If conditions change loss is taken since orders are not placed all at once this allows smaller loss Swings Each Swing investment $500 (example yours could be anything) Swing is taken as loss once -$500 is reached There are no exceptions.No running red beyond $500 Orders broken down into mini lots that satisfies each swing consist of 10-15 trades My budget for this is 2-3% of account risk say $500 for example.I then enter trades on mini lots and as long as my 500 is not consumed on DD and I am still confident of my trade I stay on it.I may choose to get out early but most times my SL is predetermined.This allows me to cast a wider net. So my 10mini lots can cover 50pip distance hence capture better RR There is advantage to trade this way.Should PA go against you and you no longer like the trade you can get out by fraction of lot invested hence your loss is minimal instead of traditional 1 trade 1lot per trade when if wrong loss is substantially higher. Numbers posted are for examples only

Trade What You See How to Proﬁt from Pattern Recognition LARRY PESAVENTO LESLIE JOUFLAS From my library of books.Notice I have been aggressively trying to install good habits on my system like Calendar events etc.Point was to be consistent in making money. STEPS TO TAKE FOR SUCCESSFUL TRADING One very important item to keep in mind while learning to trade: Each action you take repeatedly will become a habit. The habits that form will lead to either your success or your failure. Habits in and of themselves are neutral; they do not know if they have a positive or negative effect. However, the results of the habits will have a negative or positive outcome in your trading. Therefore, it is in the best interest of each trader to strive to form the very best habits that will ensure success. Traders want to strive for a point in their trading where they are just doing the necessary actions . They should have a high conﬁdence level that over time the edge in their trading will have a positive expectation .This will be developed through testing and implementing a speciﬁc trading strategy. We hope the items we have listed will help you determine which direction you are taking. If you are an experienced trader and you have already formed habits that are not producing the desired results, then take time to evaluate your trading and begin to form new habits that will get you the results you desire in trading. Chapter 13 has a worksheet titled “Twenty Sample Trades Worksheet” , designed to help traders instill new trading habits. It focuses on doing the same positive action through a series of trades to create new habits and to observe how the trading edge is played out. Positive habits will produce positive results. Negative habits will produce negative results and will be self-defeating. It may be helpful to make a list of any negative habits that are present in your trading, and a separate list of positive habits to replace those. An example of a negative habit may be that the trader consistently exits a trade before the proﬁt objective is reached. The new positive habit will have the trader hold for the proﬁt objective. Another example may be that the trader enters early before a pattern is completed. The new positive habit will have the trader enter at the correct entry point. Once traders understand and know what their edge is,they will begin to see the importance of consistently executing their plan. They will see if there is a gap between where they are and where they want to be. This is a point where the trader can then ﬁll in the necessary steps to close that gap. Conversely, pay attention to your positive habits. The actions you are doing right in your trading can be developed further into strengths. Develop support systems to help you instill new positive habits. A support system may be using a buddy system with another trader. It never hurts to have accountability with someone else that can help keep you on the path to your goals,but in the long run each action is your responsibility. Here is a list you can use to help develop your personal plan of action to reach the success level you want in trading: Ĺ Create positive habits . Ĺ Replace negative habits with positive habits. Ĺ Take 100 percent responsibility for each outcome. Ĺ Create a support system to help keep you on the path to your goals. Ĺ Take a proactive approach to making changes in your trading. Start with a list of actions that you need to take to reach your goals. Believe in yourself; know that you are a successful trader. As you study the trading patterns in this book, we hope that the aforementioned items will help you to develop as a successful trader.

Nice progress.Just a correction when I say price rallies I don't mean tiny fluctuations of price on 1min chart.Rally to me is (look at the chart) Its pretty obvious It took me many years really to understand the markets and once you do everything falls in right place. One of the key components of successful trading is mimicking what market makers/ institutional traders do that is In down trend SELL the Rallies UP trend Buy the Dips Not sure about the trend click on weekly chart and look at closed candles.Is price making HH? Yes? or Is it ranging? You have to get this right.Anyway this is to me professional way to see price and your actions should be in sink. Cyclical structure of the markets hitting heavy orders collecting profits.This happens within a larger trend. Pivots reflects this cycle accumulation distribution profit taking. --- 帖子 #24907 ---
They were told to shut down operations in Russia and I suspect there are Russian own... https://financefeeds.com/russian-for...de-trustforex/ The Association of Forex dealers, the Russian Forex self-regulatory organization (SRO), has earlier today announced that it is terminating the membership of five companies: Alpari Forex , Forex Club, TeleTrade, Fix Trade and TrustForex. The decision follows the revocation of the Forex dealer licenses of these five companies by the Central Bank of Russia. The regulator explained that the five brokers had repeatedly violated the Russian securities law. The violations range from providing false accounting statements to failures to follow the instructions issued by the Central Bank. Under the Russian laws, licensed FX companies have to be members of an SRO. Unlicensed companies cannot be members of the FX SRO. Hence, the move by the Association is in line with the law. "Alpari Forex failed to follow the instructions of the Central Bank of Russia. The company committed violations in the way it handled its internal accounting. The company also provided false accounting data and committed violations when handling risks."

Hi Davit, Another way to get around this with Oanda is by transferring to their primary in-house account server vs. their offshore V2 account server, then be able to withdraw money in $300 to $500 or more with each transaction on the same day with the same debit card. However, transferring directly into your Bank MAY incur extra fees. But this may have changed since last year after they went all to V2 except their in-house default servers. Good Luck... --- 帖子 #25019 ---
I have been PM'd this question so many times so i'll say it again here. Current weekly pivots are arrived from the calculation of previous week. Fibonacci Pivot Point Calculations Weekly Pivot is the calculation of: (H+L+C) / 3 Weekly Pivot Supports Levels are calculated as follows: S1 = Pivot - 0.382 * (H - L) S2 = Pivot - 0.618 * (H - L) S3 = Pivot - 1.000 * (H - L) ..etc Weekly Pivot Resistance Levels are calculated as follows: R1 = Pivot + 0.382 * (H - L) R2 = Pivot + 0.618 * (H - L) R3 = Pivot + 1.000 * (H - L) ..etc Meanings of abbreviations: H = Previous day's high. L = Previous day's low. C = Previous day's closing price. S1 = First level of support. S2 = Second level of support. S3 = Third level of support. R1 = First level of resistance. R2 = Second level of resistance. R3 = Third level of resistance. .....and so on

Hello all --- I am following NZD news Official Cash Rate unchanged at 1.75 percent Statement by Reserve Bank Governor Adrian Orr: Tena koutou katoa, welcome all. The Official Cash Rate (OCR) remains at 1.75 percent. We expect to keep the OCR at this level through 2019 and 2020. The direction of our next OCR move could be up or down. Employment is near its maximum sustainable level. However, core consumer price inflation remains below our 2 percent target mid-point, necessitating continued supportive monetary policy. Trading-partner growth is expected to further moderate in 2019 and global commodity prices have already softened, reducing the tailwind that New Zealand economic activity has benefited from. The risk of a sharper downturn in trading-partner growth has also heightened over recent months. Despite the weaker global impetus, we expect low interest rates and government spending to support a pick-up in New Zealand’s GDP growth over 2019. Low interest rates, and continued employment growth, should support household spending and business investment. Government spending on infrastructure and housing also supports domestic demand. As capacity pressures build, consumer price inflation is expected to rise to around the mid-point of our target range at 2 percent. There are upside and downside risks to this outlook. A more pronounced global downturn could weigh on domestic demand, but inflation could rise faster if firms pass on cost increases to prices to a greater extent. We will keep the OCR at an expansionary level for a considerable period to contribute to maximising sustainable employment, and maintaining low and stable inflation.

This is how i trade, I wait for the 4 hour close. Davit said that the 4hr is too late you will miss pips and i totally agree but i also think it prevents me being in DD. When the 4hr closes in a good pivot zone then next stage is I look at 5 day ADR. For instance the A/U is 48 so i say 50 pips. i make my mark and open positions. When price is going in my favour i add positions all away to my target but the last 1/4 i stop just incase price turns early and i have to close early. If price doesn't go in my favour then i wait until the next pivot and for 4Hr to close and the take next steps in order to gain the DD and make profit. I am a novice so i would take what i say with a pinch of salt but this works for me.
