What Im trying to say is that the ADR daily high and low is influenced by those sudden spikes in the market, if for example I used a 20 day ADR. Therefore I like to use a shorter time period. You are right the ADR cannot tell direction BUT what I have noticed is that the ADR and the TDI does really work together. Whenever the TDI indicates overbought/long caution I’ve noticed that my ADR is close to the daily high or even went beyond. Othe ADR’s will already be deep into the red numbers, and I struggled with this. For me those alerts comes with this version of the TDI PRO that I bought from Dean. That is why Im calling it my trading buddy.(TDI) Now there is two values that I get from the ADR namely, Daily high/ low, and when price passes the daily high by far going up for example. Then I would deduct the high from the low and add it to the daily high to get my overbought. Hope it make sense as I must express my self typing. As you can see from my last chart the “overbought” is @ the 85+ level. Also I’m using a 3 day for my daily high/ low and my 20 day would be my monthly. I think his point was more that the amount of trades he had taken were over the top, 65 short positions on a single trade. When we talk about breaking down fear and reducing risk by decreasing lot size and placing multiple trades were talking of breaking 1 trade into something like 10 mini lots. This allows us to add on continuations of trends, pullbacks/retests and news events that are in confluence with our bias, in turn reducing our fear of the trade going against us. I can imagine that managing 65 positions per pair could get very hectic. After a certain extent all it does is increase your pip count. I think he understands the concept that's why he suggested that 16 would be enough at 1.0 per lot. Just my opinion.

--- 帖子 #25605 ---
Some of you might be wondering why I closed EC Fine lets go over why. From left candle to right WP major R/S 1st candle.Engulfing bear candle 2nd candle.Doji When a market’s open and close are almost at the same price point, the candlestick resembles a cross or plus sign – traders should look out for a short to non-existent body, with wicks of varying length. This doji’s pattern conveys a struggle between buyers and sellers that results in no net gain for either side. Alone a doji is neutral signal, but it can be found in reversal patterns such as the bullish morning star and bearish evening star. 3rd candle larger bull candle then previous doji. 4th another doji The reason I waited because after 1st engulfing bear candle I was waiting for a continuation of that move which did not come. When you put all together Bear momentum is not looking great hence taking my profits out of the market. What I anticipate may happen back to 50 test and may provide reload.

--- 帖子 #25611 ---
Something I want to get out of my chest.Its important You'll read lots of science fiction conspiracy theories by "experts" here at FF like Forex is moved by single entity etc.Become totally cryptic to read etc. This is categorically false. Forex is tremendously huge to be controlled by single entity .Amount of volume being exchanged is in trillions not easy to hide this volume for so long if it was single entity..Fact is even big banks market makers lose money in Forex and this fact alone illustrates that players are multi and competition is fierce! How typically big Banks Market makers fill their orders Every trade that is executed in the forex markets has to have a buyer and seller and when this takes place then we have a trade. This normally happens in a fraction of a second electronically but in essence, each time you enter a buy trade you are being matched with someone who is happy to enter a sell position and take the opposite side of your trade. If this doesn’t happen then there wouldn’t be a trade. Why is this so important? Because it highlights the problems that large banks have which small traders don’t. Any retail trader is able to place whatever position size they wish into the market without ever fearing slippage or bad fill. Granted slippage may take place during high impact news items such as central bank announcements but on the whole, most of the executed trades are done instantaneously. Now if you’re a retail trader trading 1 standard Lot then you won’t have any problems with being filled at the price you want. Imagine you’re trading 100 Lots or 500 Lots or 1000 lots, these are larger positions to put into the market at any one time and it’s much more difficult to find someone to take the other side of the trade at the exact price and the exact tim e that you want and therefore might not be filled at a great price. Well, what could you do in such a situation? You have one of three options: Option 1: You could either bite the bullet and get executed at whatever price you are able to get, the only problem here is that you won’t be getting the best price possible for your trade which eats into your profits. Option 2: You could wait for the price to get to the price level you want so that you get the best execution possible and buy or sell at a much more favorable price – this is great but what if the price doesn’t get to the level you want for you to execute your trade? You will either be forced to walk away without making a trade or be forced to take whatever price you can get if doing the trade is absolutely essential Option 3: You force the price to get to the level at which you want to transact by cleverly manipulating other smaller traders to push the market in the direction you want it to go. Once you get the price to the level you want then you can carry out your transaction. How can you do this? By taking massive positions and exercising your muscle. This is similar to when large companies and conglomerates bully smaller businesses out of the market through aggressive competition. Targeting price towards stops /limit orders triggers sudden liquidity which fills MM orders and why just about every swing ends with a spike! Now you understand why sudden drop or spike of price is no guarantee that price will travel same direction of spike.Often its the opposite specially towards swing tops bottoms. I hope this explains it

--- 帖子 #24406 ---
Hi D no problem. Used fib retracement on mt4 mobile. Plotted anywhere on the screen from bottom to top. From there I highlight and hold the fib retr tool till it shows a pop-up window where you can adjust the properties. In the properties tab you can change the levels according to my screenshot values and naming it accordingly. For the two point values you can get it from the link provided in previous post. Point 1 is your Pivot Point value and point 2 is your Support 3 value. Hope this makes sense to you. EDIT: Every time you place the fib retracement on a new pair the levels are automatically set as per the new levels and naming. You need to plug the point values in for each pair then. Takes some time but def worth the while for me.

Next target I'm looking to snipe is EUR/AUD. Looking at getting in between R78 and R100 depending on PA. This will take a few days to play out 5-9 days I'm thinking. May go beyond R100 with some EUR events tomorrow so I would suggest to manage your trades and be aware of news events coming out and possible outcomes. I prefer these longer term swing trades, you need to think of these trades as a giant boat. A giant boat like the Titanic doesn't turn fast, so these will take time to turn around. Why is that? Well usually the bigger traders need time to get into their positions, they not small speed boats like us. So they take the price up/down and build their position. Sometimes the price doesn't turn around, but I feel like these trades work out about 70% of the time so you need to know when to stop out or you may be in DD for a long time if you don't manage your account. You might bust out your account if you go too large. Like Davit trades it is best to have small lots and your net cast out over a few pairs. Never trade just one trade, you need to have an average of trades that will win. If you just put everything into one trade, will likely bust out your account sooner or later. Again trying to impart some trading wisdom into the forum. Always will try to put some nuggets in. Davit if ever I say something wrong please just delete my post, but I think we are on the same page for the most part in our trading style. Best

Two Hidden Virtues of Successful Traders One of the most interesting aspects of working as a trading coach is the ability to see, first hand, what contributes to the success of traders. So often the factors that lead to success are not those emphasized in mainstream articles and books. Here are two unappreciated virtues I see among successful portfolio managers and traders: 1) The ability to tolerate uncertainty - Suppose you take any particular configuration of price in a market; say, trading x% above or below a Y period moving average. Then look at what that market does on average over the next Y period. The odds are great that for any value of x and Y, the market's directional tendency will be swamped by the variability of price within that next Y period. What that means is that, on average, the signal to noise ratio for a directional trader is low. Whatever directional tendency is present is generally not statistically significant and not readily tradeable. Given such a situation, the modal opinion of any trader should be "I don't know". Uncertainty is itself a view and, in fact, should be one's base case. When a trader cannot tolerate uncertainty and needs to manufacture conviction, the result inevitably is overtrading the objective opportunity set. It is impossible to properly manage risk if you are intolerant of uncertainty. 2) The productivity of time spent away from trading - I consistently find that successful traders spend more time identifying good trading opportunities than actually putting on and managing trades. Csikszentmihalyi conducted a fascinating study with artists in which they were shown 27 objects and asked to arrange a small group of them into a composition and generate a sketch. They had one hour for the task. The artists fell into two categories. One group quickly identified the objects for the composition and spent the better part of the hour refining their sketches. The second group spent most the hour figuring out what to draw. They selected objects, started sketches, changed the objects, sketched some more, rearranged objects, etc. By the time they found the composition they liked, they spent only a few minutes on the final sketch. The drawings of the second group were rated as significantly more creative by a group of art critics than those of the first group and, after a five year period, the second group demonstrated significantly greater success as artists. The less successful artists spent most their time sketching. The successful artists spent most their time finding compositions worthy of sketching. It's a great analogy for trading. Good things happen when these two strengths come together. The ability to accept uncertainty frees the mind to maximize time away from trading and creatively generate sound trade ideas. For the successful trader, uncertainty provides the opportunity to get away from screens and look at markets through new lenses. Overtrading exists when the need to trade exceeds the need to understand. By Brett Steenbarger, Ph.D.

Sun NZD Retail Sales q/q 0.5% 0.0% The economic calendar for next week gets an early start with key data from New Zealand during the Sunday Asian session. This data release gets extra attention because it’s a data set that we would typically expect to receive monthly. However, in New Zealand, we only get to see it quarterly. Here’s a look at what’s been going on and what we might expect from the markets even before the weekend is over. There are three versions of quarterly retail sales all coming out at the same time: Sunday 22:45 CET (or 16:45 EST). The data is relevant to the next publication out of New Zealand expected on Tuesday evening. The start of the event is the quarterly change in retail sales. This is expected to accelerate to 1.3% growth, compared to the 0.0% reported previously . This is the figure the market usually focuses on. Additionally, we have Core Retail sales , which exclude automotive-related purchases. This data is expected to increase by 2.1% compared to 0.4% prior. Finally, we have the year over year comparison in retail sales . This is expected to have increased by 9.7% compared to 2.7% in the third quarter. --- 帖子 #26190 ---
Pivot traders are those who believe that the exact value or price of a stock at any particular time is unknowable.

--- 帖子 #26191 ---
Dare I say: "Pivot traders are those that trade swings profitably. They are fully aware of news events, without making any predictions about them. They manage risks appropriately and are calm and collected during drawdowns, which they view as natural spasms of MMs running their stops. Pivot traders use a rubber-band theory, whereby prices tend to reverse after they've had a(n often MM-induced) run in one direction. Pivot traders don't trade GJ or F pairs, and they recognize that LOCATION, like in real estate, is everything. Hence, MAs are totally irrelevant, as are all oscillators and their divergence-related indicators. Pivot traders don't know the future, nor do they need to, to make money (Mark Douglas)."

--- 帖子 #26284 ---
All those pointers were great, I will add to it if I may. It requires planning in advance. If you have to question yourself, then you entered a trade based on entry alone. You should enter a trade based on an entry and exit strategy. Knowing your target beforehand will allow you to see clearer those areas where price might stall or retrace a bit but it is not quite the intended target. That is where you would most likely add. It takes time and lots of practice. My advice...there are a lot of great trade ideas in this thread and all over the internet for that matter...but until one sits down and do it without the influence of others you will start seeing these things and you build confidence and trust your system. Anyone can take someone else trade...it takes a trader to trade his own analysis. If you do not plan your trades you will be at the mercy of the market.

--- 帖子 #26294 ---
Here is how to trade pivots (TS use weekly pivot, not daily Pivot..) As price travels progressively away from weekly pivot it becomes more likely to go into correction. 61 S/R key zone 78R/S is Scott Carney's last chance for reversal (spikes stops taken before reversal) 100R/S another major zone. Should price smash 100 S/R then you are in strong trend supported by fundamentals. Attached File(s) Pivot Trading with TDI.pdf 3.7 MB | 917 downloads

--- 帖子 #26309 ---
For what it is worth I have made the following observation in regard to this system of trading. If price goes past the 61.8 - 100 Fib pivot levels and does not return to the weekly pivot. This can be regarded as a 'missed pivot'. The probability of price returning to next week's pivot is very high. You can use the following indicator which I got from Davits thread to check this out. Set the number of weeks to say 20 and look back on any missed pivots and you'll see that price almost always return to the following weeks pivot, only in exceptional cases is this not true. This may allow you to average out to a win or BE.

I still have so much to learn, but one thing that helps immensely is not getting worked up when I get stopped out. I'm learning to evaluate the trade from the perspective of a market maker and not a retail trader. I look at every chart now to see where I think stops losses and the biggest profits from their side of the trade would be. I was in a trade and didn't look to the left to see where the smartest place to put my stop would be and when they ran the market down in it got hit and I had to admire their skill in hitting it. I put it exactly where everyone else did... rookie mistake. When I take a hit (which is becoming less and less), I re-evalute things because I failed to understand the psychology of the big boys on the other end of the trade. I love making money, but I equally love the challenge of taking what seems like an irrational market and looking at it from the standpoint that it's simply market movements that undulate in precise movements to make money for the institutions. It's a privilege to be able to join them in trading so I better learn how to trade like them. --- 帖子 #23878 ---
Fibonacci Pivot Point R3 = PP + ((High – Low) x 1.000) R2 = PP + ((High – Low) x .618) R1 = PP + ((High – Low) x .382) PP = (H + L + C) / 3 S1 = PP – ((High – Low) x .382) S2 = PP – ((High – Low) x .618) S3 = PP – ((High – Low) x 1.000) C – Closing Price, H – High, L – Low Fibonacci pivot point levels are determined by first calculating the pivot point like you would the standard method. Next, multiply the previous day’s range with its corresponding Fibonacci level. Most traders use the 38.2%, 61.8% and 100% retracements in their calculations. With Davit's the 78% is also included and also all the way to 200% Link https://www.babypips.com/learn/forex...lation-methods

--- 帖子 #26800 ---
TLTRO (Targeted Longer Term Refinancing Operations) is one of the many monetary policy operations that the European Central Bank has at its disposal to help real economy: actions aimed at introducing money into the system, through banking credit, to help the real economy. Historically this is the third stimulus attempt to help economy of euro area. In simpler terms, the funds that the Brussels institution makes available in these operations are provided to the banks, which in turn will use them to improve the provision of bank loans to the non-financial private sector in eurozone. The problem is always the same: it's bank's choice to decide whether to grant or not credit to the private sector... in Italy this is not so simple to obtain, even if you are healthy and have a good balance. Better to help big indebted groups from failure or bankruptcy where banks have a lot to recover instead of small and medium companies. IMHO

--- 帖子 #26825 ---
Nice post, although let me disagree with one point- MMs do not care about retail. They do not seek to take your stops, they do not seek to catch you unprepared, they do not seek your liquidity. Retail liquidity is unimportant to them. MMs trade in lots sizes of hundred milions on interbank markets and they fulfill orders of their corporate customers or hedge funds. They even doesnt use TA that much. Market Maker in spot forex aka spot dealer, is a guy who sits in a bank and tries to not lose money when he has to fulfill order for 1 bilion USD before market moves few cents agains him, while 10 other customers calling him to make deal. Market makers seldom do directional positions, their main goal is to be squared very quickly and make only some pips on spread. Banks as whole usually have directional positions,but they are longterm. Hedge funds are actually the ones who give orders to banks to buy for them and they do apply their strategies on market, but not market makers, that is only a provider of the service. If you are interested, I would higly reccomend this video. This is actual ex-forex market maker from one of the biggest world banks and tells what the market maker job is about. It is not a selling gig, just casual conversation about his past job. I can confirm 100% of what he says from my own experience. Might be little eye opening for some... Lots of success to you! " I would like to spend a few minutes discussing the first topic. Because interest rates around the world have steadily declined for several decades, rates in normal times now tend to be much closer to zero than in the past ( figure 5 ). 8 Thus, when a recession comes, the Fed is likely to have less capacity to cut interest rates to stimulate the economy than in the past, suggesting that trips to the ELB may be more frequent. The post-crisis period has seen many economies around the world stuck for an extended period at the ELB, with slow growth and inflation well below target. Persistently weak inflation could lead inflation expectations to drift downward, which would imply still lower interest rates, leaving even less room for central banks to cut interest rates to support the economy during a downturn. It is therefore very important for central banks to find more effective ways to battle the low-inflation syndrome that seems to accompany proximity to the ELB." https://www.federalreserve.gov/newse...l20190308a.htm Got to love this guy. I really wait market reaction to this on Monday (Sunday for some). If that means there won't be any interest rate hikes this year, USD will weaken significantly.

--- 帖子 #27016 ---
This was what I was waiting for on AUD/NZD Notice I have a limit order, just in case it retest the low while I sleep. These pivot turnarounds tend to always test the lows before reversal, not always though. Some pairs do tend to test and retest more often, take note of which pairs do (USD/CAD usually test multiple times, really slow to turn around) this doesn't last forever but over months you will notice patterns. Like a lot of NZD pairs don't tend to retest the pivot (turn around area) lows/highs ATM (look at NZD/CAD or EUR/NZD recently) Keep in mind I'm trading for a few days looking for 100-200 pips. I'm not too concerned with swaps, although I try to time my entry to miss a few days of swaps when possible, if I wait until after the swap hr to enter, and exit before the swap hr I will save 2 days. Every trade is different.

Hello Bubincka, I was able to stay in the trade despite news for a few reasons. First my position was in profit to start and I don't really care if the news goes my way or not, I'm confident I will be alright. Second, I try to start every trade realizing what my max loss would be and I have accepted that. In my case trading non high ADR pairs I am trading .10 lot sizes with max loss of about 50 pips per trade. I go into every trade expecting it to lose and that is the real cost of my trade. Third, I have a target of what I realistically expect price to get to and I try to stick to it (hard to do various other reasons may come up to exit). Forth I'm not trading my entire account on one trade, always diversify. Although many times every week it will come down to 1 or 2 home run trades the other trades I have flying spread out risk even though they might be similar, I then can add to winners and thin out or not add to losers. For instance in USD/CAD now, I simply put in a stop at a level I'm good with. So if it keep crashing I'm good if it reverses I'm good too. Everyone has a different account and their own circumstances. It is important to respect your stress level. Nothing wrong with taking profit or a loss just know why you did. You can explore how you could have traded it differently after the fact and this is healthy, but don't beat yourself up about what you think you may have done wrong cause every trade is different and no certainty same thing will happen again tomorrow.

Davit's Post 27,039, March 13, 5.37am Davit has stressed the importance of the Daily Open (5pm EDT) as setting a Daily Trend but also the London Open as often setting a Session Trend. The New York Open similarly should be marked as well - often confirms the London Session trend. Tie these to Red News Events and Price Action. I have a single chart that I refer to that uses the Daily Open Indicator (x3). Simply set London 10 hours and New York 15 hours after the Daily Open. There are probably better indicators but you do not necessarily need them on each chart. As a weekend exercise, look at these Market Open times and relate them to the Weekly Pivot levels. from 2018 post Hi Guys About drawdowns This subject is often misunderstood and twisted into gross forum debates and traders who have history of blown accounts.Very few understand nature of DD DD is essential part of any successful trading system if anyone tells you otherwise they are lying and deceiving you. There is no such thing as zero DD system that is successful long term.This comes down to stop losses.Are you going to take a loss every time price goes against you 20-30pips?If yes you will deplete your account before you know it. Trades need room to develop!! If executed properly based on the Edge of the system then allow the edge to develop.Running 5% 10% even 15% is acceptable if you are growing your account same time. This is true of most successful systems. If you are running 10% DD but gaining your account same time by end of the year you will be still in great profit.This is the truth in trading The dream of novice market speculators is that they will continually bask in the warmth of profitable times. This myth is falsely promised by the promoters of trading systems and trading training programs. In fact, just the opposite is true. Most long-term profitable traders spend the vast majority of their trading careers either in Trading Drawdowns or recovering from a drawdown. Any slick promoter who tells you different is not dealing from a full deck. Most successful long-term traders are underwater the majority of time. Welcome to trading! I have and had DD most of the times.In fact it does not bother me at all because I trust my EDGE to generate more then my DD in consistent bases. That's it

--- 帖子 #27166 ---
Whenever you hear a Trader claiming 100% win rate or strike rate.Be aware you are dealing with falsehood and fraudulent characters. In trading its simply impossible. That's same as knowing 100% the future.Not possible! Don't fall for it no matter the claims! Deductive Reasoning Deductive reasoning derives specifics from what is already known. It was the preferred form of reasoning used by ancient rhetoricians like Aristotle to make logical arguments. A syllogism is an example of deductive reasoning that is commonly used when teaching logic. A syllogism is an example of deductive reasoning in which a conclusion is supported by major and minor premises. The conclusion of a valid argument can be deduced from the major and minor premises. A commonly used example of a syllogism is “All humans are mortal. Socrates is a human. Socrates is mortal.” In this case, the conclusion, “Socrates is mortal,” is derived from the major premise, “All humans are mortal,” and the minor premise, “Socrates is a human.” In some cases, the major and minor premises of a syllogism may be taken for granted as true. In the previous example, the major premise is presumed true because we have no knowledge of an immortal person to disprove the statement. The minor premise is presumed true because Socrates looks and acts like other individuals we know to be human. Detectives or scientists using such logic would want to test their conclusion. We could test our conclusion by stabbing Socrates to see if he dies, but since the logic of the syllogism is sound, it may be better to cut Socrates a break and deem the argument valid.

I don't trade well from my phone either. I monitor trades from it if I have to, but generally I close them out if I can't watch them closely. I have a medical practice that involves a lot of house calls and emergencies and I find that occasionally I'm pleasantly surprised, but usually more often than not, I don't like my outcomes. I did figure out how to use a free app called Teamviewer so I can remotely watch trades from my desktop at home and that has helped, but it's still not ideal for me on the small screen. I've using more limit and stop orders to help combat some of the screen watching. Have you tried that? I'm sure others have better ideas on it, it's just what I've been doing. Trading pushes buttons I never knew I had... and I'm used to working under severe pressure; but I do find that meditation and observation in that time of reflection help me immensely. Like Davit just posted today, I'm learning to let my DD's breathe and not close out so quickly when a move goes against me if I've studied and feel like I've made an intelligent decision. No one can be right all of the time. Heck, we all deal with that in our daily lives - we mess up -we make bad judgments and lousy calls. I'd rather lose a little bit of money than hurt the ones I love. So, kick back, reassess, and figure out your mistakes. You can do this but you can't let yourself be psyched out. Don't give up!

All, I've been reading and following the thread for a while and wanted to contribute and add some value for everyone while I'm learning. I thought a beneficial way to do this would be to mod the trade report and add a column for drawdown %. I've been testing it and it seems to work quite well. I also added the ability to input a starting balance so all the percentages shown in the report can be based off a set number (starting balance of account, or starting balance of the week etc). In addition I have also included the functionality to hide all the columns giving you the choice to pick and choose which ones to show. I'm am currently testing and it seems to be working well. However, it may have a few bugs and might not be spot on so please only use it as a reference only. These are my current trades Attached Image (click to enlarge) I think the most effective way to use the report would be to input new settings on a sunday night by first setting the time period for the coming week, then inputting your current account balance into the settings in the " use balance for calculations" field, then your results will show a proper representation of your trading performance at the end of the week Attached Image (click to enlarge) If you input a "0" into this field it will use your current balance for calculations. This is fine if that's what you want, but you may notice it skews the percentages on the report at the end of the week. Anyway, I hope this is a welcome addition to the thread and I hope everyone trading here finds it both insightful and beneficial. Thank you Davit for sharing your system and everyone here for contributing selflessly. Attached File(s) TradeReport_compact - updated Russia.mq4 153 KB | 665 downloads Kind regards, Russia

--- 帖子 #27410 ---
Davit, all you need to know is if the annual report says profit or loss &amp; how much. Then file that as Misc. Income - it's taxed as ordinary income unfortunately, not cap gains. B y default, retail FOREX traders fall under Section 988, which covers short-term foreign exchange contracts like spot FOREX trades. Section 988 taxes FOREX gains and losses like ordinary income, which is at a higher rate than the capital gains tax for most earners. An advantage of Section 988 treatment is that any amount of ordinary income can be deducted as a loss, where only $3,000 in capital gains losses can be deducted. Section 988 gains or losses are reported on Form 6781.

--- 帖子 #27411 ---
Davit, Oanda does not provide tax documents since they do not withhold taxes. So you have to look at the annual account statement for each of your accounts and report the profit for the year. I use Turbotax to prepare my taxes. I entered my Forex profit in Turbotax as follows: "Wages &amp; Income" → "Less Common Income" → "Miscellaneous Income" → "Other Reportable Income". Here I created an account name and just entered the bottom line profit for the year.

I used turbotax to report gains from forex.. There is a section where you can report 1256 straight pnl. Doesn't matter if your broker gives you form, your broker statements are enough proof. So you tally all of that and report it. 1256 is better for reporting gains because you have the 60/40 split the 988 is more for losses. If you ahvel losses you can claim all of it as ordinary income loss which gives you some tax break. this is from 2017 when i made my move to futures.. Attached Image

--- 帖子 #27446 ---
On the subject of income taxes, I'm a US citizen and I plan to open a Roth IRA. I can close out an account I have with a forex broker &amp; open the account with a custodial firm and once that account has been opened, I can roll the funds to an FX account with Oanda . I can contribute up to $6,500 USD for tax-year 2018 ($5,500 USD if you're under 55 y.o.) if I open the account &amp; deposit the money in the account by April 15th of this year. Davit you might want to consider that. Plus you can make a contribution for tax year 2019 as well. Money deposited in a Roth IRA is after-tax money so you don't get a tax deduction for it, however, you can withdraw it &amp; not have to pay federal income tax on the money you withdraw. You have to be 59 1/2 y.o. to withdraw the money without penalties. If you're thinking about having a source of money for retirement that you can withdraw without having to pay taxes on it, this might be something you could consider. I'm not a financial adviser. You need to do your due-diligence prior to setting up the account.

--- 帖子 #27455 ---
if you do not like strong emotions and do not have the very tough nerves, you should avoid GBP unless you have high probability of gain.. I prefer pairs associated with commodities, which are quieter. A good daily analysis, is always to see the DXI. dollar goes up, commodities go down. dollar falls commodities rises. why ? as you know, it is because there are Inverse Relationship Between USD and Commodity Prices. The US dollar is the benchmark pricing mechanism for most commodities, particularly oil. It is also the exchange mechanism in most international trade contracts for raw materials. When the value of the USD declines, it becomes expensive to buy commodities. Traders should keep a close eye on the price quotes of the dollar index, to study the USD and its correlation with commodity prices EVERY SINGLE DAY .

Some motivation The Power of Imperfect Starts by James Clear When you have a goal — whether it’s starting a business or eating healthier or traveling the world — it’s easy to look at someone who is already doing it and then try to reverse engineer their strategy. In some cases, this is really useful. Learning from the experiences of successful people is a great way to accelerate your own learning curve. But it’s equally important to remember that the systems, habits, and strategies that successful people are using today are probably not the same ones they were using when they began their journey. What is optimal for them right now isn’t necessarily needed for you to get started. There is a difference between the two. Let me explain. What is Optimal vs. What is Needed If you set your bar at “amazing,” it’s awfully difficult to start. —Seth Godin Learning from others is great and I do it all the time myself. But comparing your current situation to someone who is already successful can often make you feel like you lack the required resources to get started at all. If you look at their optimal setup, it can be really easy to convince yourself that you need to buy new things or learn new skills or meet new people before you can even take the first step toward your goals. And usually, that’s not true. Here are some examples. Traveling the world. Every time I travel, I see so many backpackers who have spent a fortune on gear: rainproof bags, moisture-wicking clothes, special shoes. Now I’m not saying gear is useless. Great gear can make your life much easier on the road, but it’s not required. You don’t need new shoes to start running. You don’t need new cooking bowls to start eating healthy . And you don’t need a new backpack to start traveling. Those things might be optimal, but they are not needed in the beginning. Starting a business. When you’re an entrepreneur, it’s so easy to get obsessed with optimal. This is especially true at the start. I can remember being convinced that my first website would not succeed without a great logo. After all, every popular website I looked at had a professional logo. I've since learned my lesson. Now my “logo” is just my name and this is the most popular website I’ve built. Eating healthy. Maybe the optimal diet would involve buying beef that is only grass-fed or vegetables that are only organic or some other super-healthy food strategy. But if you’re just trying to make strides in the right direction, why get bogged down in the details? Start small and simply buy another vegetable this week — whether it’s organic or not. There will be plenty of time for optimization later. Avoiding by Optimizing Claiming that you need to “learn more” or “get all of your ducks in a row” can often be a crutch that prevents you from moving forward on the stuff that actually matters. You can complain that your golf game is suffering because you need new clubs, but the truth is you probably just need two years of practice. You can argue that it’s hard to travel light without the right backpack, but the truth is you could make it work with what you have now. You can point out how your business mentor is successful because they use XYZ software, but they probably got started without it. Obsessing about the ultimate strategy or the ultimate diet or the ultimate golf club can be a clever way to prevent yourself from doing hard work. As regular readers know, I’m all for optimizing and improvement. One percent gains fill me with joy. Small habits leave me smitten. Disturbing levels of consistency make my heart flutter. But don’t let visions of what is optimal prevent you from getting started in the first place. An imperfect start can always be improved, but obsessing over a perfect plan will never take you anywhere on its own.

Why the plunge? Extremely dovish statement basically saying future rate will most likely be cut down.This takes the NZD wings out. "The Official Cash Rate (OCR) remains at 1.75 percent. Given the weaker global economic outlook and reduced momentum in domestic spending, the more likely direction of our next OCR move is down. Employment is near its maximum sustainable level. However, core consumer price inflation remains below our 2 percent target mid-point, necessitating continued supportive monetary policy. The global economic outlook has continued to weaken, in particular amongst some of our key trading partners including Australia, Europe, and China. This weaker outlook has prompted central banks to ease their expected monetary policy stances, placing upward pressure on the New Zealand dollar. Domestic growth slowed in 2018, with softness in the housing market and weak business investment contributing. We expect ongoing low interest rates, and increased government spending and investment, to support economic growth over 2019. Low interest rates, and continued employment growth, should support household spending and business investment. Government spending on infrastructure, housing, and transfer payments also supports domestic demand. As capacity pressures build, consumer price inflation is expected to rise to around the mid-point of our target range at 2 percent. The balance of risks to this outlook has shifted to the downside. The risk of a more pronounced global downturn has increased and low business sentiment continues to weigh on domestic spending. On the upside, inflation could rise faster if firms pass on cost increases to prices to a greater extent. We will keep the OCR at an expansionary level for a considerable period to contribute to maximising sustainable employment, and maintaining low and stable inflation.

--- 帖子 #27919 ---
It comes down to sheer volume of orders placed and the speed your broker can execute them at...if there's a massive amount of orders and your broker isn't that great, then slippage may occur whereby they execute your order at a different price to what you placed because they're struggling with the demand. It's pretty normal really especially for us common retail folks who get shoved at the back of the queue... Still, some brokers are better than other's it'd be good to make sure you're with a decent provider. Cheers, Ben

The spring is here, which means we want to take all of it! To get an extra hour of light several areas adjust clocks forward one hour according to daylight saving time (DST). Here is a plan for the changes. Starting from March 10, 2019 (02:00 MT Time) , WTI, BRN, XAU, XAG, Platinum, Palladium, and American stocks will be available for trading 1 hour earlier due to Daylight Saving Time coming into effect in the USA. Also, please note that the market will be closed 1 hour earlier (at 23:00 MT Time) on Fridays starting from March 15 up to March 29. On March 31 , Daylight Saving Time will come into effect in Europe. At 02:00 (MT Time), MT4, MT5, and FBS Trader platform clock will also be turned 1 hour ahead . The trading schedule for WTI, BRN, XAU, XAG, Platinum, Palladium, and American stocks will be back on track with MetaTrader time starting from March 31. If you are anyhow confused by the information, do not hesitate to contact our 24/7 customer support team. Though DST causes a lost hour of sleep it also lets you start trading earlier with a fresh mind and big hopes. Consider the DST changes when planning your trading sessions! Copied

--- 帖子 #27998 ---
Hi Halfcents, You will never win even when you launch a complaint. And this is a lesson learned for you... I believe I mentioned here that it's not advisable to put limit orders or even stop orders before red news comes out coz it's normal once red news has been released, liquidity and spreads will go wild. Your order is in queue and since there's a massive widening of spreads, you will not get the order price you wished for. I know this, coz I tried this approach a lot of times before also on CAD pairs. Before even on GBP.. I sticked with CAD pairs, coz there are more times that it will just go one direction on red news.. So, it's very easy to set two pending orders(one buy and one sell) so whichever order gets triggered that will be the winner, but it's not as easy as that coz of spread issues. Which exactly what happened to you...

Closing my EU trade now. Price in the strong zone S38, S61. Looking left the area is a strong support too. PA + pivots. After 2 years of studying and practicing this strategy I have began to develop my own personal style to this method. I used stop orders instead of limit orders. This way I will have to wait for price to get in the zone and wait for reactions before putting the orders. If price starts moving in the right direction only then the orders will get filled compare to limit orders that get filled while price is moving in the opposite direction. This requires more patience and I'm much comfortable doing it this way. For this EU trade I only started putting in the buy stop order in the highlighted area where I saw price was already reacting. Come Friday or next Monday I may start putting in sell stop orders for UJ as it's already in the strong area but most importantly I'll wait for the NFP and unemployment data release so I can make a much better trade decision. In US the Forex traders can file their taxes under Section 1256 instead of Section 988. That allows them to use the 60/40 rule and lowers down the taxes when one has gains. --- 帖子 #28225 ---
Five fundamental truths: 1. Anything can happen. 2. You don’t need to know what is going to happen next in order to make money. 3. There is a random distribution between wins and losses for any given set of variables that define an edge. 4. An edge is nothing more than an indication of a higher probability of one thing happening over another. 5. Every moment in the market is unique. – Mark Douglas in term of item 2. We dont need to know what is going to happen, When I want to have better psychological control, I try to understand what's going on. The good side is that we know something abnormal is happening. This is the result of our growth. " China and the US may announce a meeting for Xi and Trump to meet and sign a new agreement. In fact, if an announcement is not made today, the disappointment may way on the capital markets " credit to author, not for me. We have a chance to make more money tomorrow with NFP.

--- 帖子 #28226 ---
In your example, the 30K loss counts against the 50K gain, so you only pay tax on the 20K net profit. If it was the other way around, 30K gain and 50K loss, then your profit would be 0 so you pay no tax. The remaining -20K cannot be fully written off this year, you can only write off -3K. The remaining -17K gets carried over to next year. The 3K limit is only for losses that cannot be offset by gains.

--- 帖子 #26906 ---
Really nice feature to add floating DD%. I have tested it for a few weeks, works well. There is just this one case when one should be mindful: When you have overnight positions and close them today then the DD% = 0. This is because the period for the report is selected to be "Today" instead of the open of the trades to the close. This is more a limitation to this indicator rather than a bug. Another useful feature is to add column "Win ratio" (Win%) - winning positions vs losing position expressed in percentage, in the same manner as the other features: to show data for each instrument (currency, indecies, etc.), be able to choose visibility (true/false).

Importance of Daily Open and Market Open Hours (London, New York) Price Action - Pivot Levels (Zones) - Events ( PDF File below) Refer: Post 27,124 March 14 12.53pm and Davit’s Post 27,039 March 13. Following many PM’s this Post may further clarify and add strength to the importance of the Daily, London and New York Open Hours. Do some “homework” and observe how they offer Support and Resistance and especially with reversals where they lie between Pivot Levels. Apparently, many traders may not have the correct settings for these Opening Hours? The International Standard for the FX Trading Day Open is 5pm EDT. Check your Broker, Market Watch Hours. Market Watch should show 0.00 for 5pm EDT. 1. Use Daily_Open Line Indicator. 2. Check Using: i. Daily Open (Candle O HLC) on Daily Chart ii. Compare Candle ( O HLC) on H1 that this agrees iii. To Confirm: a) Select Properties, check Period separators. b) This should show the start of the Trading Day as 0.00 (5pm EDT). c) Daily_Open Line Indicator should Start Trading Day on the Period Separator Line. 3. Applying the Daily_Open Line Indicator 3-times to a Chart. i. Daily Open Default Setting, Inputs: Time Zone Data is 0. Should agree with 5pm EDT. ii. London Market Open (3pm EDT) is +10 hours = Time Zone Data setting 10 iii. New York Market Open (8am EDT) is + 15 hours = Time Zone Data Setting 15 4. Frankfurt Open - I do not apply to a chart but may be of use. I trade from USA, EDT. 5. There are specific High Probability Trading Strategies for the London Open. Refer to Kathy Lien’s publications and her YouTube Video. 6. London Open Fake Out! Very often a strong feature at the London Open is a “head fake” or Fake Out then, reversal. Look at the accompanying Chart GBPUSD H1 (Image1) – Background changed for better contrast. Use Zoom feature to view detail. 7. Take any FX Chart with the correct settings and confirm the importance of the Daily, London and New York Opening hours. 8. Settings on Standard Davit Template (Colors User Choice): (Image 2) a. Daily Open : Solid Line, Color Dodger Blue. b. London Open : Dashed Line, Royal Blue. c. New York Open : Dashed Line, Red. Price Action - Pivot Levels (Zones) - Events Price Action, Pivot Levels (Zones) and Economic Announcements first and foremost. Market Open Hours often act as Support/Resistance levels. These Opening Hours may often act as reversal levels between Weekly Pivot Levels. WATCH .

--- 帖子 #27178 ---
You need to work on this behaviour, otherwise it will make you 'feel' dissatisfied even though you are making a lot of money. It is a form of 'greed'. I deal with this partly by closing the chart as soon as I close all the trades. If I reopen the chart later, at least I have put some time between the closes and the 'regret' and have had the opportunity to reflect on my wins, percentages, whatever reinforces behaviour positively. Any improvement needed is then seen as further reinforcement rather than punishment for closing too early. Any profit is good profit.

--- 帖子 #28694 ---
My approach to calendar events is simple I educate myself what's coming up.Loosely plan scenarios what could happen then watch the market and react to it LIVE. Nobody can predict the outcome or market reaction however you being informed have a better idea and confidence then someone being ignorant. I don't know the future and I don't need to know it to make money.Seems paradoxical but that's pure trading.Every second is unknown. “If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles. If you know yourself but not the enemy (the market) for every victory gained you will also suffer a defeat. If you know neither the enemy nor yourself, you will succumb in every battle.” (Classic loser in trading) Sun Tzu above quote explains my core trading principles.

Talking Points: TueApr 16 04:30 GBP : Average Earnings Index 3m/y UK jobs report Tuesday, 4:30. The UK labor market is still doing quite well, despite Brexit. The unemployment rate stood at 3.9% in January and no change is expected. Wages, which tend to take center stage, are projected to advance from 3.4% to 3.5% in the upcoming report for February. The Claimant Count Change, which disappointed with an increase of 27K, is expected to rise again, this time by 17.3K. 18:45 NZD : CPI q/q The Reserve Bank of New Zealand has taken on a more dovish tone in recent months, with rates markets leaning towards a 25-bps rate cut in June. Forecast 0.1% to 0.3% 22:00 CNY : GDP q/y Chinese GDP: Wednesday, 22:00. China recorded the slowest annual growth in 2018: 6.6%. This may be slow for emerging markets but still shows the might of the Chinese economy. After recording an annualized growth rate of 6.4% in Q4 2018, another slide to 6.3% is projected. Also note industrial output, which is expected to pick up from 5.3% to 5.6% in March. A stronger Chinese economy could send the USD and the JPY lower. WedApr 17 04:30 GBP UK inflation: Wednesday, 4:30. Headline CPI slowed down in the UK, mostly due to falling oil prices. The recent increase in energy prices is projected to push inflation to 2% y/y. Core CPI is also forecast to accelerate to 1.9% from 1.8%. 08:30 CAD : CPI m/m // CAD : Trade Balance a Bloomberg News survey forecasts thatheadline CPI is due in at 1.9% (y/y), a meaningful increase from 1.5%, and the monthly reading is due in at 0.7% (m/m ), as it was in February. With the global trade war taking a bite out of the export sector, Canada’s trade deficit has widened in recent months. The trade deficit in January was $4.2 billion, higher than the estimate of $3.5 billion . Domestic developments have been limited however BoC rate expectations are firming and markets have almost fully priced out any risk of easing for July. 21:30 AUD : Employment Change // AUD Unemployment Rate Australian jobs report: Thursday, 21:30. Australia had a slower increase in positions in February: only 4.6K . However, the labor market looks robust as the unemployment rate fell below 5% to 4.9% , an encouraging development. Employment is expected to increase by 15.2K in March, but the jobless rate carries expectations for a rise back to 5%. ThuApr 18 03:15 EUR : French /Germany PMI / 03:30 EUR Euro-zone PMIs: Thursday, 3:15 for France, 3:30 for Germany, and 4:00 for the whole euro-zone. Markit’s forward-looking indices have been flashing red in recent months, with manufacturing PMIs falling to contraction territory, below 50 points. The most devastating drop was in Germany, with a score of 44.1 points in March . However, the services sector is doing OK. The focus remains on the German Manufacturing PMI which is expected to recover to 45.2 points . 04:30 GBP: Retail Sales m/m UK retail sales: Thursday, 4:30. UK consumers surprised economists in February with an increase of 0.4% in purchases. This time, a slide of 0.3% is on the cards. The data are volatile but an ongoing decline may be associated to Brexit. 08:30 CAD : Core Retail Sales m/m Domestic developments have been limited however BoC rate expectations are firming and markets have almost fully priced out any risk of easing for July. Core Retail sales posted a weak gain of 0.1% in January , after two straight declines. Retail sales have not fared as well, recording three successive declines. Will we see an improvement in February? USD : Core Retail Sales m/m // USD : Retail Sales m/m US retail sales: Thursday, 8:30. After a downfall in December and a surge in January, retail sales returned to normal moves in February, albeit with drops: 0.2% on the headline and 0.4% in core sales. Both figures are projected to increase now: 0.7% on the headline and 0.7% in core sales.

More dovish than expected minutes could be taken as negative/bearish for the AUD, while more hawkish than expected minutes could be taken as positive/bullish for the AUD. --- 帖子 #28820 ---
The market is in a peculiar place. We went from synchronised expansion to a longer and more protracted softening than was forecast. This made central banks take their foot off the breaks and move into wait and see mode. Without central bank influences the market has to look at the incoming data for direction. Mixed data can cause unexpected moves and anyone trading positions that are open for several sessions should be aware that they are more exposed than normal. Canada currently has issues with trade and tariffs, issues with China, problems with new nafta, and mixed to deteriorating economic data. Fundamentaly there is no real trend here. Adapt of die as they say and you should expect your position trades to give you some grey hair in this env so be prepared or alter your trade management to be slightly tighter. Holding a position over several sessions with no real direction amidst mixed data might not be the best strategy at the moment. Be aware and be prepared.

--- 帖子 #28833 ---
Hoping and praying are wholly inappropriate behaviours in trading. They go directly against Mark Douglas' principles of randomness, probability and not knowing (and not caring) what happens next. Hoping and praying (and gambling) are behaviours that are reinforced on a Variable Ratio Schedule. SOMETIMES they work but MOST of the time they don't. Because they SOMETIMES work people keep doing it regardless. (Stretched) Variable Ratio Schedules are the most addictive schedules and lead to high frequency behaviours, particularly in gambling (think slotmachines). Casinos use these schedules to hook people so that in the end they lose ALL their money.

Closed AU from last weeks spike. Running AJ from yesterday as below. These are classic pivot set ups. I threw a fib extension on AJ just to demonstrate the simplicity of the method..when applied and traded properly. AJ Weekly pivot is on the 38.2% fib retracement from last weeks high and extension beyond R100. Not rocket science. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Also strip back your charts , use the template provided, observe price action around these key 61-100 zones and never forget it is a game of probabilities . No-one knows what the next trade will do and frankly you shouldn't care. One trade should not be positioned to wipe out or create massive draw down in your account. The only time you wet your pants is if you're positioned too large to handle. Reduce your trade sizes, trade in these zones with low ADR pairs and observe yourselves doing this over a large sample of trades. Davit's post on trade size where he took 500+ pips versus another members 35 pips...on exactly the same set-up, is the defining example on this thread of how to optimise your set-up. We can all see the same set-ups, but position sizing and risk management will define your edge over a large sample of trades.

I been getting PM's asking to explain mean reversion. Here's a pic showing the basic concept: Attached Image Within the long term cycles is the "shorter term variability." That's essentially what we are trading here. As price swings to either side it may/will return to cycle continuation. That's why it's important to take the trades at the outermost levels and take profit before it comes back to you.

--- 帖子 #29116 ---
LOL I recalled when you were chasing 10 pips here and there on the thread As simple as possible: 00 level trading. I use to envy you as a very successful trader.c Even if you were, now you are a super successful trader. It was really frustrating. Udine need to see this thread to become a trillionaire if he is already a millionaire with making 10 pips daily. Each of us have the potential of becoming Davit, my dream forex trader and mentor. However, we must realise it cannot be achieved overnight. I have lost thousands of hard earn dollars in forex. but this article below by diallist together with this thread and posts by Captain Jack always give me hope of reaching the promised land which is the stage of Unconscious Competence Currently I am in stage 3 - the eureka moment and hope to enter stage 4 and 5 before the end of this year. The 5 Steps to becoming a trader Step One: Unconscious Incompetence. This is the first step you take when starting to look into trading. you know that its a good way of making money because you've heard so many things about it and heard of so many millionaires. Unfortunately, just like when you first desire to drive a car you think it will be easy - after all, how hard can it be? Price either moves up or down - what's the big secret to that then - lets get cracking! Unfortunately, just as when you first take your place in front of a steering wheel you find very quickly that you haven't got the first clue about what you're trying to do. You take lots of trades and lots of risks. When you enter a trade it turns against you so you reverse and it turns again .. and again, and again. You may have initial success, and thats even worse - cos it tells your brain that this really is simple and you start to risk more money. You try to turn around your losses by doubling up every time you trade. Sometimes you'll get away with it but more often than not you will come away scathed and bruised You are totally oblivious to your incompetence at trading. This step can last for a week or two of trading but the market is usually swift and you move onth the next stage. Step Two - Conscious Incompetence Step two is where you realise that there is more work involved in trading and that you might actually have to work a few things out. You consciously realise that you are an incompetent trader - you don't have the skills or the insight to turn a regular profit. You now set about buying systems and e-books galore, read websites based everywhere from USA to the Ukraine. and begin your search for the holy grail. During this time you will be a system nomad - you will flick from method to method day by day and week by week never sticking with one long enough to actually see if it does work. Every time you come upon a new indicator you'll be ecstatic that this is the one that will make all the difference. You will test out automated systems on Metatrader, you'll play with moving averages, Fibonacci lines, support &amp; resistance, Pivots, Fractals, Divergence, DMI, ADX, and a hundred other things all in the vein hope that your 'magic system' starts today. You'll be a top and bottom picker, trying to find the exact point of reversal with your indicators and you'll find yourself chasing losing trades and even adding to them because you are so sure you are right. You'll go into the live chat room and see other traders making pips and you want to know why it's not you - you'll ask a million questions, some of which are so dumb that looking back you feel a bit silly. You'll then reach the point where you think all the ones who are calling pips after pips are liars - they cant be making that amount because you've studied and you don't make that, you know as much as they do and they must be lying. But they're in there day after day and their account just grows whilst yours falls. You will be like a teenager - the traders that make money will freely give you advice but you're stubborn and think that you know best - you take no notice and overtrade your account even though everyone says you are mad to - but you know better. You'll consider following the calls that others make but even then it wont work so you try paying for signals from someone else - they don't work for you either. You might even approach a 'guru' like Rob Booker or someone on a chat board who promises to make you into a trader(usually for a fee of course). Whether the guru is good or not you wont win because there is no replacement for screen time and you still think you know best. This step can last ages and ages - in fact in reality talking with other traders as well as personal experience confirms that it can easily last well over a year and more nearer 3 years. This is also the step when you are most likely to give up through sheer frustration. Around 60% of new traders die out in the first 3 months - they give up and this is good - think about it - if trading was easy we would all be millionaires. another 20% keep going for a year and then in desperation take risks guaranteed to blow their account which of course it does. What may suprise you is that of the remaining 20% all of them will last around 3 years - and they will think they are safe in the water - but even at 3 years only a further 5-10% will continue and go on to actually make money consistently. By the way - they are real figures, not just some ive picked out of my head - so when you get to 3 years in the game dont think its plain sailing from there. Iv had many people argue with me about these timescales - funny enough none of them have been trading for more that 3 years - if you think you know better then ask on a board for someone who's been trading 5 years and ask them how long it takes to become fully 100% proficient. Sure i guess there will be exceptions to the rle - but i havent met any yet. Eventually you do begin to come out of this phase. You've probably committed more time and money than you ever thought you would, lost 2 or 3 loaded accounts and all but given up maybe 3 or 4 times but now its in your blood One day - im a split second moment you will enter stage 3. Step 3 - The Eureka Moment Towards the end of stage two you begin to realise that it's not the system that is making the difference. You realise that its actually possible to make money with a simple moving average and nothing else IF you can get your head and money management right You start to read books on the psychology of trading and identify with the characters portrayed in those books and finally comes the eureka moment. The eureka moment causes a new connection to be made in your brain. You suddenly realise that neither you, nor anyone else can accurately predict what the market will do in the next ten seconds, never mind the next 20 mins. Because of this revelation you stop taking any notice of what anyone thinks - what this news item will do, and what that event will do to the markets. You become an individual with your own method of trading You start to work just one system that you mould to your own way of trading, you're starting to get happy and you define your risk threshold. You start to take every trade that your 'edge' shows has a good probability of winning with. When the trade turns bad you don't get angry or even because you know in your head that as you couldn't possibly predict it it isn't your fault - as soon as you realise that the trade is bad you close it . The next trade or the one after it or the one after that will have higher odds of success because you know your system works. You stop looking at trading results from a trade-to-trade perspective and start to look at weekly figures knowing that one bad trade does not a poor system make. You have realised in an instant that the trading game is about one thing - consistency of your 'edge' and your discipline to take all the trades no matter what as you know the probabilities stack in your favour. You learn about proper money management and leverage - risk of account etc etc - and this time it actually soaks in and you think back to those who advised the same thing a year ago with a smile. You weren't ready then, but you are now. The eureka moment came the moment that you truly accepted that you cannot predict the market. Step 4 - Conscious Competence You are making trades whenever your system tells you to. You take losses just as easily as you take wins You now let your winners run to their conclusion fully accepting the risk and knowing that your system makes more money than it looses and when you're on a loser you close it swiftly with little pain to your account You are now at a point where you break even most of the time - day in day out, you will have weeks where you make 100 pips and weeks where you lose 100 pips - generally you are breaking even and not losing money. You are now conscious of the fact that you are making calls that are generally good and you are getting respect from other traders as you chat the day away. You still have to work at it and think about your trades but as this continues you begin to make more money than you lose consistently. You'll start the day on a 20 pip win, take a 35 pip loss and have no feelings that you've given those pips back because you know that it will come back again. You will now begin to make consistent pips week in and week out 25 pips one week, 50 the next and so on. This lasts about 6 months "Step Five - Unconscious Competence Now we’re cooking - just like driving a car, every day you get in your seat and trade - you do everything now on an unconscious level. You are running on autopilot. You start to pick the really big trades and getting 200 pips in a day doesnt make you any more excited that getting 1 pips. You see the newbies in the forum shouting 'go dollar go' as if they are urging on a horse to win in the grand national and you see yourself - but many years ago now. This is trading utopia - you have mastered your emotions and you are now a trader with a rapidly growing account. You're a star in the trading chat room and people listen to what you say. You recognise yourself in their questions from about two years ago. You pass on your advice but you know most of it is futile because they're teenagers - some of them will get to where you are - some will do it fast and others will be slower - literally dozens and dozens will never get past stage two, but a few will. Trading is no longer exciting - in fact it's probably boring you to bits - like everything in life when you get good at it or do it for your job - it gets boring - you're doing your job and that's that. Finally you grow out of the chat rooms and find a few choice people who you converse with about the markets without being influenced at all. All the time you are honing your methods to extract the maximum profit from the market without increasing risk. Your method of trading doesnt change - it just gets better - you now have what women call 'intuition' You can now say with your head held high "I'm a currency trader" but to be honest you dont even bother telling anyone - it's a job like any other. I hope youve enjoyed reading this journey into a traders mind and that hopefully youve identified with some points in here. Remember that only 5% will actually make it - but the reason for that isnt ability, its staying power and the ability to change your perceptions and paradigms as new information comes available. The losers are those who wanted to 'get rich quick' but approached the market and within 6 months put on a pair of blinkers so they couldnt see the obvious - a kind of "this is the way i see it and thats that" scenario - refusing to assimilate new information that changes that perception. Im happy to tell you that the reason i started trading was because of the 'get rich quick' mindset. Just that now i see it as 'get rich slow' If youre thinking about giving up i have one piece of advice for you .... Ask yourself the question "how many years would you go to college if you knew for a fact that there was a million dollars a year job at the end of it? Take care and good trading to you all. my considerations about next week events - Under construction Tue Apr 23 Tue Apr 23 21:30 AUD CPI q/q (RED =&lt; 0.2% // green &gt; 0.3) 0.2% 0.5% AUD Trimmed Mean CPI q/q 0.4% 0.4% Australian inflation data : Tuesday, 21:30. The land down under releases inflation data only once per quarter, making every publication more meaningful. Wednesday AUD – Consumer Price Index Q/Q Consumer prices account for a majority of overall inflation. Inflation is important to currency valuation because rising prices lead the central bank to raise interest rates out of respect for their inflation containment mandate. Previous was 0.5% and forecast is 0.2% (Bearish) AUD – Trimmed Consumer Price Index Q/Q Previous was 0.4 and forecast is 0.4 so with that being said AUD looks to have bearish movements across the pairs. Hold E/A longs and look for opportunity on other Aussie pairs. CAD – BOC Monetary Policy Report It provides valuable insight into the bank's view of economic conditions and inflation - the key factors that will shape the future of monetary policy and influence their interest rate decisions . CAD – BOC Rate Statement It's the primary tool the BOC uses to communicate with investors about monetary policy. It contains the outcome of their decision on interest rates and commentary about the economic conditions that influenced their decision. Most importantly, it discusses the economic outlook and offers clues on the outcome of future decisions. CAD – Overnight Rate 1.75% Short term interest rates are the paramount factor in currency valuation - traders look at most other indicators merely to predict how rates will change in the future; Expectation is for interest rates to stay the same at 1.75%. Poloz is concerned off an overall slowdown. There’s new evidence that trade policy is weighing on Canadian business confidence. The BoC’s latest quarterly Business Outlook Survey , one of Poloz’s favourite indicators, is notably downbeat. Expectations for sales over the next 12 months are positive, but “have softened,” . That being said trade CAD with caution and protect U/C shorts. CAD has external factors of Oil prices that heavily affect the currency prices. Thursday JPY –Outlook Report / Monetary Policy / BOJ Press Conference It provides valuable insight into the bank's view of economic conditions and inflation - the key factors that will shape the future of monetary policy; Will watch this closely and protect U/J trades if still holding USD - Core Durable Goods Orders m/m It's a leading indicator of production - rising purchase orders signal that manufacturers will increase activity as they work to fill the orders. Previous was -0.1% and forecast is for +0.2% so keep in mind the dollar will gain bullish movements across the board so any pairs where shorting dollar has to be protected or closed . Friday USD - Advanced Gross Domestic Product Q/Q It's the broadest measure of economic activity and the primary gauge of the economy's health; Forecast is 2.2 which is no change from last quarter however these forecast more time than not inaccurate so keep in mind. --- 帖子 #26354 ---
Drawdown is part of any business. Even big businesses experienced "down" times where they don't make profit or in the losing end for the first years of its inception. But those who are courageous enough persevere because they believe in their idea, they don't enter the business randomly, they study beforehand. They push for it really hard because they have a vision that someday it will be a reality. And needless to say, those businesses became successful eventually. Nothing's easy. But if we want to succeed badly, we persevere and recognize that early failure is just part of winning as long as we learn from it and use it to make us better. We don't feel sorry for our failures. Serious drawdowns can be a result of many things - entering early, not understanding price action, unaware of upcoming events, etc. But instead of feeling sorry for ourselves, let's analyze objectively why we ended up with that huge drawdown. So that in our future trades, we are better equipped, don't make the same mistakes, make better decisions when entering trades and increase our chances for a profitable trade.

--- 帖子 #26368 ---
I think there is a massive difference between 'averaging-DOWN' vs 'averaging-IN.' Averaging-IN, is entering the trade, with a plan to get to or close to a certain size, with a predefined max loss you are willing to take. I.e., should your active trade get close to that max loss, you exit the trade. Averaging-DOWN, is entering a trade, that happens to be going against you, and you are likely already over the size of trade you initially planned to take, and are just adding hoping to not have to book a loss at some point. Some people would say this is semantics, but I think there is a HUGE difference between those two mindsets.

Low liquidity, especially during Asian hours, can create extreme flash crashes. Recent examples of these include: 3rd January 2019 - JPY crosses +10% 7th October 2016 – GBP crosses -10% What does this mean? There will definitely be low liquidity during Asian market hours . This will mean really slow markets and wider spreads during Asian hours with the potential for extremely fast-moving markets and extreme price moves. What should you do? Plan for worst case scenarios! IC Markets urges all its clients to take precautionary measures before the holidays. Hi Cryptosurf. For clarification.... The 24 hour trading day/cycle ENDS at 5PM New York time. MT4 will show the start time for the last Hourly candle before New York close as 23:00. The NEW 24 hour trading day begins 1 millisecond after New York close. The start time for that first candle of the cycle will be 00:00. The blue Daily Open marked on Trendzy's chart adjacent to the S100 is correctly identifying the Daily Open price level. I hope that helps. Cheers

Wild week with some big moves and potentially more to come today with USD advance GDP as the key economic release. Been limited with trades this week, but wanted to show one of the additional tools in the pivots arsenal that I often make use of - using prior weekly 'missed pivots' as a guide for potential areas of price action to tend towards. It's not for everyone - just an illustration of how it helps me to plan my trades. I've used EJ as an example. Big upside moves over the past 3-4 weeks, left a missed weekly pivot for EJ in early April. Last week saw some consolidation and rejection of the 126.75 level and I went short with a couple of trades that worked out well. This week however has seen significant downward momentum with a lot of Yen strength, but it also meant that missed pivot from early April came into play and it was eventually taken out at 124.30 (around the S138-S161 area) and with a nice 4hr pin bar, i've taken a small long to see if price bounces back to around S100 or beyond. Now I have no idea where price will go. It could retrace and test further lows for the week - or it could bounce, given the significant extended down move. I'm basically playing with probability, having seen this set-up work for me previously. If it doesn't - no big deal, as will just move onto the next set-up. --- 帖子 #29543 ---
Trading pivot levels is same as trading extremes of any oscillator or price moving away from MA. When oscillator is at extremes, there are chances of it coming back to mid level(50 or 0 depends on osc) at some point. When price is away from MA, there are chances of it coming back to MA at some point. When price is at extremes pivot levels, there are chance of it coming back to pivot. there are times price catches up the indicator. there are other times, indicator catches up the price. Example, when price is moving away from say 100MA, it will eventually retraces back to 100MA, may be a sharp retrace(price catches up MA), maybe a wavy retrace(where MA and price both work together to catchup), may be a horizontal move(where MA catches up the price). Weekly Pivot Indicator repaints every week and people have to realize either price will catch up the levels or the Pivots will catch up the price. As side note, trading 20 lots, getting 20 pips with that will get you $4000 a week also. Those 10000+pips with 1000+trades and 50+lots wont impress me. Example, trading 50 lots, making 10000 a month is just making 20 pips a month. I am not sure how many lots are opened at the same time in one's account.... Assuming 10% of 50 lots would be opened at the same time, means, 5 lots times 200 pips a month will also get you $10000; which is just 10 pips per trading day; I know many many people are doing this, personally. only thing I notice in that pivot trading approach is, taking small lots....but they load up quickly which is very similar to trading big lots. may be another martingale with just pivot levels...if price beats this pivot level, take another 10 trades at the next level when price gets there, hoping for a retrace to main pivot.

The concept of the crime, which later evolved into the idea of genocide, was based on the Armenian Genocide Definition of genocide .. any of the following acts committed with intent to destroy , in whole or in part , a national, ethnical, racial or religious group, as such: (a) Killing members of the group; (b) Causing serious bodily or mental harm to members of the group; (c) Deliberately inflicting on the group conditions of life calculated to bring about its physical destruction in whole or in part; (d) Imposing measures intended to prevent births within the group; (e) Forcibly transferring children of the group to another group. — Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide, Article 2 [4] Turkish state still denies the Armenian Genocide and funds universities across developed countries for revisionism.This fight for recognition of Genocide by Turkey is not just about Armenians its about humanity! It's perfectly natural to have drawdowns trading this system. It comes with the beast. In fact, it is necessary at times, due to the seemingly random gyrations of the market. It's ok to have drawdowns as long as you feel confident your understanding of the fundamentals at the moment. --- 帖子 #30012 ---
No GBP hasnt become a safe haven. The large pensions funds are not allowed to carry FX exposures on their cross currency investments. Due to the change in the FX value versus their foreign investments at month end they are forced to balance their books to correct this exposure. This is why GBP has been bought. This is what book balancing is all about.

--- 帖子 #28520 ---
The institutions use models to value instruments so they know when they are trading at a discount (the can buy it for cheap and sell it later for a profit) or at a premium (ie can sell something expensive and buy it back later cheaper for a profit). Institutions will only deal when they have value. Those are just two lines that they will use in their models. Here is a chart of GBPUSD with three value lines. You would look to trade it when there is a divergence between value and price. First is a short where you have divergence on three value lines. Second is a long where you only have two so less probability. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Anyway I dont want to derail this thread anymore
