--- 帖子 #28533 ---
FX works just like any other auction market. When your broker (if they are a market maker) accepts your trade they are taking the otherside of that position. MMs will widen the spread or withdraw their liquidity only if and when they detect large institutional buying or selling pressure as they do not want to be on the otherside of that trade. MM make their money by facilitating large volumes of transactions. They do not care if the market goes up or down. MMs love it when the market trades in a small range. They can just rotate price back and forth and make a fortune. When they detect order flow toxicity ( term used by MMs when they detect one side of the orderbook becoming imbalanced) they will pull their liquidity to avoid being on the wrong side of the market move and only apply their minimum required liquidity in the market. Imagine you are the MM and in a room full of people helping them transact. Some guy wants to buy 50 and another wants to sell 30 so you fill the rest of that buy order and you make the spread as your profit and this happens back and forth over and over price ticks up and then down. Now all of a sudden some guy wants to buy 5000. What would you do? Would you fill that order at the current price? No you dont want to be on the otherside of a loosing trade so you tell that buyer ok Ill buy your 5000 but you give them a terrible price. You quote them a much much higher price. You have widened the spread or withdrawn your liquidity. This is what happens when you see fast moves away from balance areas. This is the market makers model and how their business works. They do not care about your 3 lot stop loss. Here is an interview with a MM goes into an explanation of their business, that they have no directional bias, how they are concerned about volatility how they protect themselves through the options markets, dont care about your stop losses etc etc. Inserted Video

--- 帖子 #28538 ---
For sure stop loss hunting happens but its not your broker or the market maker that does it. As you say its rather done by the large directional players in the market. However its usually done to get off their position and not done during an accumulation. Below is a diagram of what a usual market accumulation pattern looks like. The value line (purple starts to go up) so the institutions will want to get long and so will create a pattern of lower lows and lower highs creating the illusion that the market is in a downward trend to encourage sellers into the market. They will then start to accumulate all that selling at a pace so as not to stop the downward move. They will also cap any move back to the upside ( red boxes) until they have accumulated enough size on their books. Once the detect that selling has started to drop off and no more sellers are coming out to play they will then start the mark up phase. Price moves back into value and starts to pull back. When the market maker detects that buying is now coming in above the 50% pullback level they take this as a warning from the institutions that they want to mark up prices and they pull their liquidity. This is when you get the fast moves away from the balance area. For them the biggest issue now is how to get off their large buy position. The juxtaposition is that they need to find BUYERS at higher prices. How do they get people to buy something that is more expensive. Well they have created the perfect setup for it. All those sellers have their stops above the market at the red lines. The institutions term this 'Paycheck' for when they mark up the price through those levels they trigger those stops and those sellers have to become buyers to get off their positions. The institutions have now found their buyers at higher prices and will start getting off their trade in the green box. The move up is not fuelled by new buyers but rather by the old sellers forced to become buyers. This is the one advantage retail traders have over the institutions. We can deal anywhere on the chart whereas the institutions cannot due to the size of their positions. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Here is a good example on CL contract Orange line is value... Each time price trades below a pivot (blue lines) the liquidity is bought. Look at all the paycheck levels above the market. Once the MM detects buying above the 50 line they pull their liquidity. You can see it by the long bars, fast money move away from the balance area. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #30489 ---
This is not surprising, because weekly pivots are based on the high, low and close of the previous week. The high and low can vary a bit from br0ker to br0ker due to spread, but it is the close that can vary markedly because not all br0kers close off the week at the same time, some stop price action five minutes before NY close, others two minutes. Combine this with huge differences in closing spread and you end up with 'widely' varying pivots. This is why we trade pivot zones rather than defined pivot levels.

Hi ikdenk. Just a quick note... Candles only reflect the BID price.The spreads will not have any effect on the pivots, as the the Open, High, Low and Close.....are all BID prices. Spreads will only affect the ASK price levels.....which aren't reflected in the candles so will not be taken into account when the pivots are calculated. I hope that helps. Cheers.

Below sounds bullish" " Growth in employment in the March quarter had been strong, following similar outcomes over much of 2018. Most of the growth in employment since mid 2018 had been in full-time employment. The unemployment rate had remained around 5 per cent in March. Members observed that conditions in the labour market had signalled a significantly stronger pace of economic activity since mid 2018 than indicated by the GDP data. Leading indicators of labour demand had eased over recent months and provided a mixed picture of the near-term outlook. As a result, employment growth was expected to be similar to the growth rate of the working-age population in the near term. The unemployment rate was expected to remain around 5 per cent through most of the forecast period, before declining to around 4¾ per cent in 2021. Members noted that the forecasts for the labour market suggested that there would be some spare capacity in the labour market throughout the forecast period, although there was uncertainty about how quickly the spare capacity would decline and how progress would feed into wage pressures. The central forecast was for wages growth to pick up gradually. In combination, the forecasts for wages growth and consumer price inflation implied that real consumer wage growth would be low but positive over the forecast period. This is the part kind of confusing and very dovish.Note they dont say its their view its "Financial market participants" view Financial market participants' expectations of cash rate cuts were brought further forward following the release of the March quarter CPI. --- 帖子 #30633 ---
Thanks for the indicator, can be useful on some charts for overview. For actual trading decisions I prefer individual charts for each pair. I just label the chart with SELL or BUY for the preferred direction, mainly based on the size of the swap. I will buy and sell if the swap is only slightly negative in both directions, like audnzd. I try to avoid trading against large negative swap, like buying euraud or selling usdjpy for example. The swap is based on the interest rates of the individual currencies and the fundamental direction in the long term would be trading with positive swap. This also helps to reduce the drawdown if you are 'forced' to hold onto trades longer than anticipated.

--- 帖子 #30854 ---
As this comment is slightly outside Davit rules i will wait he give me permission for explain it. I only will make a small observation Im some time thinking how deal with strong trends. As people knows PV swing levels works great in range but in strong trends you can suffer over extended levels ( above 100 ). Even watching PA is hard know when a retracement is real swing in this kind of moments. After some analysis i saw if you use ADR week for make current PV levels, that levels are closer to movements. This happens because if you are in a strong trend this levels are wider. But trend movements are temporal in overall then these levels alterations not show real areas. Using new approach you have constant levels ( small variation ). I set a few rules for cover all possibilities. I will wait Davit decide if is interesting. Personally i see this approach give more entry precision and more mechanical behavior...

--- 帖子 #30864 ---
My goal is keep Davit original rule about to be simpler possible. Then I only use 3 levels. As we are working with ATR, I divide levels in equal size 50% - It have a role when week start. As we don't know if price will be in range, area between 50% levels make a full ATR range. If week start don0t have big gap normally will start near PP and if is in range it will be move around PP and 50% levels 100% - This level is touched in strong trends. Normally movement start in PP 150% - Overextended level PP - I use 2. It have a reason. PP blue is original pivots PP. Orange PP is based in ATR levels and its shifted. Using both I fit price at open price better and I create a small range area inside for have better vision about movements near PP. This area is very tricky using original pivots. This approach helps to enter in right direction Next post I will show entries... PD: I let template and tools. No expiration

--- 帖子 #30868 ---
I forgot a thing about levels. Even looks different to original, really is same base. This approach only packed original swing levels in 2 groups. 1) 38/61 as 50% ( many times 38% is swing after long movement even this is not original Davit rule ) 2) 78/100 as 100% As levels are made with averaged ADR ( ATR ), swing levels tends to be closer to real movements. Some pairs with many days below ADR can have swings slightly shifted ( around 80/90% of ATR ). That means swings will happens around levels 40/90 ( not 50/100 ). As usual PA rejections are main signal

--- 帖子 #30919 ---
I would like give a tip for people will want check new idea this weekend. Its complicate that price swings every time touching current levels. But as many people knows price "have memory". As normal pivots, previous weeks can have some levels are tested in current week. With this approach we use last 4 weeks. Then when we have a swing between 2 levels we have check if previous week/s had a level in that area ( or very closer ). If happens take that swing as real because this approach only have 3 strong levels ( 50,100,150 ), then swings normally are not fake

--- 帖子 #30976 ---
I like Harmonics as an extra confirmation. I like to look at the Harmonics T1 and T2 measured reactions and see how they line up with some pivot points. If we get a Bearish Harmonic pattern completed for example @ R61 and T1 correlates with the WPP and T2 lines up with S38 then I'm going to be looking at those levels as exit zones for my trade. A Harmonic pattern that completes at a WPP doesn't interest me, like Pivot points all they are doing is showing us potentials. They also work really well on small time frames if you are in pivot zones and are experiencing price action. I use them early in the morning to trade indices. In conventional pivots the S&amp;P had a run up in the last week and is above the MR1 so the only thing I was interested in was selling it this morning.

I'm longer term trader than most on here but with position sizing heavily influenced by Davit. I have enough small positions that when in DD like at present on AJ, NJ, CJ (longs) and EN short I use pullbacks to close some positions at open (only the swap as profit) and replace them lower /higher as appropriate (depending on short or long entry) if price goes against me again. I call it climbing the 'rungs' up or down to shuffle my positions closer to an eventual turning point. Currently hoping that G20 meetings will provide some pullbacks (eg some optimism) if not reversals (eg trade deal).

The US economy advanced an annualized 3.1 percent in the first quarter of 2019, slightly below earlier figures of a 3.2 percent expansion and in line with market expectations, the second estimate showed. It follows a 2.2 percent growth in the previous three-month period. Nonresidential fixed investment and private inventory investment were revised lower and while upward revisions were seen exports and personal consumption expenditures. GDP Growth Rate in the United States averaged 3.22 percent from 1947 until 2019, reaching an all time high of 16.70 percent in the first quarter of 1950 and a record low of -10 percent in the first quarter of 1958. Source trading economics

--- 帖子 #31126 ---
I'm trying to implement trade plotter to give you a better idea of some of my trades (see my previous post with query) but for me the psychology of trading is such that one of the worst things that could happen for me after DD and a significant move in my favour is for me to close nothing and have price to go back against me (to original DD or worse). When trading with many small positions I therefore don't care if I close some of them for small profits and miss out on greater profits as it's a lesser evil. eg AJ I've closed off about 29% of my positions on current pullback. Still have plenty to profit if continues in my favour but can reload near the bottom and below current low if price goes that way. In your case I would have staggered closes as price moved in your favour - some would have been worse than the 'current' price on your posted chart, some would have been better.

--- 帖子 #31154 ---
This is final version of formula. Black boxes shows areas previous delay are removed. Trend areas are not affected showing previous uniform signal. Green box shows failed break level. For you have valid signal you need level is crossed and formula signal is same direction ( color ). In that case you have cross level and blue color. its BUY but a few candles later price cross level going down and formula shows red ( sell ). Then its a SL close and a SELL open. If formula change color near level but is not crossed then you dont have valid signal. This happens in orange box. You have sell signal but level is not crossed before go down then its not a rejection and sell signal is not valid This is my rules idea with this pivots. I think is easy trade them. You dont must worry about movements between levels and even you dont need use previous levels

--- 帖子 #31207 ---
ABN AMRO look at the implications for the next Federal Open Market Committee interest rate decision (meeting is on 30-31 July). ABN AMRO set the stage for Friday's data: Markets will be particularly sensitive to incoming data as we approach (the FOMC) The key question for markets remains whether the Fed will cut 25bp or 50bp, rather than whether they will cut at all a 25bp cut is fully priced by OIS forwards a 50bp cut is 2/3 priced The bank expects +175K, which is above consensus (160K), citing the May number was a very weak +75k (the Jan-April average was +195k). … likelihood of some payback for the May weakness OK, for Fed implications: June nonfarm payrolls will therefore attract even more attention than usual A somewhat weak print (120-150k) would not have a significant market impact, but if we were to see another sub-100k reading, markets would likely take it to mean a higher likelihood of a 50bp rate cut, at least as a kneejerk reaction For the Fed, we doubt such a figure would be enough by itself to lead to a 50bp cut, and so we suspect such a market reaction would not last (by the same turn, we doubt a strong print would derail cuts).

Why withdraw it all? Take a small portion enjoy and compound the rest. Here's an interesting tool to put some figures into. Remember as your account grows you can't change the rules on how you play. You have to be prepared to slowly take bigger losses as well as bigger wins. http://www.forex21.com/forex-compounding-calculator/ Its also not just pivot levels plus harmonics they show whats potentially there, quite often its paying attention to the Fundamentals. You could be at S78 on a AUD USD for example and have a Bullish Deep Crab pattern on a H4 time frame if its a RED news event and the RBA cuts prime interest rates by another .25% and the AU falls right through S100 then suddenly the Deep Crab and the S78 meant nothing! You have to pay attention. Technical's alone don't cut it. You need to use a well rounded approach like Davit shows everyone.

--- 帖子 #31252 ---
I put my Robot to work last night. Nice making money while you sleep. There was going to be news on the London session @1:30 am my time. I looked at GU considered the support levels it was at and decided to turn the robot on with a program I had written before I went to bed last night. The trading platform I use has its own proprietary signal system, the developer admitted after being asked for years whats behind it. The system has some Fibonacci based algorithms that spit out the red buy or sell arrows. When things are going up in price the bars are green, down they are red, and neutral they are yellow. So this particular program I had written I asked it to only take a long position on a signal. it had been 200 or so pips down since it gave its last signal in the top left corner. We were at a pivot levels and had harmonic patterns so I figured there was a possibility of getting a trade last night so I turned it on before I went to bed (the green vertical line) 4 bars later at 3am it spit out a signal, and I was in while sleeping like a baby. Being the GBP I don't want to be too heavy in it right now as there is still so much unresolved going on, and red USD news on Thursday. I just took one 10K position and I could have closed the robot and managed it myself today but I let it run its course and do exactly what it was told to do. Close the trade after 9 bars if there was more than 5 pips of profit. The developer of this system is a pilot and has his own high performance plane which is why he nicknamed the robot program autopilot. He cautions traders using this system though, and says you can program an autopilot to fly into the side of a granite mountain and it will do it with absolute precision. The same applies to trading, program it to do something really bad and it will do it for you exactly as instructed. I've done a lot of work with it over the years and I can get it up to around a 60% win rate on pure technicals, so if you take fundamentals into account and activate it at times you see are favorable the win rate can be much higher. I like using it to watch price action if we are at levels that may be a trade and I'm not going to be around. ie: the London session while I'm generally sleeping.

--- 帖子 #31495 ---
I have not posted for awhile but this is the only thread in FF worth contributing to imho! Davit's Weekly pivot trading is the the way to go, but the pivots by themselves are only good if the rest of the story is in place. When you integrate the weekly/daily chart into your trading and the zones created in their history, and you take fundamentals into the picture, suddenly the price action around the pivots lend credibility to your decisions and give you the confidence to take a longer approach to your entries. Eg....8 days ago Aussie rallied into a daily/weekly zone of resistance. The 4 hour touched the R78 and stalled. The 1 hour fluctuated around the R78 for almost a day indicating there was little action to the upside. The fundamentals backed the short entries and the news for the upcoming week gave little in the way of danger to the upside....This turned out to be a very good trade but it took 7 days for it to mature fully... even now Aussie threatens more downside, but for now I am out......but the point is when all the factors are in place short term trades make little sense to me unless you can sit at the computer all day. Attached is my trading page for this currency....

--- 帖子 #31602 ---
EG on a H1 Crab pattern. One thing I want to add about these patterns to anyone following them. A pattern does not constitute a trade, it's merely an extra tool helping show you the potential measured retracement zones and work well in conjunction with Davits pivots because they are both Fibonacci based. You still have to consider what news events are up and coming that may give us the movement we need and make the pattern valid, or make it null and void. A perfect example was the EG I posted earlier this week on a 4HR. GBP data was lousy Euro soared higher pattern negated. Quite often they also on many occasions run up to the stop zone or beyond before reversing so keep that in mind as well. Check the news and watch the price action. Have a great weekend!

I like to know the levels and mark them on my chart even though its not a news event quite often after the expiry especially if it expires close to a level you can see 20 pip or better moves. This is useful to know when a pair is looking good at a particular pivot point levels. Sometimes price will get pushed prior to 7 am to defend the option. https://www.forexlive.com/Orders

The London session and the London NY overlap are predominantly the busiest times in the forex market. The NY cut as its known occurs at 10:00am NYT. All I'm saying as Pivot point traders its good to be aware of these levels, and how it may affect our trade exits or entries. Watch price actions at those times before and after the expiry.

Hello fellow pivoteers. I saw Egbert's post last week with a new TMS Angleator indicator &amp; thought this is a good opportunity to share a utility indicator called Snapshot_PipBull. You attach the indicator to a chart &amp; it automatically takes a picture of the chart at the close of every candle. It stores the pictures in the chart terminal folder. You can view the pictures by clicking as follows: File/Open Data Folder/MQL4/Files. The program creates a folder under the Files folder. You stop the picture-taking process by simply removing the indicator from your chart. The chart doesn't have to be open for the process to work; it can be minimized on the taskbar but your computer must be on. The original Snapshot indicator has been around for many years but I don't think it gets discussed much because it really only adds value when you have an indicator, like TMS Angleator, that leaves no visible record of it's readings. I did not create the original Snapshot indicator, nor did I change the picture-taking part of the program. I made some minor changes to make it easier to manage the picture files. With my version, when you add the indicator to a chart it adds 2 labels to the chart. It adds "Snapshot_PB" and a chart-time stamp. Those labels let you know the program is taking pictures. When you remove the indicator from the chart to stop the picture-taking process, the chart-time stamp disappears but the "Snapshot_PB" label remains to remind you that the pictures are stored as described above. After you've reviewed the pictures you can go &amp; remove the label. I hope by sharing this indicator others will study the TMS Angleator &amp; share their findings with the group. PB

I'm exhausted but very pleased with the day....I will not be posting for a few days and I hope others will...but I just had to make one point that could turn ones trading from so so, to very profitable and that is" Know Your Currency. Story telling time with a point. About 12 years ago me and a trader from Wisconsin traded together nearly every day on Ivocalize. He was a farmer and excavation contractor, I was a machinery distributor so we got along very fine. He was a very very aggressive trader, one day alone he grossed 6 figures and I watched in awe. In the middle he had a margin call that needed to be satisfied, he cleared it and at the end of the day all he could say is "I think I am going to have a tax problem this year". We kind of lost touch after my wife became very ill, and eventually I sold my contracts and had to pick up my life once again, this time alone. But my friend taught me something about knowing your currency that has always stuck with me. He would trade only GBPJPY, GBPUSD and EURO and he watched and analyzed every move they made during the day. He liked moving averages, pivots, levels, and, yes, Stochastic, but never set in the way all of us were taught, he had special settings and he still uses them today. For example today's GBP........You saw I was short many times during the past few weeks, cashing out when I had nice profit, no different today after the reaction to the Feds.......but one thing GBP does over and over, just before a big move a nasty spike will occur, taking out tons of stops and new entries. I had just closed both my Euro and Gbp positions and I was happy with the results.....but then the spike (see the highlighted candle)...and where did it come to a abrupt halt??? Yep...under the R38 and I hammered it with a shotgun blast of small entries with a tight mental stop....if it went against me to the tune of 300.00 I would close and walk away....but did it? Nope...So, I dedicate this trade to my old friend here in FF...Digger...thanks dig!!!

There’s also nothing wrong with scaling out trades and maybe letting a couple run. IMO old adage of cutting your losers quick and letting your winners run is just that. An old adage. I have better consistency when I target a setup and a minimum target. Typical that’s it 50pip increments. I don’t care if I missed out on a longer run, I know there’s another setup around the corner. I can scale in larger trades at each new setup, without waiting to see if an existing trade has more legs. Plus it’s much less stressful.

--- 帖子 #32128 ---
There is a thing called "Turnaround Tuesday" in trading. It references mostly to stocks and index's but is very much present in forex. Price seldom moves in a straight line right off the sunday open. Often you'll see price revisit/retrace from the weekly open and or previous weekly high. Trader Dante had mentioned in the past the stats on the euro doing the very same thing. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Rarely will I take a trade off the open. If I do then I prepare to close it out as the possibility of it retracing is high. Typically I will wait till close of Tuesday daily and the assess. My typical trades will be in on Wed candle, out by late Thursday or Friday.

--- 帖子 #32162 ---
The market doesn't care whether you're short or long. It's emotionless and will do whatever it wants. What we're doing here are SWAG's as Lan Turner calls them. (Scientific Wild Ass Guesses) hopefully by combining technical and fundamental analysis we get it right half the time or better. My average in over a 1,000 fx trades has been 2/3 of the time I'm right. The 1/3 of the time I'm wrong I just rack that up to the cost of doing business. If you had a bricks and mortar business you'd have all kinds of expenditures. rent, property tax, utilities, employee payroll, etc. Pick whatever column floats your boat and stick your losses in there. I had a client in the brokerage that I was doing a lot of business with, suddenly they just stopped paying their bill they had 50 K in credit, luckily it was caught early and we put them on credit hold eventually all the numbers on the left moved to the right. In the eleventh hour they paid their bill and a week later ceased operations. People say trading is gambling, the reality is everything is gambling. Business or crossing the street, there are no guarantees in life. You teach them well Davit. If they don't pay attention to news events, risk management and position sizing its out of your hands.

AUD Governor Philip Lowe suggest the Bank is in no hurry to lower rates again. Quarterly inflation data released this week did little to add pressure on the RBA to ease again and so the AUD stands to extend its recent gains if the Bank seemingly rules out another near term cut. EUR Looking at the data, business surveys will start the week, with the final October print of the manufacturing PMI out on Monday along with the November Sentix Index, followed by the final services PMI on Wednesday. Eurozone retail sales are also due on Wednesday. German numbers may attract more interest given the growing worries of a recession in the country. GBP The Bank of England’s policy decision on Thursday will be the main event and could prove to be the Bank’s most important meeting for some time.Bank may be forced to cut interest rates even if lawmakers were to approve a Brexit deal as the ongoing political uncertainty, not to mention the long drawn-out trade war and the resultant global slowdown, weigh heavily on the British economy. CAD The Bank of Canada surprised everyone by flagging a possible rate cut at its policy meeting this past week. Loonie is more likely to react to negative data than positive ones in the coming weeks, including the October employment report due on Friday. NZD One crucial piece of the jigsaw for the RBNZ will be Wednesday’s quarterly employment numbers. The unemployment rate is projected to have ticked higher to 4.1% in the third quarter and for jobs growth to have moderated to 0.3% from 0.8% over the quarter. JPY are unlikely to stir much of a response in the Yen but will be watched to determine how long the Bank of Japan will be able to stay on the sidelines.

Should be exciting night Red Rate event on AUD Its funny that I get excited about red events while some of my colleagues run away and shut their PC's To me its all about volatility.How can we exploit this? RED EVENTS SHOULD ALWAYS BE LOOKED AT AS POSITIVE DEVELOPMENT Opportunities to make bank Its shifting your mindset from fear of the market to opportunity to make money.This point was thoroughly covered by Mark Douglas in "Trading in the Zone" The market doesn’t generate happy or painful information From the markets perspective, it’s all simply information. It may seem as if the market is causing you to feel the way you do at any given moment, but that’s not the case. It’s your own mental framework that determines how you perceive the information, how you feel, and, as a result, whether or not you are in the most conducive state of mind to spontaneously enter the flow and take advantage of whatever the market is offering. Mark Douglas

The Road Not Taken Robert Frost - 1874-1963 Two roads diverged in a yellow wood, And sorry I could not travel both And be one traveler, long I stood And looked down one as far as I could To where it bent in the undergrowth; Then took the other, as just as fair, And having perhaps the better claim, Because it was grassy and wanted wear; Though as for that the passing there Had worn them really about the same, And both that morning equally lay In leaves no step had trodden black. Therefore its not always trade working out but HOW LONG it takes to work out.Not saying it may not work out next 8rs but I hate capital being kept hostage

Heres a google sheet I use for the calendar event selection and review It uses the Forex Factory calendar csv file from the site. Heres how: Use the weekly link on the bottom left of the Forex Factory page. ( Should look like this https://cdn-nfs.faireconomy.media/ff_calendar_thisweek.csv?date=10.2019 in the sheet ) Right click on it and select "copy link address" See attached picture Then paste the link in the box on the sheet. Select your time zone Check the boxes of the events that interest you, and make your notes Review what you have done on the "Review" tab Only fill in the data on page 1 You can replace the link the following week the same way and reuse this, just clear you notes or save it as new file for review later. Just helps to organize everything i want to see. You can: Filter days Filter events Filter currencies Make notes for the events Check boxes to have all the info sent to a review sheet Here is the link to the doc https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets...hWlGsgBR5p5aEo FYI.. You need google sheets to run this. Cheers

USD In the United States, the calendar is relatively thin until Wednesday, when Fed Chairman Jay Powell testifies before the Joint Economic Committee of Congress. AUD staged a spectacular recovery lately, with an improving trade outlook and the RBA signalling that it’s done with rate cuts for a while fuelling the rally. Markets now assign a mere 15% chance for another cut in December, and that could fall towards zero if the upcoming wage price index for Q3 (Wednesday) and employment data for October (Thursday) come in strong. EUR Considering how weak the German PMIs were throughout the quarter, such an outcome, unfortunately, seems quite likely. If that’s the case, it may be a very unpleasant week for the Euro, as the ‘doom and gloom’ of recent years returns to haunt it. That could raise the odds that the European Central Bank (ECB) rolls out even more monetary stimulus under the leadership of Christine Lagarde, something that markets currently don’t consider very likely judging by the pricing of future rate cuts. GBP As usual, the pound will probably react only to politics; not economics. All eyes remain on the election campaign, and the biggest driver for sterling now may be what opinion polls signal. CAD remains in a range between 1.33000 and 1.31000 and while it could become a pair of interest for now we’ll wait until further price action development. NZD The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) will announce its decision early on Wednesday, and markets seem somewhat split over whether policymakers are going to cut rates. Inflation was stronger than the RBNZ had projected in Q3, as was the labour market, while the US-China ceasefire painted a brighter picture for exports. JPY The silver lining is that domestic demand likely stayed solid, but that may change in Q4, as the sales tax was raised in October. The last time Japan raised this tax back in 2014, a recession followed, so the BoJ will likely wait for Q4 results before it draws any conclusions on the economy. Keep an eye on your charts for possible major price moves.

Hi all, Davit, thanks again for this great thread. I am extremely pleased to see you absolutely nailing it. Very well deserved. The same goes for the other main contributors. I will become more active on this thread now that I can focus back on trading again. There has been a number of posts regarding GBP. Just wanted to add my 2 cents (well pence I guess ). The General Election is 4 weeks away and that, at the moment, is by far and away the main driver behind any major moves on the pound. Any economic news coming out at the moment regarding the British economy is going to have minimal effect whilst we are in the midst of this election (outside of any shocking economic news of course). The very basics of it are: The Conservatives (Boris Johnson) building on their lead in the polls is positive for GBP. Any erosion of their lead via Labour (Corbyn) &amp; Lib Dems (Swinson) will have a negative impact on GBP. Why? If Boris gets his majority in parliament then Brexit will get done (ok not necessarily good for the British economy but the businesses/markets seem to just want it sorted now so that they can start planning etc) If Boris loses/does not get majority then the whole Brexit drama continues creating more uncertainty. This is a pretty good site for daily blogs on British Politics and gives updates on polls etc: http://www2.politicalbetting.com Cheers all, Steve

I won't make a habit of posting here because it is an offline chart and does not conform to the thread's regular pairs. The aim is to encourage all basket traders to incorporate Davit's style of pivot trading into their strategy (actually to make it their MAIN strategy), as well as to present existing pivot traders with the possibility of adding offline basket charts to their existing line-up of pairs. AUDNZD As we approach the end of the month I submit an observation with respect to Monthly Pivots . I look at these monthly pivots towards the end of each month albeit briefly and rarely consider them of much importance for Davit style trading. However, this month will they be of significance??? AUDNZD is at an interesting juncture?? In the past 9-moths, this pair has bottomed 3 times at S100 - seemingly close to a 3-month cycle?? Each time, close to the end of the month or very early into the new month (August). Although, August was a spike down, news related, the other "bottoms" showed indecision on the daily candles as the end of the month approached. Price action on the Daily candles as the month ends, may suggest we are approaching a reversal zone. I have stated before in previous posts on this thread that failure at S38/R38 is a familiar characteristic of this pair. Today, have we reached a reversal at S38 now? With NZD and AUD News today it will be interesting to observe how this level for AUDNZD acts today and over this week before month end?

I agree with you 100%. I am also focused on the opportunities offered by the market, those with the highest probability rather than a single approach. I can take positions in the direction of the fundamentals, in favor of the trend or against, swings, etc... it doesn't matter, the important thing is to bring home pips (I say "scratch the cheese" ). The pivots are the main weapon but I don't dislike the trading of some formations of patterns (when the MM is manipulating). I often trade "bi-directional" that is, while I follow a main direction (usually droved by fundamentals) and I adding positions, at the same time grab pips by taking positions in the opposite direction. Some trades takes more time to develop (weeks, months...) and others are closed faster (minuts, hours, days...). The biggest problem with the failure of traders is the lack of adaptation to the various situations of market and volatility.

--- 帖子 #32919 ---
IF EURNZD @ 1.71619 if nzdusd @ 0.64120 if EURUSD @ 1.10042 Yes absolutely. You're right !!!! I learned to do these accounts with you. Thank you my friend kk It is a mathematical formula. prices from: EURNZD x NZDUSD = EURUSD (1.71619 x 0.64120 = 1.10042) EURUSD / NZDUSD = EURNZD EURUSD / EURNZD = NZDUSD We're only talking about 24 pips for EURNZD to reach 1.7185 We really have to evaluate. One pair depends on another. Let's say each one moves 12 pips. So: EURUSD 1.10396 / NZDUSD (+ 12pips) 0.6424 = eurnzd (1.7185) or EURUSD (-12pips) 1.09922 / EURNZD 1.7185 = NZDUSD 0.63964

Hey ppxdf my friend, I see what you are doing, and since market does its own thing, you ended with a winning trade. Good job. For me, I still wouldn't take that trade and here are further reasons: 1. I also look at future pivots to prepare for following week, but do not trade them. I use them more for tp if in a trade because price tends to move toward following WP on Friday. 2. Considering #1 price in Oanda EN closed at 1.71463 right at WP. Not optimal location for a high probability trade. 3. Choosing my reason for entry: a. Some trades look like a good setup and I will find an indicator ADR, TDI, even Pivot to confirm my bias. b. Some trades look like a good setup because it is at peak of my trading method rules. Trades will always look good, that's part of this business. However, if I stick to one method only, then I only execute that method and let its probabilities work out. If I look for anything else I then open myself up for interpretation, then anything goes. Why would I want to do that? Notice Davit's list has Trading Psychology #1 on list. We as Humans are quick to fool ourselves into believing anything, we see things that are not, and fail to see that which is not plain to see. That is why simple clear rules are essential to stay on right path, that is why keeping trading record part of successful traders. If I trade 61-100 reversals only (moved by fundamentals) for example, I only wait for those setups. If those are my rules yet trade anything else, especially if it goes into profit, I not only did not trade my rules, I reinforced my flawed thinking and will start looking for and justifying other setups. Might give me immediate satisfaction, but will certainly lead to failed trading while still having a winning system, one we then see as nonprofitable. I don't need to take every trade, just those that fit my methods criterias. It is not my job to be right on every trade, it is my job to do every trade right. Market thrives on bad decisions. Not only in trading but life in general we allow simple actions go unchecked, when in fact they are creating habits that go against what we established as right path. We justify by minimizing its importance until we notice we are exactly opposite we wanted to be, wondering how we got there. It's all in the mind. Pivot, news, method, this thread pick anything that makes this method great, but master your mind...and not just your trading, Life will move to higher levels. That is all for this weeks session...Lol. Now let load up on pips. Probably dissected this too much but that is how my mind works on all things. Drives my wife nuts...

--- 帖子 #33154 ---
For new and experienced traders joining us its important to understand where I am coming from. Mark Douglas had profound influenced on me and totally changed my view of the markets.When others see pain and suffering and loss I see the market as ever present opportunity to prosper. Its shifting from fear to opportunity from sure trade to probabilities.With this in mind lets refresh Mark Douglas gold nuggets Winning and being a winning trader are two different things… Anyone, and I literally mean anyone, even a 5-year-old child, can find themselves in a winning trade. It does not require any special skill to get lucky on any particular trade and hit a winner. All you have to do is open your trading platform and push a few buttons and if you get lucky, you can make a lot of money in a short amount of time. As a result of the above, it’s natural for a trader who has not yet developed his or her trading skills to take the leap from “it’s easy to win” to “it can’t be that much harder to make a living from this”. This is how many traders’ careers get started. Needless to say, it is also how they get on the path to losing a whole lot of money just as fast or even faster than they made it. A winning trader has the mental skills to realize, understand and utilize the FACT that any particular trade he or she takes has basically a random outcome. That is to say, they cannot possibly know the outcome of that trade until it is over. The winning trader knows this and they also know that they must trade in-line with this belief over a large series of trades and ignore all the temptations and feelings that get kicked up on each trade they take. They are able to do this because they keep their eyes on the bigger picture. That bigger picture is the fact that IF they execute their method flawlessly, over and over, over a long enough period of time / series of trades, they will come out profitable. Thus, do not mistake a winning trade for you being a winning trader, yet. A very easy trap to fall into. Mental skills are the key to trading … A key point that Mark Douglas really seems to want to drive into people is: Even if your method is a high-probability method, it’s the proper execution of that method that you need proper mental skills for. If you don’t have those mental skills, even a winning strategy will lose. Mental skills are things like; staying focused on the process, on your method, and not worrying about the consequences if this trade goes wrong. If you don’t have the proper mental skills to stay positively focused on the process of trading; on doing exactly what you need to do when you need to do it without reservation, hesitation or fear, you will not make money in the market. It’s critical to remember that no matter how good your technical method is at generating wining trades, turning those winners into a consistent income takes the ability to do or not do some things that the method can’t help us with . The method can’t force us to pre-define our risk, or with making the mistake of moving our stop closer and stopping us out prematurely, it can’t stop us from hesitating and getting in too late or from over-trading or from getting out too soon and leaving money on the table. No matter how good the method, if you make mental errors you will lose. If you really boil down what Mark is saying by his comments on “mental skills”, it basically comes down to having ice-cold ‘blood in your veins’ discipline. Mental skills like discipline essentially means the ability to control yourself and especially your behavior / actions in the market against the CONSTANT TEMPTATION the market gives us. Essentially, as a trader, you are fighting against yourself to see which part of your brain has more control; the older, emotional and more primitive part or the more advanced logic and planning parts. Technical price patterns aren’t designed to tell us what ‘will’ happen next… Technical methods of any kind, price action included, are not designed to tell us what a market will do next. As Douglas says, they are designed to help us put the ODDS of success in our favor over a SERIES of trades. There are some profound psychological implications that go along with this fact… The outcome of any particular signal is unique and random. There’s no way to know in advance the outcome of any particular signal or the sequences of wins and losses or over a series of trades. In other words, the nature of trading is random. Douglas goes onto to describe something that may be a little difficult to understand at first, but that is critical for you to grasp if you want to make consistent money trading: By accepting the random nature of trading I can produce consistent results … Now, on the surface, it seems contradictory to say you can produce consistent results from something that is random in nature. However, let’s dig a little deeper… Technical methods and patterns will give a trader the same advantage a casino has over any individual player. A casino has an “edge” for every game they offer. What a casino knows is that whilst any singular instance of someone playing their game might result in the player winning money or even hitting the “jack pot”, due to the edge they hold, over-time and over enough series of events, the casino will make a profit, and a large one at that. Remembering this point will help you make the transition from thinking in ‘certainties’ as I put it, to thinking in probabilities as Mark describes and as you should be thinking. If you don’t integrate the randomness principle, you will find trading is the most frustrating endeavor you can undertake. You can only generate consistent returns by understanding that each trade is random and unique, and then taking that information and using it to control yourself after each trade. Do not get hung up on your last trade. Instead, focus on consistently trading your method over and over. Frustration comes from expecting something our method can’t do. Technical methods find and identify patterns in collective human behavior, the problem is, the outcomes don’t always correspond with the pattern on a trade by trade basis. There doesn’t have to be a relationship with the outcome and pattern. There is no guarantee that this trade will be the exact same result as the last one, even if they look the same. Rather, the method only tells us that IF we use it consistently, then over a series of trades, we should be profitable. Think in probabilities, not certainties… Perhaps the point Mark Douglas is most famous for drilling into traders, is that you need to learn to think in probabilities. We did discuss this a little earlier, but it’s critical to understand that there’s a random distribution of wins and losses over any sequence of trades . Traders who learn to think in probabilities do not experience the mental ‘trauma’ like those traders who haven’t learned to think in probabilities because they are not ‘expecting’ a winner on any given trade like those who don’t think in probabilities. Learning to think in probabilities releases your expectations from trades because you are focused on the results of the overall series of trades, not on the result of any given trade. If you have a weighted coin that will be heads 70% of the time, you still don’t know the sequence of heads and tails, all you know is OVER TIME 70% of the flips will be heads. Germany Manufacturing PMI was revised higher to 44.1 in November 2019 from a preliminary estimate of 43.8 and compared to October's final 42.1. The latest reading was the highest since June, but still comfortably inside contraction territory. Output contracted for the tenth consecutive month, the longest sequence of decline since 2008-09, while both new orders and export sales fell at the slowest pace since January. In addition, buying levels and employment across the manufacturing sector dropped at softer rates, while business sentiment was in positive territory for the first time since June. On the price front, input costs fell by the most since March 2016, amid reductions in the price of chemicals, metals and plastics; and average factory gate charges decreased for the fifth month due to strong competition for new work. Manufacturing PMI in Germany averaged 51.68 from 2008 until 2019, reaching an all time high of 63.30 in December of 2017 and a record low of 32 in January of 2009. Part of this system is breaking up lots into smaller lots so You can "capture the move" post from 2018 from 2018 "This system takes advantage of market volatility and uses same tools MM use to take your stops in your advantage. I use fish net method versus sniper.Multiple entries vs single. When price is at example R61 UJ example I place 5 orders when PA moves in my way.I will add more should price continues going south but suppose after 4hrs price goes against you.That's fine remember we still have not added all our intended orders and price is still in the zone.Price spikes at 100R basically taking stops and creating liquidity for large MM orders and you added additional 5orders. This is not adding to losers this is BUILDING A POSITION when entire order is 1 batch of trades! Think of the CAT we got it covered from tail to head. Now suppose price smashed 100R and started to go north even more.I usually wait to see if its a fake out or not because vast majority of times its a shake up spikes.Lets say it was not then I close 25% of my red trades and wait to see how PA reacts.If everything goes against me I may close all positions as loss .NO big deal continue hammering trades because I firmly believe in sample size.My account does not die with 1 batch or 10batch of red trades!!!!! This is not martingale nor brainless way to trade in fact its pretty sophisticated taking advantage of spikes and volatility when others die you thrive!" Bubincka makes good use of this concept and many others.

New Zealand’s GDP expanded 0.7 percent on a quarterly basis in the three months to September 2019 , up from a 0.1 percent expansion in the previous period to beat market expectations of a 0.6 percent rise. Growth was nudged by retail activity, up 2.4 percent (vs 0.8 percent in Q2) and boosted by spending on electronics such as appliances, mobile phones, and computers. Several GDP components rebounded in the third quarter, namely: primary industries 1.1 percent (vs -0.5 percent); manufacturing 0.6 percent (vs -1 percent), and construction 0.6 percent (vs -0.9 percent). In contrast, utilities contracted 0.2 percent after expanding 0.8 percent. On annual basis, activity rose 2.3 percent following a 2.1 percent expansion. GDP Growth Rate in New Zealand averaged 0.64 percent from 1987 until 2019, reaching an all time high of 2.80 percent in the third quarter of 1999 and a record low of -2.40 percent in the first quarter of 1991 Last Q could be dramatically worse since Trump trade war.That's gonna be released later 2020

--- 帖子 #33340 ---
You forgetting pink elephant in the room BREXIT Lots of uncertainty and that includes Euro zone countries their PMI CPI GDP's To me we may see massive dumping of Euro by the end of the year. Based on location and everything else going long EA before major news was big no. anyway keep honing your skills from 2016 The Importance of Mistakes All automatic guidance systems reach their goals by constantly correcting mistakes. A guided missile on its way to its target has sensors that detect when its off course. The guidance mechanism then makes the necessary adjustment and proceeds. This is done thousands of times on its journey. The guided missile relies on this negative feedback to guide it to its destination. Without this negative feedback, a guided missile would actually not know where it was going and would never reach its target. The same is true for the human servo-mechanism. It is unfortunate that so many of us interpret mistakes as a failure and suffer feelings of frustration and discouragement when actually the mistakes we make are exactly the information that our servomechanism needs to make the necessary corrections to take us to our goals. Your servomechanism has no opinion one way or the other about mistakes. It simply uses the information to guide it to its objective. What we call mistakes are actually valuable lessons for success . An important part of Psycho-Cybernetics is learning to use mistakes creatively and to remove the negative feelings that mistakes cause. above from book Emotion free trading (clipoard -Davit's philosophy) Oct 2016 This is from PDF on clipboard under Davit's Philosophy.Obviously changed the title for copy rights reasons Chapter 24 FORGIVENESS One of the biggest problems I see with traders is that they refuse to forgive themselves for trading mistakes. This causes a much bigger problem than most people realize. You see, when you make a trading mistake, you need to forgive yourself for making that mistake. But the thing is many people do not forgive themselves for their mistakes. In fact, they do quite the opposite. They beat themselves up and continually picture what they did wrong in vivid detail. This is the very worst thing you can do after making a mistake, trading or otherwise. Forgiveness is a key concept in Psycho-Cybernetics. As weve just learned about how our subconscious works, we know that if we continually picture in vivid detail something, it causes that picture to come true for us. Or it at least makes it much more likely for it to come true. So it only makes sense that if we make a mistake, we must forget that mistake and forgive ourselves completely. If, on the other hand, we dont forgive ourselves and relive the mistake in our minds again and again, what do you think is going to happen? Its obvious that we will repeat the mistake. This happens because our subconscious does not care whether we give it good or bad information, it simply sees the clear pictures we give it and tries to act it out in our lives. Obviously, it can only act this picture out if its within our capabilities. And I think we all know that making trading mistakes is quite within our capabilities. This is the reason it is so important to forgive ourselves when we make a mistake or an error. If we dont, we are likely to relive the mistake in our minds and then most likely project it onto our trading. This will cause big problems. If you think back, Im sure can you think of times where you made mistakes and beat yourself up for it. Not forgiving yourself, no matter what the mistake, will bring out the worst emotions. Remorse, regret, self-doubt, and guilt all come with not forgiving ourselves for a past mistake. Youve heard it all before. Im sure youve been told to forget a past losing trade and move on to the next one. Emotions are used correctly and appropriately when it applies to something in the present time. Since we cannot live in the past, we cant appropriately react emotionally to the past. As Dr. Maltz says, The past can be simply written off, closed, forgotten, insofar as our emotional reactions are concerned. We do not need to take an emotional position one way or the other regarding detours that might have taken us off course in the past. The important thing is our present direction and our present goal. We need to recognize our own errors as mistakes. Otherwise, we could not correct our course and steering or guidance would be impossible. But it is futile and fatal to hate or condemn ourselves for our mistakes. One of the biggest reasons people get into losing streaks while trading is because they confuse their losing trades with themselves. In other words, we conclude that because we had a losing trade or a series of losing trades, we are a losing trader. But the important thing to remember here is we are not our losing trades. Losing trades are part of trading. There isnt a single trader in the world who doesnt have losing trades. The only way to avoid them is not to trade in the first place. You cannot be a successful trader until you take mistakes and losing trades for what they really are. They are simply by-products in the trading game and need to be used to gain learning and understanding. But in no way do they define us as a person. But that is where the big problem comes in. Many people let their losing trades and mistakes define them. If they're having trouble and have had a series of losing trades, they start to think of themselves as a loser. They continually think of themselves in that way. As we know from before, this kind of thinking will just bring on more of the same. Forgiving yourself completely is the only way to avoid this trouble. You are not your mistakes and losing trades. You must put the past behind you and go forward. Holding a grudge against yourself only hurts yourself. Forgive yourself, its the only way to be successful. Above its extremely important paradigm shift how you see trading and how you see mistakes and losers.To me its where one should be ideally or strive to reach.Once you truly grasp probability factor of my system then a loser is just a statistic by product of sample..Its all probability over series of trades and like MD says on my 1st page "You don’t need to know what is going to happen next in order to make money." Its so simple and profound same time.I still get chills reading simple things like this by Mark Douglas

I am going to give you honest opinion.Starting with Mark Douglas The 5 Fundamental Truths of Trading: 1. Anything can happen. 2. You don’t need to know what is going to happen next to make money. 3. There is a random distribution between wins and losses for any given set of variables that define an edge. 4. An edge is nothing more than an indication of a higher probability of one thing happening over another. 5. Every moment in the market is unique. All trading is reactionary that means we react what market provides.I dont know what's going to happen but I do know I have no fear in me whatever that may be.In short I am in control if I must take a loss I'll take it then look for another trade then that's just fine.Anyone telling you they know the future is bullshitting including Bloomberg ,news media , trading firms and hedge funds.Nobody knows.Bloomberg has been wrong numerous times and could be they are already have positions influencing the market.Does not matter we react what market does and that's as real as I can put it. My Calendar Analysis for the upcoming week: This week I don't pay attention to USD data since US conflict with Iran is too big to ignore which means news headlines will probably overshadow other events. Monday GBP : Composite PMI (Dec) Generally, UK's PMI shouldn't be a big market mover and, with likely limited political news for U.K.'s divorce on Jan. 31, focus will probably shift to BoE and whether it will cut. Since a weaker November GDP and a rate cut are widely expected, I personally like to see a weaker PMI to go short on GBP. So for me WPP and even R38 will be levels to watch: Attached Image (click to enlarge) EUR: Markit Composite PMI (Dec) + German : Services PMI (Dec) Although some FX calendars have not ranked this event as High Impact , but this week they'll attract a lot of attentions. If last week's improvements continue, this should be interpreted as " the beginning of an end " meaning we can keep a positive sentiment that PMI's are moving towards 50 territory. If so, they'll be positive enough for EUR to stop getting further dragged by Brexit headwinds; at least in the short run... Tuesday EUR: CPI (YoY) (Dec) After 11 months of disappointing PMIs, last week we finally saw signs of stabilisation for EUR zone and specifically German and France. This weeks CPI, if printed as expected and, even better, more positive than forecast, can provide grounds for some beautiful upward reactions. But what if not? Like I said, good PMIs and Business confidence improvement to its greatest level since June, suggests some signs of rising optimism which means I'll still wait to buy dips no matter what: Attached Image (click to enlarge) Wednsday CAD : Ivey PMI (Dec) We all saw what happened between US and Iran; the dramatic reaction of oil price was anything but logical with regard to the market share of Iran's oil these days. But like they say: anything can happen . I personally prefer to get out of way when it comes to emotional trading where gossips take over! NZD : GlobalDairyTrade Price Index I might be wrong, but I've noticed NZD often follows global macroeconomics and geo-political events rather than its own data; especially those related to China and its sister: Australia. Although in both cases we've seen some up-pushing events in recent weeks, but the problem is NZD has already come too far. However, this doesn't mean we must expect downward movements, but rather I'd say a ranging market seems more logical to my eyes. In this regard, honestly I wouldn't trade "both" ways since fundamentals are pointing more to up than down: Attached Image (click to enlarge) Friday AUD: Retail Sales (MoM) (Nov) Last week, China lowered the amount of reserves that banks need to keep on hold. This will inject fresh liquidity into their banking system and is a good sign Beijing will boost economic growth in 2020 which is a + for AUD. But downside is AUD has already come too far and I can't imagine any further upward movements until something real happens. In addition to this, Australia's bush fires have given rise to some serious concerns over it's near-term growth. bottom line: I'm expecting a range market for AUD which, like Davit always says, is a blessing; in other words, I've fallen in love with range markets too but from the look of it, next station looks like a buy: Attached Image (click to enlarge)

There is a problem in your calculation. The pivots are calculated with high, low and close price of previous week. So it makes absolutely no sense to look at next week levels when the actual week is not finished. There will be always a "reaction " at R38 and S38, since open price can never be below S38 at opening of the week.... So better forget this theory.

It's interesting between different websites where the news events are featuring different levels of importance, different estimated numbers, and even different numbers when they come out. An interesting example was last week was on Wednesday FF had US ISM manufacturing marked as a RED flag event consensus 48.1 and a RED miss @47.2. myfxbook had Markit Manufacturing PMI coming out 15 minutes earlier and marked as an AMBER event consensus 52.5 and a miss @ 52.4. The question is which data are we supposed to believe. One thing I like about myfxbook is it counts down and starts flashing in the last minute then dings on the screen with the news right on schedule FF is lagging way behind these days and you have to refresh the screen if and when the data comes up. I've found lags of 10 and 15 plus minutes not uncommon on FF.

different levels of importance The different levels of importance are according to what each of them understands or interprect what kind of news or speculation is moving the currency. Could be the combinations of 4: Ecnomic data Politics Central bank policy or Risk Sentiment different estimated numbers, the estimate, depends on what institute is making the poll. usually they use reuters Poll, but sometimes there are some others, . even different numbers when they come out This is hard to happen. what happens are rounding or approximation but it is possible to know where the exact numbers are An interesting example last week was on Wednesday FF had US ISM manufacturing marked as a RED flag event consensus 48.1 and a RED miss @47.2. to be red, numbers must be below the minimum, not below the estimate and depends which institute they are refering to. to be green numbers must be above the maximum, not just above the estimate and depends which institute they are refering to. the exact number is in the press realease

The latest Service PMI boosted investors' optimism that economic growth will rebound in the first half, dampening expectations for monetary easing; however MUFG Bank says we need more evidence to back this optimism. Also, according to BoE, there could be a “relatively prompt response” from the bank if it looked like the economy faces a period of prolonged weakness. Technical Side: One interesting thing I've noticed is GBPUSD is currently almost on WPP which happened to be right in the middle of two key support/resistance lines in daily time frame. Technical Side: We shouldn't forget that EUR's last bunch of PMIs caused optimism and were interpreted by many as sign of stability. Technical Side: Again, if no surprise happens, like I said above, prices below this week's S61 will attract a lot of attention IMHO. What to look for on Fundamentals Economic Release &gt; Leading Indicator for the Economic Release USD - US DOLLAR 1. Non-Farm Payrolls &gt; Employment Component of Non-Manufacturing ISM 2. Retail Sales &gt; ICSC Chain Store Sales Report &amp; Johnson Redbook Survey 3. ISM Manufacturing &gt; Chicago PMI, Philly Fed and Empire State Manufacturing Surveys 4. ISM Non-Manufacturing &gt; ISM Manufacturing 5. Producer Prices &gt; Import Prices 6. Consumer Prices &gt; Producer Prices 7. GDP &gt; Retail Sales and Trade Balance 8. Trade &gt; Manufacturing ISM and Export Orders Component of the Report 9. University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index (UMich) &gt; IBD/TIPP Consumer Confidence 10. Conference Board Consumer Confidence &gt; UMich and IBD Survey 11. Personal Income &gt; Average Weekly Earnings 12. Personal Spending &gt; Retail Sales 13. New Home Sales &gt; Existing Home Sales EUR - EUROZONE **For Any Eurozone Data, Look at individual German and French Data **As the largest country in the Eurozone, German data impacts the EUR most almost exclusively. 1. --- 帖子 #33902 ---
Mark Douglas’s “Trading in the Zone” is a seminal classic of trading psychology. The book should be read from cover to cover but it's essential tenents are : 1. Anything can happen. 2. You don’t need to know what is going to happen next in order to make money. 3. There is a random distribution between wins and losses for any given set of variables that define an edge. 4. An edge is nothing more than an indication of a higher probability of one thing happening over another. 5. Every moment in the market is unique. Everyone one of those points is a fundamental truth trading and the title itself is a reference to the idea of trading without fear. When you are in the “zone” you focus on process rather than outcome and therefore build an indomitable psychological mindset that helps you perform to your best ability every single day. Douglas’s points are timeless and true, but I want to discuss something much more mundane -- literally trading in the actual “zone”, which is often overlooked as a key ingredient to trading success. This week I was in Philly for an impromptu get together with some of my oldest and dearest camp friends. Now I am a horrible map reader and whenever I get to a new place I usually just try to get the general direction of where I am going and then set out on foot. So against Google Maps better warning that I should take public transport or Uber, I simply stepped outside the 30th street station, found my way to Chestnut Street and then just headed to downtown Philly. Philadelphia is less than 90 minutes away from New York but like almost every New Yorker I know, I never visit the place. Which is a shame. Because it’s a great city with a wonderful history, beautiful architecture, a thriving nightlife and generally a level of cool that no longer exists in the stodgy you-can-only-live-here-if-you-are-a-billionaire Manhattan. But my walk down Chestnut was more than just a rumination on gentrification, it was an indelible lesson in geography. I quickly grasped how Philly is contained between the Schuylkill and Delaware rivers. As I crossed Chestnut and Broad I finally understood the term Broad Street Bullies ( a name given to the legendary 1970’s Philadelphia Flyers hockey team). And as I made my way towards the Delaware river I could see Indendence Hall on my right and literally imagined Franklin and Jefferson writing the country’s constitution. My pedestrian stroll through the City of Brotherly Love made me more knowledgeable about the place than any Google Map ever could. Nothing beats touch and feel for not only acquiring but absorbing knowledge. Which brings me back to Trading the in Zone. Being mentally tough is a laudable goal for sure, but what about trading in the actual zone? What about studying every tick and quirk of the timeframe you trade. For the past several months K and I have been making Market Mapper tools to help traders see price patterns more intuitively. But it was only after walking those maket maps day in and day out that I started to pick up subtle clues to price action that improved my edge tremendously. This is why wizened market veterans always talk about the need for screentime . And it’s absolutely true. There is just no substitute for engaged observation. That’s why newbies traders who are just looking for a “winning setup” always fail. There are no winning setups. There are only setups that you adapt to your own style. So just like a native of a city, I can point the tourist in the right direction but to truly discover the place you need to do your own walking and discover the Zone that works for you. Boris Schlossberg.

I don't, but ... Here's an interesting fact I've found about myself and am sharing it with other members in case there are others out there having the same issue as mine! Like you've always emphasised, psychology is one of the most powerful facets of trading and to know ourselves and to learn how to curb our bad habits is probably the most challenging battle field that traders have to fight in. One of the most powerful forces I have discovered in myself is what they call FOMO ( F ear O f M issing O ut). I am not going into details here as there are loads of good articles on the Internet on that. Now I've found an interesting fact about myself. A super-easy technique to negate FOMO is to let it do whatever it wants but in a controlled manner . In other words, in order to get rid of this monster, I trade nano-lot size (sometimes 0.01, the least possible size) so that I can be my logical self again and think more clearly. Cheers ...

Brexit week This Wednesday the European Parliament will vote on the Brexit. If agreed, and this is in line with expectations, the UK will leave the European Union on 31 January. Only after Brexit can the EU and the UK start negotiating the details of their future relationship. This will include agreeing on what conditions will apply to EU-based companies that want to do business in and with the UK after the transition period. There will be more clarity on the new relationship between the EU and the UK only once this phase of the negotiations has been completed. The new agreements will enter into force after the transition period, which will end on 31 December 2020. These new agreements, too, will have to be approved by the individual member states, the UK parliament and the European Parliament. If no agreement is reached about the future relationship between the UK and EU, there will be a ‘no deal’ Brexit after the transition period.. With that said the ‘soap of negotiations’ will continue this year and can last till 2022.. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Just would like to share whats on my journal regarding Aud and CAD (also applies to NZD in lesser effect) AUD was severely affected by US-China Trade war which goes to show that AUD, as a commodity currency, depends on robust global trade to be strong. Now, with the advent of the 2019-nCOV scare affecting mostly China and some cases elsewhere, which has a potential to spread rapidly, investors are again fearing a temporary slow down in global trade thus AUD weakness. Oil demand is also preceived to decrease thus the correlation to CAD weakness. Keyword here is temporary. We don't know what will happen to nCOV phenomenon or how long it will last but looking at SARS in 2003, it took about 8 months before the issue subsides. Chinese government was not fully transparent that time thus the swift spread of the disease. This time, Chinese government is more transparent reporting minute detail of affected population to somewhat ease international sentiment. It all depends though on the level of containment by authorities and how soon they are able to address the spread of disease, so not to elevate this as international emergency. To this end, given that authorities able to contain the disease successfully, the likely outcome is market sentiment on global trade will be positive and would translate to AUD, CAD recovery. Note: AUD red news tomorrow on CPI. If green, would provide temporary boost to AUD. Market sentiment is generally negative on AUD unless nCOV is addressed.

FACTBOX -Airlines suspend China flights because of coronavirus outbreak - Reuters News 01-Feb-2020 01:52:48 Adds Qantas, Air New Zealand suspensions AIR CANADA Air Canada said on Jan. 28 it was cancelling select flights to China.
