AIR NEW ZEALAND Air New Zealand said on Feb. 1 it will suspend its Auckland-Shanghai service from Feb. 9 to March 29 due to travel restrictions affecting crew and a decline in forward bookings. AIR SEOUL South Korean budget carrier Air Seoul said on Jan. 28 it had suspended all flights to China. AIR TANZANIA Tanzania's state-owned carrier said it would postpone its maiden flights to China. It had planned to begin charter flights to China in February. AMERICAN AIRLINES American Airlines said it will cancel flights to Beijing and Shanghai starting Jan. 31, and run through March 27, though it will continue to fly to Hong Kong. BRITISH AIRWAYS BA said on Jan. 30 it had cancelled all flights to mainland China for a month. CATHAY PACIFIC AIRWAYS Hong Kong's Cathay Pacific said it would progressively reduce capacity to and from mainland China by 50% or more from Jan. 30 to the end of March. DELTA AIR LINES Delta Air Lines announced cancellations, with its last flights out of mainland China on Feb. 5, running through April 30. EGYPTAIR Egypt's flag carrier said on Jan. 30 it would suspend all flights to and from China starting Feb. 1. EL AL ISRAEL AIRLINES El Al Israel Airlines said on Jan. 30 it was suspending flights to Beijing until March 25. Israel's Health Ministry said it will not allow flights from China to land at its airports. ETHIOPIAN AIRLINES The African carrier on Jan. 30 denied reports it had suspended all flights to China. The airline's statement contradicted its passenger call centre, which told Reuters earlier in the day that flights to China had been suspended. ETIHAD AIRWAYS Abu Dhabi's Etihad Airways said passenger flights between Beijing and Nagoya, in Japan, had been temporarily suspended due to low travel demand. FINNAIR Finland's Finnair said on Jan. 31 it was cancelling all flights to mainland China between Feb. 6 and Feb. 29 and to Guangzhou between Feb. 5 and March 29. KENYA AIRWAYS Kenya Airways said on Jan. 31 it has suspended all flights to China until further notice. LION AIR Indonesia's Lion Air Group said on Jan. 29 it would suspend all flights to China from February. The airline has suspended six flights from several Indonesian cities to China so far and will suspend the rest next month. LOT POLISH AIRLINES Polish carrier LOT said it had decided to temporarily suspend its flights to Beijing until Feb. 9. LUFTHANSA Germany's Lufthansa said on Jan. 29 it was suspending Lufthansa, Swiss and Austrian Airlines flights to and from China until Feb. 9. The airline continues to fly to Hong Kong, but it will stop taking bookings for flights to mainland China until the end of February. QANTAS AIRWAYS Australia's Qantas said on Feb. 1 it was suspending direct flights to mainland China. The Australian national carrier's direct flights from Sydney to Beijing and Sydney to Shanghai will be halted from Feb. 9 until March 29. ROYAL AIR MAROC Moroccan airline Royal Air Maroc (RAM) has temporarily suspended its direct flights to China, the company said on Jan. 30. RAM had on Jan. 16 launched a direct air route with three flights weekly between its Casablanca hub and Beijing. RUSSIA All Russian airlines, with the exception of national airline Aeroflot , will stop flying to China, Deputy Prime Minister Tatiana Golikova said. RWANDAIR Rwanda carrier RwandAir has halted flights to and from China until further notice, the airline said in a statement on Friday. The decision will be reviewed later in February, it said. SAS Nordic airline SAS said on Jan. 30 it has decided to suspend all flights to and from Shanghai and Beijing from Jan. 31 until Feb. 9. SAS offers 12 regular weekly connections from and to Shanghai and Beijing. SCOOT Singapore airline Scoot said it was suspending all flights between Singapore and China from Feb. 8, media reported. SHANGHAI AIRLINES Shanghai Airlines said on Jan. 31 it would suspend its Chengdu-Budapest flight between Feb. 4 and March 28 and its Xi'an-Budapest flight between Feb. 6 and March 26 according to a statement on the website of the Budapest Airport operator. The airline's Shanghai-Budapest flight is unaffected. SINGAPORE AIRLINES Singapore Airlines Ltd said on Jan. 31 it would reduce capacity on some of its routes to mainland China in February. The cuts include flights to Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Chengdu, Xiamen and Chongqing, some of which are flown by regional arm SilkAir. Its budget carrier Scoot is also cutting back on flights to China. TURKISH AIRLINES Turkey's flag carrier said on Jan. 30 it would decrease frequency on scheduled flights to Beijing, Guangzhou, Shanghai and Xian between Feb. 5 and Feb. 29. UNITED AIRLINES Chicago-based United announced cancellations, saying last flights out of mainland China will be Feb. 5, running through March 28. United had previously suspended 24 U.S. flights to Beijing, Hong Kong and Shanghai between Feb. 1 and Feb. 8 because of a significant drop in demand. UNITED PARCEL SERVICE INC UPS has cancelled 22 China flights, as a result of the Wuhan quarantines and normal manufacturing closures due to the Lunar New Year holiday, UPS Chief Executive David Abney said on Jan. 30. He did not specify how many flights cancellations were due to the virus. VIETJET Vietnam's Vietjet will suspend all flights to and from China from Feb. 1, the company said on Jan. 31. Vietnam Airlines will suspend some flights to China. VIETNAM AIRLINES Vietnam Airlines will suspend its flights to destinations in China next week over coronavirus concerns, the company said on Friday. VIRGIN ATLANTIC Virgin Atlantic said on Jan. 30 it would suspend its daily operations to Shanghai for two weeks from Feb. 2. --- 帖子 #34449 ---
Inductive Reasoning There are two different methods for reasoning, inductive and deductive. While deductive reasoning looks for certainties, inductive reasoning is used when a circumstance is seen as supplying evidence that a conclusion could be true. The belief in a conclusion based on inductive reasoning is highly probable and based on evidence that can be seen and measured but is not 100% certain. Inductive reasoning is a tool for making well informed educated guesses using all the available data and information you have at the time. It doesn’t mean you will be correct but this type of reasoning will give you the best estimation you can make based on the current known facts. Deductive reasoning is a tool you use when you don’t know something to be a fact 100% or you are having to make the best decision in an uncertain environment. The different types of inductive reasoning: Generalization: Drawing a general conclusion about all of a group based on an observation. All the chickens I have seen are white, so all chickens must be white. Statistical: Make a high probability guess based on statistics. If 90% of all chickens are white then out of ten chickens, nine should be white.* Sample: Making an educated guess about others based on a sample size. If nine out of ten chickens on this farm are white then 90% of chickens will be white on my neighbors farm. Analogous: Makes a conclusion based on the shared attributes of two types of things. 90% of chickens are white and ducks are birds like chickens so 90% of ducks are probably white too. Predictive: Makes a conclusion by using a prediction from a past sample of data. When I went to this farm three years ago 90% of the chickens here were white so when I go back tomorrow 90% of the chickens are likely to be white again. Causal inference: Makes a conclusion using a causal connection. 90% of chickens on this farm are white. I just saw a white bird in the woods behind the farm. The bird I saw was likely a chicken. Inductive reasoning can be a tool to use for a higher probability of having a correct assumption over randomness. However it can be dangerous when used to see links that are not really there or to assume too much from a limited set of data. In the business, investing, and trading world inductive reasoning must be used a lot of the time because in those environments people must manage so much uncertainty in the future that they can only make the best decisions possible using the available data. The quality of decisions using inductive reasoning are based on the value and real connections of the data to reality. This goes to heart of trading.Calendar events analyses are basically preparing you set of actions depending outcome of data however based on previous examples of market reactions inductive reasoning is used to connect data to reality.Its basically creating an edge over randomness. Example if you look past green NFP and market was bullish right after on USD then we can use inductive reasoning to predict market reaction on similar economic conditions to be same. Same manner if market expects rate cut and similarly starts selling it prior of event then we can conclude likely future markets reactions on other rate cuts.In general market is ahead....of actual important events. Pricing in the event is what usually takes place.Recent example Brexit spike then deflation after the event.

--- 帖子 #34450 ---
Great post! This can also be explained in a chess analogy. You can reasonably predict the next move or two of your opponents using these same techniques. However, the farther into the future you are predicting the less accurate your predictions become. You can add to your predictive models the tendencies of your opponents, gaining slightly more accurate predictions, but this will only take you so far. I often find myself using inductive reasoning to gauge the market and its sentiments and even model its future.

Excellent story. I work in logistics as a freight broker it has been so slow the last year that I've been actively seeking other things to do. A lot of companies run in a JIT (Just in Time) business model where they cut things to the bone and trucks become their warehouses and critical parts supplies that keep the factories running are rolling down the road if the truck breaks down or crashes it can shut a factory down. A car might say GM the Heartbeat of America , however the reality is a lot of the parts in that car are made in China like the engine,and the vehicle is assembled in an American factory. Some of the entire cars are being made in China like some of the Buicks, Cadillacs, Volvos. How about Tesla with their crazy stock run up last week? That's what the companies did with Obama's bailout money they built plants in China. All the major manufacturers are using cheap shit Chinese parts, and they sell cheap shit Chinese parts in their replacement parts supply chain. It takes two weeks to a month for a container ship to leave China and arrive in the USA. We'll definitely start seeing the ramifications of this soon as the container ports and manufacturing plants are shut down in China. It won't take long for the effects to start showing up here, so don't be surprised when car plants start shutting down in North America and Mexico. Even the major truck manufacturers use lots of Chinese parts in their "American iron" Chinese windshields, wiring harnesses, u-joints, brake parts, exhaust, etc. Cummin's has lots of parts made there, and they are inferior garbage. There were some local trucks a few years ago that were brand new Kenworth's with Cummin's engines in them and they got around the 50,000 thousand mile mark which is just getting broken in for a semi, and engines started blowing up. The crankshafts went out on them and the entire engine grenaded. Cummin's blamed their Chinese supplier who did not build the bearings to the proper specifications so they failed. It won't take long for vehicles to be left sitting in need of repair also as the part is not available. It also won't take long to start seeing empty spaces on store shelves either as practically all the shit on the shelves is made in China. So don't be surprised in the near future when there are shortages of cell phones, microwave ovens,etc. Perhaps we'll see a correction in this irrational exuberance that has been going on in world stock markets that have been soaring to higher highs on poor data and earnings ratios that don't add up.

--- 帖子 #34514 ---
The expectations are that the RBNZ will stay on hold. So, with a hold the most likely outcome, the focus will shift on to the forward guidance from the RBNZ. The NZD has been losing value against the AUD over recent days and there is a belief that New Zealand will be hit harder than Australia if/when the coronavirus impact grows. The thinking is that New Zealand is more vulnerable to the virus as trade makes up about 60% of New Zealand's economy compared to around 40% of Australia's economy. Tourism in New Zealand amounts to just under 6% of the economy, while Australia's tourism is around 3%. So, when the rate statement is released, the market focus will be on the forward guidance. If we get a dovish tilt, remember the BNZ and the ANZ GDP reductions: However, the outlook for New Zealand is tempered somewhat by the coronavirus outbreak expected to weigh on GDP figures. Both ANZ and BNZ have cut their growth forecasts for New Zealand's GDP projections

Its strange, it feels, that the governments all over the world try to make trading hard for people. The german government has passed a law which will change the way how wins and losses resulting from trading derivatives (which includes forex) are treated by taxation. At the moment it is common at the end of the year to offset wins and losses in order to pay a 25% tax on the wins or zero tax when the losses were larger than the wins. After the law will be introduced it will only be possible to offset max 10.000 EUR of losses. Example: A trader has earned 1.200.000 EUR in a year of trading and accumulated 1.000.000 EUR of losses. In the past That means he has to pay (1.200.000-1.000.000)*0.25=50.000 EUR tax His income will be 200.000-50.000=150.000 EUR 2021 (same numbers) Tax to pay (1.200.000-10.000)*0.25=297.500 EUR Income 200.000-297.500=-97.500 EUR Another goodie of the new law will be that a german trader has to pay tax for every win instantly and can get the money back at the end of the year via his annual tax declaration.A trader has earned 1.200.000 EUR in a year of trading and accumulated 1.000.000 EUR of losses.

--- 帖子 #33107 ---
I will consider these 7 indicators on this RISK-OFF &amp; RISK ON....INDEX That is the same idea as traders are driven by two emotions: RISK-OFF or FEAR and RISK-ON (GREED). In terms of Equities, too much fear can sink stocks well below where they should be. When traders get greedy, they can bid up stock prices way too far. This obviously affects the economy and consequently the Forex market. Idea being improved. New upgrades may occur soon. https://br.tradingview.com/chart/VIX/yHYeogM7/ ======================================= RISK-OFF &amp; RISK ON INDEX ================================================ 1. Stock Price Momentum: Measuring the Standard &amp; Poor's 500 Index ( S&amp;P 500 ) versus its 125-day moving average (MA) 2. Stock Price Strength: Calculating the number of stocks hitting 52-week highs versus those hitting 52-week lows on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) 3. Stock Price Breadth: Analyzing trading volumes in rising stocks against declining stocks 4. Put and Call Options: How much do put options lag behind call options, signifying greed, or surpass them, indicating fear 5. Junk Bond Demand: Gauging appetite for higher risk strategies by measuring the spread between yields on investment-grade bonds and junk bonds 6. Market Volatility: CNN measures the Chicago Board Options Exchange Volatility Index ( VIX ), concentrating on a 50-day MA 7. Safe Haven Demand: The difference in returns for stocks versus treasuries Each of these seven indicators is measured on a scale from 0 to 100 , with the index being computed by taking an equal-weighted average of each of them. A reading of 50 is deemed NEUTRAL . Above 50 signals the market with RISK-ON. (GREED) Below 50 , Signals the market with RISK-OFF (FEAR)

The Aortic Stenosis condition is found in up to 2% of the aging population - pretty common. It is called the Trans-aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) done under local anesthesia and sedation to allow opening of your left groin artery to place stents that go up the aortic valve with first ballooning open the valve then slipping a new artificial AV and the stents removed, groin artery stitch up and skin tissues to close up the opening. EURAUD Daily trade started on 20 Feb 2020 In harmonics(according to Scott Carney), the patterns will give you 2 opportunities 1. Reaction (Sudden or sharp move to target 1, 38.2% of AD) 2. --- 帖子 #35136 ---
Armenia’s 5-star care for quarantined citizens makes global headlines YEREVAN, MARCH 3, ARMENPRESS. Posh suites and a luxury hotel – these are the conditions that the Armenian authorities have provided for the 32 quarantined direct contacts of the first novel coronavirus patient. The direct contacts are quarantined at the Tsakhkadzor resort town’s previously defunct Golden Palace five-star hotel. PM Nikol Pashinyan had earlier said that those quarantined must be treated “like we would like our families to be treated” in such cases, and noted that the quarantined citizens will receive dignified conditions. And this move has already received global attention. “Being quarantined on suspicion of carrying a deadly contagious disease is quite an ordeal, but at least Armenia is making up for the hassle by placing coronavirus patients in a 5-star hotel”, writes RT. “In some countries, repatriated coronavirus patients are met with stones and threats, but in Armenia, they have so far received drastically different treatment”, the news agency wrote, posting the video shared by PM Nikol Pashinyan showing hazmat personnel handing out meals to the people in the luxury hotel suits. The Turkish NTV has also touched upon Armenia’s quarantine conditions, emphasizing that the Armenian premier has ordered a five-star quarantine condition for the persons. Armenia reported its first novel coronavirus case on March 1. The virus was confirmed in an Armenian man who traveled to Iran. He was hospitalized in Yerevan, while his direct contacts were taken to the Tsakhkadzor resort town’s previously defunct Golden Palace hotel. U.S. dollar n et long position falls in latest week Speculators reduced their bullish bets on the U.S. dollar in the latest week , according to calculations by Reuters and Commodity Futures Trading Commission data released on Friday. The value of the dollar's net long position, derived from net positions of International Monetary Market speculators in the yen, euro, British pound, Swiss franc and Canadian and Australian dollars , was $17.28 billion , in the week to March 3. That compares with a net long position of $21.21 billion the previous week. The Reuters calculation for the aggregate U.S. dollar position is derived from net positions of International Monetary speculators in the yen, euro, British pound, Swiss franc and Canadian and Australian dollars. EUR 12107 + JPY 4939 + AUD 3420 + CHF 0.424 = 20890 GBP (-2815 + CAD -0.790) = -3604 NET = 17285 BILLION Attached Image Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attached Image Attached Image Attached Image Attached Image Attached Image Attached Image

What is Exponential Moving Average - EMA? An exponential moving average (EMA) is a type of moving average (MA) that places a greater weight and significance on the most recent data points. The exponential moving average is also referred to as the exponentially weighted moving average. An exponentially weighted moving average reacts more significantly to recent price changes than a simple moving average (SMA), which applies an equal weight to all observations in the period. EMA puts more weight at present data hence less lagging.There is fine balance we need lag to keep us away from early entry but not too much as miss a trade by wide margin. EMA suits the best.Think of 8EMA as yellow in traffic light and 21 as green or red. 8 is "heads up" So If price is at R61 and 15 chart price crossed 8EMA heading to 21 I will be all eyes as possible trade option once cleared 21 Simple.Sure as always there will be losers but that's true on all systems. I like how AN is closing nice.

--- 帖子 #35460 ---
There are tons of questions to answer when the trader uses MAs. What MA, SMA, EMA, LWMA, TMA... ? What parameter, 3,5,12,21,50,100,200... ? Single MA, dual MA, triple MA, quadruple MA... ? Price cross MA, MA1 Cross MA2... ? What does price re-represented by MA(statistical representation) mean? What's the purpose of re-representing ohlc price with statistical MAs? What governs the choice of the chosen MA, calibration and usage? Basically what additional info MAs give that price doesn't? What additional info the trader seek that can't be found from price? And so on..... Mostly MAs are used without proper in-depth research, it's mere optical illusion(looks good to the eye) whether to pull the trigger or not - a psychological crutch.

In trading you never can answer a question with only a solution. It's relative market moment and how trader read charts. But taking a simple base ( separation between both MAs ) trader have adapt reading depending price behavior. For example I use a MA compression approach when happens a breakout and a simple MA cross + price above/below MAs if swing is a big parabolic movement. It's something you learn along the time. I use other MAs setup but at the end important is find one trader feel comfortable. Rules are always same. Only change chart clearness depending how setup shows every market moment This is an example how I read market. I use MAs + stoch but I use them in a different way as many do it. Basically I use stoch patterns with MA confirmation. And this helps me can anticipate movements and filter a lot of noise Anyway every trader use his own approach and to use pivots is right as others if trader uses right rules. Finally only important thing is trader feeling

I'd like to share my reflections trading weekly pivots on the last period and and listen to your comments. Weekly Pivot strategy has worked well for me in the last two years. In the latest months I suffered big losses making me doubt the strategy in itself. I've come to the conclusion that the strategy works very well when in the markets there is a "normal" volatility and conditions. In exceptional periods like this one when there's no mean reversion at all for a prolonged time, when we see 600-700 pips candles on H4 TF for EA and more than 1,000 pips on daily for the same pair, when we have a global average daily volatility calculated on the major 28 pairs amounting to 300 pips the method is suffering big. Even applying EMAs filters I find it risky and dangerous. All reasonable assumptions based on fundamentals no longer work and markets are driven by other irrational forces we cannot nor foresee neither control. The 80-20 rule says markets trend about 20% of the time and spends the other 80% grinding through trading ranges, therefore my view is that in times like the one we are living we should stop trading this method or as Davit and others already suggested lowering lot sizes and # of positions reducing activity to the minimum. As for myself I'll reduce trading weekly pivots to the bare minimum if not abstain totally until a sort of normality will be restored. Now is the time to pray and think of other values such as one's own health and that of the whole planet, I assure you that I live in Italy the situation is dramatic and constantly worsening. The world has always managed to overcome these difficulties and I am sure that it will succeed even this time even if the battle promises to be very hard. Best regards, Bubincka

In post#35,654 I entered a long position on a bullish bat pattern (AUDCAD) to collect target 1 (Reaction move). Most of the harmonic patterns will give you 2 opportunities which are called Reaction and Reversal. Between reaction and reversal, there is a Retest move. Below is an example of me catching this restest move on the same pair. A note for our health guys. Specifically OUR BACKS. I am a retired Professional Firefighter. Firefighting is not easy on the body , not whining , just comes with the territory. I suffered for years with severe lumbar region back pain and attributed my back pain to injuries I suffered while on the job. A young firefighter finally convinced me to go to a chiropractor. I went , and the results were an improvement which decreased my pain by about 40% , then I plateaued. However , it didn't get any worse either. THE MAJOR BREAKTHROUGH , for me , came when one of the Fire Dept's Mechanics advised me to see a well known OSTEOPATH in my city. Took me 3 months to get an appointment to see this man , who is now in his 60's. Peter ( his real name) , told me that he could make another significant reduction in my back pain , BUT , it was really going to hurt. Peter wasn't F%#kin KIDDING !!!! There is a muscle called the PSOAS MUSCLE , it connects to your spine and goes down through the groin area. Found out that my psoas muscle was severely tight and THAT WAS WHAT WAS ACTUALLY CAUSING MY BACK PAIN FOR ALL THOSE YEARS THAT I SUFFERED IMMENSELY. 2 BACK TO BACK TREATMENTS INITIALLY , and one a year for the past 3 years. PETER TOLD ME that the release of my psoas was about as close as a male can get to what a woman experiences at childbirth !!!!! I had tears pouring down my face !!!! THE MAIN CAUSE OF A TIGHT PSOAS MUSCLE IS SITTING !!!! Super painful , but , BEST THING I EVER DID FOR MY BACK !!! I "listen to my body" now. Finally , at age 57. I wait for help with heavy things that need lifting. Working out everyday again on a stationary bike and leg curls on a bench lying on my stomach to work the hamstrings , low weight , nice and slow , high repetitions , "listening to my body which tells me when to stop". Just my 2 cents worth guy's , but , it totally changed my life. While trading , I force myself to get up , walk around , then stretch before I sit down again. Numerous other firefighters and police officers have gone to this man and they have had the same results as me. --- 帖子 #34111 ---
Want to mention I risk more then average trader.You decide what % you feel comfortable There is slight hinder on goal achievement targets.Example if you have 5k account and you risk 2% max it will take very long time to reach 100% gain Sure it will be safer but much much longer. So the way I look at risk is Experience x time factor. I basically reached 100% on 5k margin in a week.Some takes a year.I can do that because I know my abilities but I dont recommend it. Risk is up to you but 10% 15% is common among experience traders.You need lots of screen time before risking a lot of money. Cheers When you gain experience you'll know where to go big and where to go small. Example last week AN reached below 100 all the way to teens.Well at teens that's where you go big.You were historic bottom.Does not come up often anyway there are situations where you should be more "riskier" As you gain experience and confidence in the markets risk should fluctuate based on trading location situation.So even if you are conservative you make a decision on size based on quality of the set up. Example UC at 45 short.That's where you dont hold back...Again you need screen time. Example from today I liked AN at 150 so went bigger then usual.Hope this helps, EC went smaller GC even less

--- 帖子 #36220 ---
[/highlight] Read the book again. "Most investors believe they know what is going to happen next. This causes traders to put too much weight on the outcome of the current trade, while not assessing their performance as a probability game that they are playing over time. This manifests itself in investors getting in too high and too low and causing them to react emotionally, with excessive fear or greed after a series of losses or wins." Fear of Losing The fear of losing when making a trade often has several consequences. Fear of loss tends to make a timer hesitant to execute his or her timing strategy. This can often lead to an inability to pull the trigger on new entries as well as on new exits. As a market timer, you know that you need to be decisive in taking action when your strategy dictates a new entry or exit, so when fear of loss holds you back from taking action, you also lose confidence in your ability to execute your timing strategy. This causes a lack of trust in the strategy, or more importantly, in your own ability to execute future signals. For example, if you doubt you will actually be able to exit your position when your strategy tells you to get out, then as a self-preservation mechanism, you will also choose not to get into a new trade. Thus begins analysis paralysis , where you are merely looking at new trades but not getting the proper reinforcement to pull the trigger. In fact, the reinforcement is negative and actually pulls you away from making a move. Looking deeper at why a timer cannot pull the trigger, a lack of confidence causes the timer to believe that by not trading, he is moving away from potential pain as opposed to moving toward future gain. No one likes losses, but the reality is, of course, that even the best professionals will lose. The key is that they will lose much less, which allows them to remain in the game, both financially and psychologically. The longer you can remain in the trading game with a sound timing strategy, the more likely you will start to experience a better run of trades that will take you out of any temporary trading slumps. When you're having trouble pulling the trigger, realize that you are worrying too much about results and are not focused on your execution process. By following a strategy that unemotionally tells you when to enter and exit the market, you can avoid the pitfalls caused by fear. Wealthy traders learned long ago that unemotional (non-discretionary) timing strategies prevent losses during emotional times in the market. They know the strategies work, so they put aside their fears and make the trades. And remember, you must be able to take a loss. Consider them a part of trading. If you cannot, you will not be around for the big gains because you will be on the sidelines guarding your capital against that potential loss. Every trade you take has the potential to become a loss, so get used to this reality and take every buy and sell signal. That way, when the next big trend starts, you will be onboard and profit from it." I lost money good deal like many others on virus spike some on this thread got destroyed by it both financially and mentally some continuing with genuine understanding that plenty of time left to catch up and regain and make profit for the year. My response has been intense focus on execution and my winning % has gone up exponentially. My attitude is on high gear like I said before 1 spike can't destroy or wipe out 8 years of trading experience! You must trust yourself! What's life without real challenge?For me to achieve ultimate success in trading is worth pursing despite of adds. At this junction in my life there is no option but success. thank you, look at my stop this way.... my primary basis for entry was price having moved above daily pivot I normally use the logic that if my reason for entry is wrong I should be out of the trade therefore, if I can target good entry points close to my reason for entry then my stops should ordinarily be small. however, placing it immediately below pivot when the entry is so close to pivot is simply too tight initially, so I took into account to small dip made below pivot and set my stop under that. Such that if it is hit, the following conditions are true: it's below pivot and a new recent low price = no reason to still be long above pivot and a small stop so I don't get sucked into draw down. I normally move my stop to BE fairly quickly as the trade progresses. regards

--- 帖子 #36522 ---
Well, at the moment we do have irregular market conditions so its use is somewhat lessened, for example today every USD pair has blown right through the 5 day ADR ... Normally however it does show you the average range of trades over the last 5 days so if you are in a trading in a smooth market (if there is such a thing anymore!) the idea of this indi is you can see if your pair is approaching the distance of the ADR, so you should pay attention to possibly getting out of that trade (unless you are trading swings of more than one day of course). I find it easier to visually picture the ADR with this than to look at the old number in the top right corner and have to measure that number of pips on my chart.

--- 帖子 #36529 ---
For me it's one of those indis that you can use but is not necessary. However, for short term trading it can be useful. As far as resistance and support it is useless since the prices in which it starts the day are not set to stay. Both move depending on actual price movement of pair. Example: Start of day lets say top price is 1000 bottom 500 and adr is 200, if price only move up once 200 pip adr reached prices will be at 1200 and 700 on the ADR Marker not the original 1000 and 500. So be careful with that. One good feature is that you can visually see an ADR Marker that you can use once price heads strongly towards it. Usually, once close enough, it will reach it. And once it overshoots it, you can do a quick scalp back towards ADR. Check today UC. Again usually, just like any other factor in forex...Anything Can Happen.

--- 帖子 #36530 ---

Nostromo Pivots to keep chart clean and RN to gauge in between pivots. Added MA for visual, but will give it a go for now. I want to train my eyes to see these things without use of indi.

--- 帖子 #36595 ---
Oil Contracts expire every month unless you are setup with your broker to have your contracts rollover to the new month your trade will be closed whether you are in a profit or a loss. If you're trading CFD's on Oil in an FX account depending on your broker it may close on you 1 or 2 days prior to the CME expiration. Here's a link to CME. https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/ene...r_futures.html Don't get mad at your broker, take the time to understand the instrument you are trading. Contact them and ask what their policy is on close dates. They may be 2 days ahead as next Tuesday is the day so that would be why your position was closed on you this Friday. They will probably provide you with a calendar so you know. Here is FXCM 's calendar. https://www.fxcm.com/markets/cfd-expirations/

I am going to log off soon but food for thought Why is it Impossible for the Market to Move the Exact Same Way Twice? For this new pin bar to move exactly the same as how the previous pin bar did, it would have to have exactly the same traders in the market with exactly the same size orders. The same traders would have to be getting in and out with exactly the same size orders at precisely the same time, to the exact moment. They would have to be exchanging their orders to the exact same people on the exact same platforms to make this new pin bar move in the exact same way. Obviously this is impossible! Why back testing is faulty logic. “Every Moment in The Market is Unique” Mark Douglas Why I love Pivots? Because they are constant irregardless of history.

--- 帖子 #36923 ---
Kathy Lien Tomorrow’s U.S. non-farm payrolls report is expected to be the worst ever. Economists believe that more than 21 million jobs were lost in the month of April, which would drive the unemployment rate up to 16%. The last time the jobless rate was in the double digits was in 1983, just after the 1980s recession. Historic job losses should drive currencies and equities lower, but with everyone looking for an ugly report, how much impact will it really have on the markets? Expectations are one thing, but price action is another. Taking a look at currencies, the persistent sell-off in USD/JPY over the past few weeks tell us that forex traders have positioned for a weak report and, while staggering job losses could still drive USD/JPY lower, the sell-off may be limited if the data doesn’t veer far away from expectations. However, equities and 10-year Treasury yields are hovering near one-month highs, which suggests that traders in those markets are either looking past April data or aren’t prepared for a weak release. We’d like to think that it’s the former since the evidence of staggering job losses are everywhere, but given that stocks and Treasury yields are up over the past month, even a modestly weaker report could send equities tumbling lower. For currencies, this means there’s scope for broad gains for the Japanese Yen and Swiss Franc and extended losses for USD/JPY. Keep an eye on average hourly earnings because that’s where the big surprise could be. Economists expect earnings growth to hold steady at 0.4% and rise from 3.1% to 3.3% year over year. This is difficult to fathom considering widespread reports of companies keeping employees on payroll but cutting salaries. If wage growth turns negative and the rest of the jobs report is in line, it could be enough to send equities and currencies sharply lower. In what scenario could stocks and USD/JPY rise? If every part of Friday’s labor market number is in line with expectations – that means stronger wage growth, an unemployment rate of 16%, 21 million jobs lost and no revisions to March data – the markets could rally. The numbers could also be so weak that we see a sharp sell-off that triggers a vigorous recovery as investors think that’s the worst of it and move on. So in a nutshell, the best way to trade NFPs is to either sell ahead of the report and close before or wait for the numbers to be released, prices to stabilize and see what becomes the real move of the day.

Me personally I trade small but work on quick get in, get out, get on with life. Basically waited for move to stop and sold dollar for a quick 8% additional gain for the week. All this while I had breakfast then shaved. Some days trades take longer to develop but when weeks like this one that PPE is working like clockwork...you stay patient, wait for the market to bring the trade to you. Get in...get out...get on with life. Do not fall in the trap of "could've held...left money on the table...closed too early" because that is faulty thinking. All you are doing is programing your mind to, first of all, not see the great trade made and by doing so you discredit the system and your ability to follow it and second, think in terms of the market owes you. This brings about disasterous results because it is when bad trade habits are followed like revenge trade, greed and anger. Trading should be emotionless and mechanical. I get out when I get out and like this week I probably could have made an additional 1000 pips had I held. But I traded how I wanted and yes trades went to where I expected and double...but I made my goals and more. Holding at times, has made me lose money I had already earned, or worse kept me on DD and waiting for days or weeks to close at loss or less money than before. So I set my goal, once reached I am done. Again weeks like this one, you just take advantage of it, because usually one week it nothing works, so you compensate...that's all. Have a great weekend...and Happy Mothers Day to all Moms ever...

--- 帖子 #37005 ---
From years of successful trading using pivots. Trading from the outer levels is nothing more then swing failure/mean reversion. You also get to see price structure and patterns forming that lead to higher probability trades, ie an “edge”. Trading from the mean there is no edge. There is nothing to tell you which way its going to go. So you’ll most likely burn thru more capital with failed trades before a direction is made.

--- 帖子 #37173 ---
This system could easily be traded using line chart. I have analized charts on ocassions using line, and it works just fine. It takes away the illusion of red sell, green buy, hence why I use white candles, and a small candle size, because it is the closest to a line chart. The illusion of red and green has everything to do with psychology. We program our mind with everything...even what we might consider irrelevant. We tend to do away with the obvious things that affect trading psychology like indicators, revenge trading, motivational stuff...etc but we usually do not consider the hidden ones, the ones that might cause us more trouble. I don't have the answer as to what Price action might be; however, I use structure at a price point when making my decision. Ex. price in relation to pivot, psychological levels such as 00...250...500...750, News, market structure, ADR and price...yes price (is it at a bargain, is it too high ex. USDMXN is so high it cannot survive at that price for too long. Once it plummets, UC will go along the ride and of course WTIUSD will climb once again.) Fiinally line chart might have one lose so called top or bottom but it would eliminate a lot of early entries.

--- 帖子 #37176 ---
The price movements on the market always follow the same pattern. You can imagine it like that. The price is constantly oscillating. The price swings from one extreme to the next. Our task is to recognize and act on these extremes early on. This happens very often at the extreme pivot points from 61 and higher. When these extremes are reached, the market pulls back in the direction of its initial movement like an extremely stretched rubber band. This oscillation takes place in every time frame. For the weekly pivot points, the time frames 30 min to 1 h are very suitable. The price action takes place at the extremes. The price action that takes place is due to the stop loss, buy or sell orders of other traders that are often located there. From a purely technical point of view, the fundamental messages also play an important role. That's why what Davit keeps saying is very important. When there is one of those Cryptosurf low hanging fruit, late week markup then usually trades work out well, especially when closest to WP. Just like late Friday pairs usually head towards following week WP. For those who will ask Nostromo pivots plots future pivots. That is what I use it for. That is why at times my best trades are at the beginning of the week. Problem has been that once those trades work out I place another trade...big mistake. Instead I should wait for price to be at key pivots then place trade, which is usually Wed - Fri. Once I get this under control I can get back to trading first two weeks then be done for the month. Get in, get out, get on with life.

That hurts. Maybe Egbert has an idea. If your entries where better then your exits as is would be good. For my liking, you have way too many indicators. Price is bound to hit one of them, maybe you might think it is a good entry point or exit because it hit it...but if you are trading Davit Pivot trading just keep weekly pivots. Price will eventually go from one pivot to the next...sooner or later it will. With just pivots one is more inclined to allow price move and head towards pivot. Just keep pivots, ADR and look at market structure. This is for everyone including me. Take your image for example...price ran from you and surely entered as it ran up. Price eventually (on a Friday of course) came back to where price had stalled for a while. That should have been a clue for you to exit. Especially since price moved to almost 100R ran back quickly to 38R, that is 3 pivots lower, that is good for a weeks worth and you got it in a few hours. Also, if you study your chart closely, you have 5 indicators plus market structure in that zone...why would you not take profit there. If anything, why would you have so many indicators if you are not going to listen to them? Maybe it's hindsight, but if you do not learn from this you will commit the same mistakes and the goal is to identify the trading errors, adjust mentally, and commit to doing it mechanically. Notice I did not say doing it right, I said mechanically. It might work some times and others it won´t but in a larger series of trades it will reward you. Which is what you are looking for.

--- 帖子 #37419 ---
I have gone back to what has worked for me best. I stopped reading around FF and every other news and noises all over the internet. Decided to once again just study my charts, do my analysis and place my trades. When looking at others I tend to pay more attention to what my bias is already and not even consider those with opposing bias, so why bother. Some will say buy, some will say sell, so I will just go with my system and analysis. This is my plan. * Have just a handful of news and information sites to keep up-to-date with current events. No analysis, trade predictions and/or signals. * Will use Daily to set ranges for week. * Analyze trades on 4hr, place trades on 1hr, if scalping like this week, use 5M exclusively. * Limit number of pairs watched and pairs traded. * PPE * Study and use news for the week. * Pay attention to following weeks news. * Follow the system, follow the plan, follow my gut instinct. * Use common sense. * Will not improve what is working, and not deviate from what works. I have found that while placing trades others have analyzed I can win or lose, but mostly lose because it might not be based on rules I have set for myself and cannot manage adequately. So if those are the odds and outcome, why not just trade based on my system? Besides if trading a profitable system odds are that even when losing some trades it will eventually, in a series of trades, be profitable. Truth is, there is nothing more satisfying than seeing your trade develop and end in profit. It creates victories, and those victories...memories, and those memories reinforces behaviour conducive to repeating the process. Habits are created by repeated behaviour. And following a working plan, a profitable plan, repeatedly creates a winning habit, even if your trades ends in lose. I decided on trading just AU this week, trading less but more precise trades. I spent the early part scalping the pair gaining 200+ pips. It was stressful but since it was on a range I took what the market gave. Today I waited for news, this was my trade for the week. Traded the AU long till WP, now common sense was easy on this one, since RN 69000 was just under WP, and pair had not been able to stay past either. No AU news (although CAD affects it, it was not strong enough), there was no fundamental reason for it to break WP or 69000. closed long at Pivot and went short for a ride. Did not foresee it going so short but rode it 6870, my tp was 6860. Classic pump then dump on a Friday. Pair was slowly climbing all night so that it can bring it back down to where it started. These are market structures and moves that one burns into our memory for future use. I had great days only to give back some, so I set out to adjust my mental state, my trading plan, and my habits. This is my business, this is my career, I had to take drastic measures immediately before I develop bad trading habits. Since I take this serious, I had to get serious with it. Now looking forward to next week and putting in place the plan. Enjoy your weekend.

Kevin Schwantz Kevin Schwantz's racing career is filled with the kind of extremely painful injuries that would have sidelined almost anyone else. Two great examples: in 1992, he dislocated his hip and broke his left forearm during a race at Assen. After having a plate put in his arm to hold it together and having a custom cast made, he was back on the bike racing within two weeks. Then, in 1994, Schwantz had what he reckons was the defining moment of his career, at Donington Park in the UK. Although Schwantz had won the 1993 World Championship title, 1994 was anything but a sure thing.With his left wrist in a cast from a crash a few races prior, Schwantz had a huge high-side during qualifying that didn't break anything new, but exacerbated the pain of the earlier injury. Schwantz went on to win that 1994 500cc Donington Park race by beating Mick Doohan . Oh, did we mention that he did it one-handed? The left wrist kept getting tingly and numb, so Schwantz had to keep shaking it whenever he reached a safe point to do so on track. It was the last time he'd ever win a GP race--but quite possibly also his best win ever. Inserted Video

--- 帖子 #37858 ---
GM NLtrader, This question was brought up years ago here in the early days of this Pivot Thread. No one could figure it out (including Davit) and the other high impact traders here at the time. I was trying to calculate it myself with no real accurate formula hoping to "save the day" ! No one here could get to the author(s) of the Indicator as well. Davit at the time, explained his old standard approach by outlining the H and L of the Week TF and draw a line through the middle making it the Fib 50%. Then, just go to the lower TFs to calculate the width of the extremes using the Fibonacci MT4 function here. Most recently in March 2020, Davit emphasized the importance of watching the ADR% turning Red and to see whether the 1 Day ADR was at least half of Today ADR signaling a possible coming Reversal or Swing of the PA. In general, I try to follow the wisdom of trying not to take a new trade 1 hour before major news or the actual NYO - and then, not before 1 to 2 hours afterwards in general - unless you are Scalping the PA response with small TP trades to get-in and get-out ! I hope this helps you and the others here. Regard and GM to all ! DJ

--- 帖子 #37862 ---
there are several different calculations by different traders. the calculation in Davit template post #1 and Post#2 chart is as follows: the average ADRavg is the sum (ADR1+ADR5+ADR10+ADR20) divide by 4. the ADR% is the current Today ADR divided by the ADRavg there will some discrepancy because some brokers have the Sunday New York candle and this is usually very small. some indicator has the options to exclude the Sunday candle.

--- 帖子 #38015 ---
Your method seems sound but i think its the candle you used to confirm bullish on a monthly pivot. With monthly pivots one should look for a clear weekly candle close above the pivot in order to consider it a bullish move. H4 is much to small and it looked more like a rejection by the monthly pivot. I always use the main pivot points from 3 different timeframes. Smaller pivot, Large pivot, Larger pivot. I look for a break of the larger pivot with a close of the next lower timeframe candle above/below the larger pivot. Heres an example of what I mean. In this case break of larger pivot is monthly while the weekly is the smaller pivot and largest pivot is yearly(i didnt plot yearly pivots) on the following Silver chart: Attached Image (click to enlarge) Also its best to do this after a trend to get a nice proper reversal. Your USDX looked like a long trade after a bull run which is not ideal

when you see this.Trade it.Its my favorite range market situation. "safest" trades are IMO commodity pairs against eachother. AC NC AN I made shitload trading this set up. If move is 20-30 pips or less then you increase lot size to compensate smaller moves. 2lots at 20pip move is 40pips on 1lot.Bigger the move smaller relative lot size.Small moves bigger lots.This eliminates the concept that you need 70-100pip moves to make money.You dont.You increase position size on smaller moves hence any day is good day to trade.

Hi. It's my first post in this thread. First of all I want to thank Davit for his great thread and also other active traders here. I've learned lots of things here. I'm trying to understand the system. So far this is what I've understood: 1- Every week we try to understand which currency is probably the weakest and strongest based on fundamentals 2- Then with the correct mindset we try to find pair which have the most potential 3- Then we look at the charts to find out which pairs are going to be exhausted and turn back near key pivot points (specially between R61-R100) 4- Also we use ADR to help us find probable exhaustions better 5- Then we look at price action to confirm our findings (any sign of weakness in the current short term trend) using patterns, candlesticks, volume, and/or momentum analysis (which can probably lead to a reversal) 6- When we are confident that the price hits an important resistance or support and cannot go beyond and is going back, we enter our trade towards the center Pivot and away from the turning point pivots Any comments would be appreciated. Best Regards. By the way, I took these two trades today based on the steps I mentioned before.

Hi traders, One of the great things I discovered while I was reading the "Bird Watching In Lion Country" was the meaning of margin and leverage. Dirk du Toit, the author, explains nicely how the concept of let "your profits run and cut your losses" is a misleading advice for many traders. He also suggests the opposite and after I reread the phrase and thought about it, my aha moment triggered. This is really game changing. I do not suggest anyone who read my post here to go and enter trades without stop losses, but what I understood from the book is that you should have enough capital and margin left in your account to give your trades enough breathing room to show whether they are going to work or not before being stopped out too soon. Also you should understand that anything can happen and be ready for the worst scenario (another rational reason why to risk very small percent of your account in each trade at least during the entry point). Thanks Davit for sharing with us such a great book. Thanks a million for being an honest, selfless human. Last week I made a mistake and entered a trade at late hours before market close. The setup was not perfect and the reason why I took the trade was merely overconfidence (I had 6 consecutive wins in a row, shame on me). However, I respected one thing, I traded only 1/5 of my normal size. I planned to enter more when the high of the candle was broken. Things didn't go well and the week ended with my negative trade still open (another mistake). Today, When I saw the price bounced back from S38 I took the opportunity and opened another 1/5 at much better price and could close the trade for 1% profit. The point is that I could easily tolerate nearly 60 pips loss with no more than 1% negative effect on my account.

--- 帖子 #38454 ---
Thanks Egbert. Volatility is the most important factor for speculators . However, this simple fact is ignored by most traders. I think brokers purposefully misdirect the newcomers. Everybody is talking about liquidity and trading volume and how pairs like EURUSD are safe because of liquidity and low spread. But none of the marketing experts in this industry is talking about range of movement. When a pair doesn't move we cannot make money simple as that. Therefore, I think trading volatile pairs with wider spreads are a lot safer than trading liquid pairs with narrow spread and narrow movement range. Moreover, there is another ugly truth that I think brokers don't want us to realize. If you want to make money trading pairs like EURUSD you need much more leverage to compensate for the lack of volatility and that is exactly what they want.

Hi everybody, another win on EN 1.70%. This is the end of my first month trading Pivot Points seriously. Things I discovered so far after 1 month of live trading and 2 months of paper trading: 1- Davit is a great teacher and his system has amazingly high win/loss ratio 2- All A+ trades I took where near R/S78 and to me above R/S100 is a good place to accept that you were wrong and close the trade 3- I found that when there is a confluence of pivots and perfect round numbers the chance of reversals are higher 4- If there is a recent important horizontal S/R the chance increases even further 5- If the momentum decreases near pivots the chance of reversal increases way more higher (I only use price action to study momentum like when the candles start to get smaller, swings start to travel the previous distance with much less angle, and much more time and . . .) 5- If the reversal is in line with daily trend the chance is even higher (Honestly I didn't make things complicated for myself and ignored the daily trend) 6- As Davit said AUD,CAD,NZD are gold nuggets (for example if I see that EUR is getting weaker I prefer to trade EA,EN, and EC more than EU) 7- Studying the charts of Davit and other great minds here like Egbert is mind opening Still struggling to learn fundamental analysis and news analysis and harmonic pattern recognition. But I'll get over it eventually. As MD said " All change is the function of desire ". Best Regards

--- 帖子 #38471 ---
Thanks a lot Ekim and congratulations for having sharp eyes and deep understanding just by looking at my trades. You've just pointed to my biggest weakness. Large lot sizes has been my main weakness. Next week I'm going to to do something about it. I plan to enter in four stages: stage one two 0.01 lots if the candle in m15 is in my favor I enter 2 more 0.01 and then one more after the third candle for the total of 0.05. If the price goes towards the R/S 78 I'll enter two more there. If it goes further towards R/S 100 I enter two more at the middle point of R/S 78-100. (Now I have 0.06 lot) Eventually if it reaches R/S 100 I'll enter four more there. (Now I have 0.1 lot) Now I have my biggest position near my stop loss (a close of two M30 candles above/below R/S100 or 5% whichever happens first). I think in this way I'm going to have both flexibility and risk management at the same time. The only downside to this method that I'm going to use for my next 30 trades is that the losers can be larger than winners. However, there are several reasons that I think this method is not very bad: 1- Davit method has a very high win/loss ratio so even if the losing trades are two times the wining ones I'm still making money 2- Pivot Trading are reversal trading in nature. Therefore there is a good possibility that you sell a top and that top turns out to be the start of a massive reversal trend and goes for hundreds of pips. So my entering method makes me benefit from that move nicely because I can close 80% of my positions and keep the ones I have at the top and ride the trend and collect pips. 3- My biggest position is near my stop loss so if I'm right I'm going to win big because I entered at the best price possible but if I lose I don't lose much because my biggest position was near the stop loss. 4- The same is true for wining trades. I enter 2 + 2 + 1 if the last one loses, my account won't take a lot of damage because the last one was the smallest in size. I want to thank Davit again for building such a great community here. I want to thank all great traders here for sharing their ideas and helping people like me especially Egbert for sharing his views on everything especially fundamental analysis (I became familiar with AK with the indirect help of Egbert and I'm learning a lot since) I also want to thank GE for directing me to MD's "How to Think Like a Professional Trader" series. It is a gem. Have a great weekend Best Regards

--- 帖子 #38508 ---
Same was here. However, one simple mindset changed everything for me 12 years ago when I accidentally read an article about how some gamblers could make fortunes using a loaded dice. Every edge needs large enough sample size to show itself. For that I need to survive long enough. For example a casino has a slight edge over the gamblers but it has large enough initial capital to tolerate the losses until its edge show itself in the long run. What I did to train my brain back then was tossing coins and adding 1.5 to my account when it was head and subtracting 1 when it was tails. I didn't have an edge in win/loss ratios but my wins were 1.5 times larger. As you can expect I was able to grow my account on paper. The interesting part though was the drawdown. Sometimes I got 8 or even 10 tails in a row. I entered the results into an Excel spreadsheet and plotted an equity curve. But after 100 to 1000 tosses the account was consistently growing. After that I changed the experiment I made a loaded dice and tried the same thing but with equal sizes for wins and losses. Positive 1 for even numbers and negative 1 for odd numbers. The dice was slightly heavier on one side that made number 4 to happen more frequently than 1/6th of the times. The results were the same as before but drawdowns were larger and the curve wasn't as smooth but when I tossed it 1000 times (I literally was that crazy and had free time) the curve became smooth and when I zoomed out it became smoother even more as if there was not any drawdowns. That was my aha moment. By the way you can make yourself a loaded dice using the following article but don't make it too much loaded just enough to have a slight edge. https://www.wikihow.com/Load-Dice Best Regards

--- 帖子 #38592 ---
Hi, Pivoteers. As I continue my studying an interesting concept is forming in my mind. I like to share it here. I don't know it's true but the more I absorb knowledge the more convincing the concept is becoming. From the little knowledge I've absorbed so far I've come to the conclusion that all we do as traders is finding anomalies and trying to position ourselves towards the norm or equilibrium. The interesting point is that we do it in all kinds of analysis technical or fundamental. Anything which is far from normal can be considered as an opportunity because nature is somehow likes it. It hates chaos and whenever something is going out of the boundaries of normal behavior forces of nature push it back. If the price goes far from the pivot it comes back If the price goes more than its average ADR it comes back If the inflation, unemployment, growth are far from the average rates something will happen soon to get them back to normal Everything is about being normal and evading chaos. I'm fascinated by the accuracy of Fibonacci numbers. I know the relationship between these numbers and price reversals is considered as correlation but something is telling me that what if the relationship is cause and effect. I know it sounds silly and there are lots of fundamental factors behind the price but what if the world is made in a way that these factors happen at certain times. Fibonacci numbers seem random but evidence shows otherwise but why are a set of numbers highly correlated to certain behaviors?

There is more to it and I covered this here many times. Its not about how many pips but size of the position. When I think its not going to move much I increase position size so 10pips at 3lots example is roughly 550 dollars but if I am shooting longer pips I reduce position to 2lots or less.Idea is aiming certain number irregardless of pip distance. Hope this helps why to me its pointless how long you hold .Its the weight of the position that counts.

On the topic of numerical law's I watched a documentary recently on Bendford's law. You can see how almost numbers in everything abide by this law(finances, populations, even volcano sizes). Auditors use it to detect fraud in data. The universe will always abide by certain law's, even if they seem random- they are not! Really interesting stuff. Fibonacci's will always have significance in FX, since there will always be a battle between buyers and sellers on every level. Basically what I'm trying to say that randomness is a planned construct of the universe, so take from it what you will. Just a cool weekend thought

Hi guys There was an interesting PM regarding COT report.Is it important? Obviously there are many ways to trade and I am not going to say I am correct or my way is best but I can share what I think based on 10yr experience trading forex. COT report,Volume are things that are not substantive to base trading decisions because it takes only one or two major bank to wipe out all Cot positions in fact often is the case more small fish buying opposite prices get pushed.You can think of smart money VS damn money What you should focus is Pivots Price Events Pivots=structure of the market often corresponding support and resistance levels Price=encompassing sentiment.One can learn great deal by just watching prices move.Where it stops where it ranges etc.Did not mention price action since I believe its over played idea.One should be able to make money even with line price without any candles.Dont ask me why I think so its just something I noticed over the years... Events=The engine behind the market.Pay attention to it.You'll learn more from events reactions then from books. Well no magic formula.Everything comes down to paying attention. When you hear a great pianist playing you get carried away thinking he/she has tremendous talent....maybe so but what you dont see years and years of practicing as much as 8-10hrs every day.Well I had weeks that I slept 3-4 hrs a night because I wanted to be up on key events and wanted to make money and have done this often and still do.Too much effort? You bet but that's what it takes commitment to succeed

#Davit Just some food for thought regarding the Angleator, (13/34=0.382)- By default Then you tried 8 on the TDI. (8/34=0.235) And you said that 23.6 does not have any meaning, why then go from 13 to 8 period? The only reason I can see was to catch the move early, hence the 8 period on the TDI. The draw back was that the Angleator will cycle through "price action" to fast. ( uptrend, down trend ,uptrend, down trend....) If one would change from 13 to 8 period. Instead one must get price action on the Angleator to respond quicker BUT keep the uptrend or down trend(above 50 or below 50) according to market conditions? You said way back that its time to leave the Angleator behind and trade without it, you where loosing to much pips. Please, I'm not attacking you, just sharing my thoughts on something great. THE QUESTION WOULD BE HOW DOES ONE CHANGE PRICE ACTIONS RESPONSE (ON THE ANGLEATOR) AND NOT THE TREND? PLEASE DO NOT THINK I WANT TO RE-INVENT OUR WAY OF TRADING.

I get PM's all the time people asking how I do it etc.No secret really. Every Saturday I go over the calendar in detail.Draw a rough idea where prices may go.Example CAD rate is on Weds. Either market dumps CAD until rate decision or buys up then dumps after.So that's on my list to monitor.Trades will be placed accordingly how market decides to move CAD Every red news is gone over. Homework done confident week starts trades are placed according to system.Its as simple as that.When I started this thread here very few threads, traders actually placed any importance to Events on calendar.Noticed lot of them do now. I also see lot of them started placing pivots on their charts.Its obvious this thread has had great influence here and elsewhere. Lets make that next week

--- 帖子 #38926 ---
Hi All I have been trying to sort out my risk based on a cash amount per batch trade, so i wanted to get things even as best i could My first stage is to match cost per pip across all base currencies, i have worked it out in GBP as i am UK so i took EG as it has a cost per pip of £1 with a £0.10 lot size I got it as close as possible but not exact but im sure it will be close enough or at least many times better than it is, so excluding leverage all below lotsizes will roughly be £1 per pip XXX/GBP = 0.10 XXX/USD = 0.14 XXX/CAD = 0.18 XXX/JPY = 0.15 XXX/AUD = 0.19 XXX/NZD = 0.20 XXX/CHF = 0.13 So if we are breaking our entries into 10 peices we can use the above lot sizes and say 500 pips on each currency will now roughly be the same loss or profit on any pair Whereas before using 10 entries with the same lotsize of 0.10, 500 pips on EG would have a value of £500 profit but 500 pips on say EN would only be £250 profit, this way they will both be around the same

Hi Guys , does it seem reasonable that a spike with one Broker would not be seen with another Broker simply due to the positioning of a Broker's clientele on a particular currency pair ? Seems reasonable to me. As MD stated in one of his video's , a particular move in a currency pair during one hour can be totally different in the next hour simply due to the fact that an entirely different set of traders are now in the marketplace with a totally different perspective. I'm not stating anything that us trader's don't already know. To the best of my recollection , Oanda , my Broker , has never been prosecuted in a lawsuit , ever , and they have always served me well. In fact , due to a funding glitch of my account on Oanda's part in the amount of $6000.00 CAD , which I lost. Oanda admitted their mistake , apologized , and reimbursed my account the total amount. The transaction took 6 weeks to resolve, however , I was very happy with the outcome. I stand by Oanda , they have served me well. Just passing along info to fellow traders worthy of consideration , imo. Sincerely GE

I am going to share valuable tip about how to use Oscillators properly. Most Oscillators used by Retail traders are erroneous and result losing trades such as shorting above 70 line or buying below 30! DON'T DO THIS! Instead watch Oscillator turn around 1st from 70 or higher level come back 70 level pointing south+with red candles on chart then you got higher probability trades. This is key using oscillator properly because price can stay above 70 for LOOONG TIME or below 30 LOOONG time! resulting massive DD

Hi Don, I don't really use MT4 to trade anymore as Currencies only make up approx 30% of my trading these days but loaded it up and used what should be mostly Davits. The important point is Davits pivot system is a return to the mean against weekly range expectations which is better used in pairs that is consolidating. I have attached my Stnd TradingView chart which has a Weekly Range deviation of 1,2 and 3 over a 21 period. The 3rd deviation should mostly always match with Davits 78 area. With DAVITS trading style you're looking for RANGE OVEREXTENSIONS, PRICE, AND STRUCTURE trading into the over-extended range to what you think should hold. The rest for success will be based on your experience, emotional ability, news awareness, entries, and the scale of your trade leverage. The range is used in my trading but my trading is mostly done in identify volume moves, liquidity areas, inefficient pricing leading into longer-term areas. M charts will always be a mix of these trying to tell the story of what I am seeing. Hope this helps. Good luck with your trading.

--- 帖子 #39736 ---
Keep fundies in mind..... Euro hit a year to date low against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday after quietly trending lower for the past 5 weeks. Economic performance and monetary policy direction are the two most important drivers of currency flows and in the case of euro, both have been calling for further weakness. #EUR/USD consolidated above 1.1550 for more than a week before finally breaking lower but even with today’s move, it is not a clear break as the new low was only a few pips below last week’s low. For EUR/USD to sink to the next support level on the 1.13 handle, the pair needs a solid break of the psychologically significant 1.15 level. On a fundamental basis, there are plenty of reasons for the EUR/USD to underperform. There’s been a string of data disappointments from Germany and the Eurozone. PMI, factory orders, industrial production and today’s ZEW survey missed expectations. Investors are worried about the impact of rising energy costs and supply chain bottlenecks on corporate profitability. On a monetary policy basis, the European Central Bank reduced PEPP purchases but their warnings against tightening too soon have investors looking for a rate hike in late 2023. Throughout this monetary policy cycle, the ECB lagged behind its peers and while they cut PEPP before the Federal Reserve tapered asset purchases, the Fed will surely lift interest rates before the ECB. So not only is EUR/USD pressured by softer data and a dovish central bank but investors are bidding the greenback higher ahead of next month’s Fed meeting where a taper announcement is expected. Euro is weak against the dollar but its underperformance is the most dramatic against sterling, the Australian and New Zealand dollars. EUR/GBP is down more than 2% from its September high, EUR/AUD lost value 8 out of the last 9 trading days while EUR/CAD declined 15 out the last 16 trading days. Tomorrow’s Eurozone industrial production report should keep the downtrend intact as the decline in German industrial production signals weakness.

--- 帖子 #39799 ---
Price action supported by fundamentals........2 parts of this 3 part system. Remember, pivots are just lines in the sand. This system can be used both counter trend and with the trend. The pivot element works best in ranging markets and with ranging pairs. However, you can look at a higher TF chart and spot a strong trend. Price is still close to WPP at market open on Sunday night. Strong trends....simply go with the tend away from the WPP, with the stop 30-50 pips above/below WPP. You can also look at previous week history and on these strong trending pairs, you see they have not gone above/below WPP for 3-4 weeks in a row. Trade that until it stops, once it stops, it will more than likely range again and respect the 61-100 zone(s)

--- 帖子 #39920 ---
Difference of averaging in vs adding to losing position. Lot of people get this wrong. Adding to losing position when you are committed fully into position and you are in red then add more lots to break even or minimize losses more or less like martingale.This is dangerous and not recommended. I recommend averaging in meaning you dont commit fully to position and slowly add remaining lots hence full committed lot is spaced out.

--- 帖子 #40523 ---
Past results are not indictive of future performance. But I've personally been trading this system for over a year profitably. I've actually transitioned into using Prop money. Without knowing completely. I can already see what you are trying to get "at". The thing with this system is even if I had 3 years of backtest data it would be worthless too you. 1. You don't trade like I do. You won't execute the exact way I executed because the execution is ever changing based on Technical and Fundamental reasons 2. The same Geo-Political environment that "created" that set of data. Doesn't EXIST anymore its ever changing. That is why "backtesting" is for the birds. Those market participants aren't the SAME ones today impacting price. So its practically useless. The strategy is more a "framework". to use against Price action and Fundamental Analysis. This is the KEY reason why all these EA's getting touted around die off just as fast as they come around. Because those market variables change. This strategy requires price action analysis and NEWS/Fundamental analysis. Things that will not and cannot be replicated in the future.

--- 帖子 #40541 ---
I use the middle pivots only since they are the most powerful pivot. Also I use them for sentiment to trade trend reversals. Not really for support and resistance. What is more powerful than a levels ability to hold is the market's search for a level(fair price and advantageous price). This is why all my trades are the same. I wait for a trend to form. Then wait for it to end in a balance rotation for the whole session(intrady session, day session, week session etc), then if the session ends in a balance(range) when price moves out of the range and is on the proper side of the pivot for my trade(above for longs, below for shorts) I trade the market's search for a new fair price which is typically the fair price established in previous periods(I make sure that the new fair price is far away from the fair price the market is leaving so I get a nice big move). This objective approach ensure that all my trades are the same and look the same on any timeframe. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #40542 ---
Heres a trade I took on Silver yesterday. Same idea, same set up all the time. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Very important to have the middle pivots of all timeframes so you know where you are on all timeframes. I call it pivot world. This range formed right around the yearly pivot which can be a bounce for a big gain. Also notice where the market is turning now at the picture. Look to the left and you see a previous value area(range). The market has found fair price and advantageous price there so the search is paused. Hence I exited half my trade

--- 帖子 #40543 ---
AUDNZD Attached Image (click to enlarge) White arrow is entry. same as always. Notice I enter when price moves abouve the fair price of the previous days. this shows it is searching for a fair price and the next price the market considered fair price is above the weekly pivot(light blue pivot) so I will exit now. Daily pivots are white, monthlys are orange, yearly is black.

--- 帖子 #40547 ---
Oh yeh last one. GBPCHF. This is to show how this can be done on weekly pivots as well. Downtrend. Price consolidated for an entire week last week. This week price moves up above weekly pivot and previous weeks fair price. I enter long. You must make sure the previous weeks fair price is far away so the market can search for it which is what Im trading. Im trading the search for the move. If a range is in the way the market may not search far since it will find fair prce quickly and it may stop you out. This was 2 trades at same level. I do that so I can have different exits. First trade exit was at fair price poc level(white line to the left there.) I usually exit a few pips before that zone but look how perfectly timed the exit was. Traders saw that level as fair and advantageous and they stopped the search but then the search continued and pushed price up to the second target which is my lovely monthly pivot where i exited at perfect timing as price again dropped right from that level. Pivots are a formidable tool my friend. Very dexterous and resourceful Attached Image (click to enlarge)

NO big deal continue hammering trades because I firmly believe in sample size. My account does not die with 1 batch or 10batch of red trades!!!!! --- 帖子 #40758 ---
Spectacular but there is nothing magic about ADR H and L: they are calculated and refreshed during daily session, and represent distance of current price to today's high and low. It's all about probability: if today a pair has done at least the average daily number of pips, then perhaps a big continuation is unlikely and a retrace usually occurs, but it's not sure at 100%.

--- 帖子 #40926 ---
They can be traded, GA actually respects pivots pretty well. I simply adjust the size and use wider stops and targets. When building a "position", my first entry say at R or S 61, I usually set stop at 2 x ADR, however, sometimes that R or S 61 may already be close to or beyond 1x ADR, so you may use tighter stops. Then simply adjust size to the % of account you are willing to risk......if you are position building with 5 trades with total risk on position 2% for example, each trade would be 0.4%. If trade remains valid as price moves against you, positions can be bigger and still be 0.4%., simply due to stops being tighter. Very often, I build my position across 4 or 5 accounts, still only risking same %. One account at the 61, another at the 78 and maybe 1-2 at the 100. If I hold for the wpp, those later trades obviously earn more profit while keeping the same % of risk. Just pulled up 4H on GA.......look at last week's rejection on this weeks R78, look at the support at WPP. I mean we are talking to the pip. You couldn't make it any better if you tried.
